docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
These programs come with TerrainGen.

  • Command line covers the terraingen command, which generates terrain from a configuration, and all its options.
  • GUI covers viewing and editing a terrain in the terraingen --gui app.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text: The terraingen command generates the terrain a JSON configuration describes and writes its heightmaps, albedo, crater and boulder lists, and terrain and boulder meshes. The Python package installs it, as do the releases. The Quickstart runs a first configuration, and the configuration reference lists every setting.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
This is what terraingen --help prints.

Usage:
  terraingen CONFIG [--output-dir DIR] [--log-level LEVEL] [--threads N]
                    [--backend auto|cpu|gpu|vulkan|cuda|metal]
                         Generate the terrain the JSON file CONFIG describes
  terraingen validate CONFIG
                         Check CONFIG without generating
  terraingen schema      Print the configuration schema, for editors
  terraingen backends    Show where terrains can be evaluated here, and the
                         default
  terraingen -V, --version
                         Show version and build information
  terraingen -h, --help  Show this message
  terraingen --gui       Not available yet: the GUI is still in work

Options:
  --output-dir DIR       Write outputs with relative paths under DIR rather than
                         CONFIG's folder
  --log-level LEVEL      Log at LEVEL, one of
                         trace|debug|info|warning|error|off. The default is info
  --threads N            Generate on N threads, or 0 for every hardware thread,
                         the default. The result does not depend on it
  --backend NAME         Evaluate the heights on NAME. The default is cpu, or
                         TERRAINGEN_BACKEND when set. gpu picks the best GPU and
                         auto picks the best GPU or the CPU

terraingen exits with 0 on success, 1 when generating or validating fails and 2
for a usage error.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Generate a terrain, writing its outputs beside the configuration.

terraingen config.json

Check a configuration without generating, then generate it on a GPU into another folder.

terraingen validate config.json
terraingen config.json --backend gpu --output-dir out/

Point an editor at the configuration schema, for completion and checking as you type.

terraingen schema > terraingen.schema.json

docs.title: Workflows
docs.text:
Detailed walkthroughs and tutorials that take several steps, with the choices along the way, such as upscaling a DEM of a landing site or preparing terrain for a rover simulation. The Quickstart walks through a first terrain and the tasks show single steps.

  • Customize TerrainGen replaces each part of a terrain with one of your own, from sources and layers to upsamplers, crater models, density maps, albedo and rock meshes.

docs.title: Customize TerrainGen
docs.text:
Every part of a TerrainGen terrain is an object you can replace with your own. That covers the starting heights, the relief over them and how coarse heights are refined. It covers how many craters there are, how old they are, their shape and how they wear. It also covers where features gather, the albedo and the rocks boulders are made of. Your parts work exactly like the built-in ones. They join the same terrains, are listed and queried the same way, and evaluate over any grid or at single points.

This guide walks through each kind of part, from combining built-in parts to writing your own, in Python and C++. Every example is run as a test, and every image is made by the code above it. Each step is also a task under Customization.

To change Subclass Implement The starting heights Source the grid it covers and the heights of a block of samples The relief over them Layer (FormulaLayer in C++) the height at a point from the height before it How posts are refined Upsampler the heights of a block of samples from the posts around them How many craters or boulders there are SizeFrequencyDistribution the cumulative count N(>= D) How old craters are CraterAgeModel the lifetime by diameter, and optionally how ages are drawn The shape of a crater CraterProfile the height by distance from the center, and its reach How craters wear DegradationModel each crater's fresh and current depth and rim Where craters and boulders gather SurfaceField the value at a point and the largest value The starting albedo AlbedoSource the number of bands and the value at a point Changes to the albedo AlbedoLayer the value at a point from the value before it The shape of a boulder none, a list of meshes the meshes, read with read_mesh

docs.title: Compose built-in parts
docs.text:
Before writing anything, many terrains are a matter of combining what is built in. A noise layer adds a stack of fractals, each with its own seed, wavelength, amplitude, octaves and type. Here broad fBm hills come first and finer ridged noise goes on top.

PythonC++ 
hills = terraingen.Fractal(seed=1, wavelength=200.0, amplitude=6.0, octaves=4)
ridges = terraingen.Fractal(
    seed=2, wavelength=60.0, amplitude=1.5, octaves=5, type=terraingen.FractalType.RIDGED
)
noise = terraingen.NoiseLayer([hills, ridges])  # added in order
terrain = terraingen.Terrain(source=terraingen.FlatSource(257, 257, 1.0), layers=[noise])
heights = terrain.evaluate()

Fractal hills = Fractal::Fbm(1, 200.0, 6.0);  // seed, wavelength and amplitude in meters
hills.octaves = 4;
Fractal ridges = Fractal::Fbm(2, 60.0, 1.5);
ridges.type = FractalType::Ridged;
ridges.octaves = 5;

const auto noise = std::make_shared<NoiseLayer>(std::vector<Fractal>{hills, ridges});
const Terrain terrain(Surface{}, std::make_shared<FlatSource>(257, 257, 1.0), {noise});
const Raster<float> heights = terrain.Evaluate();

Broad fBm hills with finer ridged noise on top, hillshaded.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
A source gives a terrain's starting heights. It defines the grid it covers and the height at any point and sample spacing. It can be an analytic surface, a DEM in a format of your own or the ground of another simulation. Layers are laid over it as over a GeoTIFF. Here a Gaussian dome takes craters.

PythonC++ 
class Dome(terraingen.Source):
    """A Gaussian dome 20 m high and 60 m wide on a 129 x 129 grid of 1 m cells."""

    def grid(self):
        return terraingen.RasterGrid.centered((0.0, 0.0), (129.0, 129.0), 1.0)

    def fill_samples(self, samples, spacing, threads):
        p = samples.positions()
        r2 = p[:, 0] ** 2 + p[:, 1] ** 2
        samples.heights()[:] = 20.0 * np.exp(-r2 / (2.0 * 30.0**2))

craters = terraingen.CraterLayer()
heights = terraingen.Terrain(source=Dome(), layers=[craters]).evaluate()

// A Gaussian dome 20 m high and 60 m wide on a 129 x 129 grid of 1 m cells.
class Dome final : public Source {
  public:
    RasterGrid Grid() const override {
        return RasterGrid::Centered({0.0, 0.0}, {129.0, 129.0}, 1.0);
    }

  protected:
    void FillSamples(SampleBlock& samples, double /*spacing*/,
                     unsigned /*threads*/) const override {
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < samples.Size(); ++i) {
            const Vec2d p = samples.Position(i);
            const double r2 = p.x * p.x + p.y * p.y;
            samples.Height(i) = static_cast<float>(20.0 * std::exp(-r2 / (2.0 * 30.0 * 30.0)));
        }
    }
};

const Terrain terrain(Surface{}, std::make_shared<Dome>(), {std::make_shared<CraterLayer>()});
const Raster<float> heights = terrain.Evaluate();

Craters on the dome, hillshaded.

fill_samples(samples, spacing, threads) is the one method that makes heights. A sample block is either the cells of a grid or a list of points, so the same code serves whole grids and single queries and both give the same height at the same place. samples.positions() gives every position and samples.heights() is the array to fill, NaN where the source has no data. resolution_at(x, y) tells crater and boulder layers which features the source already resolves, so they add only the smaller ones. post_spacing_at(x, y) gives the spacing of the posts behind each height, measured or generated, which roughness estimates sample the source at.

docs.title: Layers
docs.text:
A layer changes the heights beneath it. One whose height at a point depends only on the height there and the point implements apply_at in Python, or derives from FormulaLayer in C++, and is then evaluated over grids and at points like the built-in layers. Layers after it are laid over what it makes, so here craters fall on ridges.

PythonC++ 
class Ridges(terraingen.Layer):
    """Ridges 2 m high and 40 m apart, running north."""

    def apply_at(self, height, x, y, context):
        return height + 2.0 * math.cos(2.0 * math.pi * x / 40.0)

craters = terraingen.CraterLayer()
terrain = terraingen.Terrain(source=terraingen.FlatSource(129, 129, 1.0), layers=[Ridges(), craters])
heights = terrain.evaluate()

// Ridges 2 m high and 40 m apart, running north.
class Ridges final : public FormulaLayer {
  protected:
    float HeightAt(float height, double x, double /*y*/,
                   const LayerContext& /*context*/) const override {
        return height + static_cast<float>(2.0 * std::cos(2.0 * kPi * x / 40.0));
    }
};

const Terrain terrain(Surface{}, std::make_shared<FlatSource>(129, 129, 1.0),
                      {std::make_shared<Ridges>(), std::make_shared<CraterLayer>()});
const Raster<float> heights = terrain.Evaluate();

Craters laid over the ridges, hillshaded.

A quick change needs no class at all. FunctionLayer turns a function of the point, the sample spacing and the height so far into a layer, a Python function or a C++ lambda.

A layer that needs more than one point at a time, such as a filter over its neighbors, implements apply(heights, context) in Python, changing a raster in place, or ApplySamples on Layer in C++.

docs.title: Upsamplers
docs.text:
An upsampler decides a source's heights between its posts and below their spacing, as cubic interpolation or diamond-square refinement do. Registered under a name, configurations use it like the built-in ones, as a source's "upsampling", so a custom part can be chosen from JSON without changing any code that reads the configuration. Here it holds the nearest post's height, rounded down to 2 m terraces.

PythonC++ 
class Terraces(terraingen.Upsampler):
    """The nearest post's height, rounded down to a multiple of 2 m, which makes flat terraces."""

    def fill_samples(self, posts, samples, spacing, threads):
        heights = samples.heights()
        for i, (x, y) in enumerate(samples.positions()):
            col, row = posts.transform().world_to_pixel(x, y)
            height = posts.read(math.floor(col), math.floor(row), 1, 1)[0, 0]
            heights[i] = 2.0 * math.floor(height / 2.0)

    def reach(self):
        return 1

terraingen.register_upsampler("terraces", Terraces)  # Terraces(**settings) makes one
config = terraingen.TerrainGenConfig.from_dict(
    {
        "schema_version": 1,
        "source": {
            "type": "synthetic",
            "pixel_size_m": 4,
            "stack": [{"wavelength_m": 120, "amplitude_m": 8, "octaves": 3}],
            "upsampling": "terraces",
        },
    }
)
terrain = terraingen.build_terrain(config)
grid = terraingen.RasterGrid.centered((0.0, 0.0), (128.0, 128.0), 1.0)
heights = terrain.evaluate(grid)

class Terraces final : public Upsampler {
  public:
    int Reach() const override {
        return 1;
    }

  protected:
    void FillSamples(const PostLattice& posts, SampleBlock& samples, double /*spacing*/,
                     unsigned /*threads*/) const override {
        const GeoTransform transform = posts.Transform();
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < samples.Size(); ++i) {
            const Vec2d p = samples.Position(i);
            const Vec2d pixel = transform.WorldToPixel(p.x, p.y);
            float height = 0.0f;
            posts.Read(static_cast<std::int64_t>(std::floor(pixel.x)),
                       static_cast<std::int64_t>(std::floor(pixel.y)), 1, 1, {&height, 1});
            samples.Height(i) = 2.0f * std::floor(height / 2.0f);
        }
    }
};

RegisterUpsampler("terraces",
                  [](const std::string& /*settings*/) { return std::make_shared<Terraces>(); });
const TerrainGenConfig config = ParseConfig(R"({
    "schema_version": 1,
    "source": {"type": "synthetic", "pixel_size_m": 4, "upsampling": "terraces",
               "stack": [{"wavelength_m": 120, "amplitude_m": 8, "octaves": 3}]}
})");
const RasterGrid grid = RasterGrid::Centered({0.0, 0.0}, {128.0, 128.0}, 1.0);
const Raster<float> heights = BuildTerrain(config).Evaluate(grid);

Heights refined from 4 m posts onto 1 m cells, as 2 m terraces.

reach() is how many posts either side of a point the upsampler reads, so tiles read enough of their neighbors to join seamlessly. Settings given in the configuration are passed to the factory, in Python as keyword arguments and in C++ as JSON text.

docs.title: Size-frequency distributions
docs.text:
A size-frequency distribution gives how many craters or boulders there are of each size, as the cumulative count N(>= D) per square meter. Only the cumulative count is needed, since the incremental count and the inverse used to draw diameters are derived from it. Any crater layer or boulder layer takes it in place of a published distribution.

PythonC++ 
class SteepPowerLaw(terraingen.SizeFrequencyDistribution):
    """N(>= D) = 0.2 D^-2.5 craters per square meter, D in meters, from 1 m to 100 km."""

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(terraingen.SfdKind.DENSITY, 1.0, 1e5)

    def cumulative_at(self, diameter):
        return 0.2 * diameter**-2.5

models = terraingen.CraterModels(
    SteepPowerLaw(),
    terraingen.FreshAges(),
    terraingen.NoDegradation(terraingen.lunar_fresh_crater_morphometry),
    terraingen.FassettThomsonProfile(),
)
options = terraingen.CraterLayerOptions(
    seed=3, generation=terraingen.CraterGenerationOptions(min_diameter=2.0, max_diameter=60.0)
)
table = terraingen.CraterLayer(models, options).craters((-100.0, -100.0, 100.0, 100.0))

// N(>= D) = 0.2 D^-2.5 craters per square meter, D in meters, from 1 m to 100 km.
class SteepPowerLaw final : public SizeFrequencyDistribution {
  public:
    SteepPowerLaw() : SizeFrequencyDistribution(SfdKind::Density, {1.0, 1e5}) {}

  protected:
    double CumulativeAt(double diameter) const override {
        return 0.2 * std::pow(diameter, -2.5);
    }
};

const CraterModels models{std::make_shared<SteepPowerLaw>(), std::make_shared<FreshAges>(),
                          std::make_shared<NoDegradation>(LunarFreshCraterMorphometry),
                          std::make_shared<FassettThomsonProfile>()};
CraterLayerOptions options;
options.seed = 3;
options.generation.minDiameter = 2.0;
options.generation.maxDiameter = 60.0;
const CraterList craters = CraterLayer(models, options).Craters({-100.0, -100.0, 100.0, 100.0});

The craters it gives on 200 m, drawn to scale and colored by diameter.

A crater layer is made of four models. They are this distribution, the ages, the degradation and the profile. The next three sections replace the other three.

docs.title: Crater age models
docs.text:
A crater age model gives how long craters of each size stay visible. It draws each crater's age within that lifetime, uniformly unless you say otherwise. Freshness degradation wears craters over the same lifetimes, so the ages also set how worn each crater is. Here small craters are erased quickly and large ones last, so small craters are always young.

PythonC++ 
class ErasedBySize(terraingen.CraterAgeModel):
    """Craters last 10 Myr per meter of diameter, up to 3.5 Gyr, so small ones are always young."""

    def lifetime_at(self, diameter):
        return min(0.01 * diameter, 3.5)

    def sample_age_at(self, random, diameter, lifetime_gyr):
        return lifetime_gyr * random.next_double()  # optional; uniform when left out

ages = ErasedBySize()
models = terraingen.CraterModels(
    terraingen.PowerLawSfd(0.05, 2.0),
    ages,
    terraingen.FreshnessDegradation(ages, terraingen.lunar_fresh_crater_morphometry),
    terraingen.MartinParkesDunstanProfile(),
)
options = terraingen.CraterLayerOptions(
    seed=4, generation=terraingen.CraterGenerationOptions(min_diameter=4.0, max_diameter=200.0)
)
table = terraingen.CraterLayer(models, options).craters(REGION)  # with each crater's age

// Craters last 10 Myr per meter of diameter, up to 3.5 Gyr, so small ones are always young.
class ErasedBySize final : public CraterAgeModel {
  protected:
    double LifetimeAt(double diameter) const override {
        return std::min(0.01 * diameter, 3.5);
    }

    double SampleAgeAt(RandomStream& random, double /*diameter*/,
                       double lifetimeGyr) const override {
        return lifetimeGyr * random.NextDouble();
    }
};

const auto ages = std::make_shared<ErasedBySize>();
const CraterModels models{
    std::make_shared<PowerLawSfd>(0.05, 2.0), ages,
    std::make_shared<FreshnessDegradation>(ages, LunarFreshCraterMorphometry),
    std::make_shared<MartinParkesDunstanProfile>()};
CraterLayerOptions options;
options.seed = 4;
options.generation.minDiameter = 4.0;
options.generation.maxDiameter = 200.0;
const CraterList craters = CraterLayer(models, options).Craters({-250.0, -250.0, 250.0, 250.0});

Each crater's age by its diameter, under the lifetime that grows with size (left), and the craters drawn to scale and colored by age (right).

docs.title: Crater profiles
docs.text:
A crater profile gives a crater's height by distance from its center, shaped by its current depth and rim height as fractions of its diameter, which the degradation model sets. It also says how many radii from the center it reaches, so the layer knows which craters touch a point. Here a straight-walled cone replaces the default bowl of Martin, Parkes and Dunstan.

PythonC++ 
class ConeProfile(terraingen.CraterProfile):
    """A straight-walled cone to the rim, and a rim that falls off as the cube of distance."""

    def height(self, distance, diameter, state):
        x = distance / (0.5 * diameter)
        depth = state.current.depth_ratio * diameter
        rim = state.current.rim_height_ratio * diameter
        return rim - depth * (1.0 - x) if x <= 1.0 else rim * x**-3

    def reach_radii(self):
        return 2.0  # how far from the center it changes the ground, in radii

models = terraingen.CraterModels(
    terraingen.PowerLawSfd(0.05, 2.0),
    terraingen.FreshAges(),
    terraingen.NoDegradation(terraingen.lunar_fresh_crater_morphometry),
    ConeProfile(),
)
options = terraingen.CraterLayerOptions(
    seed=1, generation=terraingen.CraterGenerationOptions(min_diameter=6.0, max_diameter=60.0)
)
craters = terraingen.CraterLayer(models, options)
heights = terraingen.Terrain(source=terraingen.FlatSource(129, 129, 1.0), layers=[craters]).evaluate()

// A straight-walled cone to the rim, and a rim that falls off as the cube of distance.
class ConeProfile final : public CraterProfile {
  public:
    double Height(double distance, double diameter, const CraterState& state) const override {
        const double x = distance / (0.5 * diameter);
        const double depth = state.current.depthRatio * diameter;
        const double rim = state.current.rimHeightRatio * diameter;
        return x <= 1.0 ? rim - depth * (1.0 - x) : rim / (x * x * x);
    }

    double ReachRadii() const override {
        return 2.0;
    }
};

const CraterModels models{std::make_shared<PowerLawSfd>(0.05, 2.0),
                          std::make_shared<FreshAges>(),
                          std::make_shared<NoDegradation>(LunarFreshCraterMorphometry),
                          std::make_shared<ConeProfile>()};
CraterLayerOptions options;
options.seed = 1;
options.generation.minDiameter = 6.0;
options.generation.maxDiameter = 60.0;
const Terrain terrain(Surface{}, std::make_shared<FlatSource>(129, 129, 1.0),
                      {std::make_shared<CraterLayer>(models, options)});
const Raster<float> heights = terrain.Evaluate();

Cone-shaped craters, hillshaded (left), and a fresh 100 m crater's height over diameter with the cone and with the default profile of Martin, Parkes and Dunstan (right).

On the GPU a profile of your own is tabulated per crater, so craters shaped by it are still drawn by the crater kernel.

docs.title: Degradation models
docs.text:
A degradation model gives each crater's depth and rim height, both fresh and now. It reads only the crater's diameter, age and ID. The profile shapes the crater to this state. Crater lists report it as each crater's depth ratio and freshness, so you can check it without evaluating any heights. Here craters lose half their depth and rim every Gyr.

PythonC++ 
class ShallowWithAge(terraingen.DegradationModel):
    """Craters 0.2 times as deep as wide when fresh, losing half that depth every Gyr."""

    def state(self, crater):
        fresh = terraingen.CraterMorphometry(0.2, 0.04)
        share = 0.5**crater.age_gyr
        now = terraingen.CraterMorphometry(0.2 * share, 0.04 * share)
        return terraingen.CraterState(fresh, now, 0.0)

surface = terraingen.EquilibriumSurface(
    terraingen.extended_neukum_production_function(),
    terraingen.trask_equilibrium(),
    3.5,
    terraingen.neukum_lunar_chronology,
)
models = terraingen.CraterModels(
    surface.density(), surface.ages(), ShallowWithAge(), terraingen.MartinParkesDunstanProfile()
)
craters = terraingen.CraterLayer(models)
table = craters.craters((-100.0, -100.0, 100.0, 100.0))  # with each crater's depth ratio now

// Craters 0.2 times as deep as wide when fresh, losing half that depth every Gyr.
class ShallowWithAge final : public DegradationModel {
  public:
    CraterState State(const Crater& crater) const override {
        const CraterMorphometry fresh{0.2, 0.04};
        const double share = std::pow(0.5, crater.ageGyr);
        return {fresh, {0.2 * share, 0.04 * share}, 0.0};
    }
};

const EquilibriumSurface surface{
    std::make_shared<SplicedSfd>(ExtendedNeukumProductionFunction()),
    std::make_shared<PowerLawSfd>(TraskEquilibrium()), 3.5, NeukumLunarChronology};
const CraterModels models{surface.Density(), surface.Ages(), std::make_shared<ShallowWithAge>(),
                          std::make_shared<MartinParkesDunstanProfile>()};
const CraterLayer craters(models);
const CraterFeatures listed = DescribeCraters(craters.Craters({-100.0, -100.0, 100.0, 100.0}),
                                              models.Shape());  // with each state

A 100 m crater's height over diameter as it ages on Martin, Parkes and Dunstan's profile, worn by the model, which halves its depth and rim every Gyr (left), and by the default diffusion degradation (right).

docs.title: Surface fields
docs.text:
A surface field is a value that varies over the ground, read at any point. Crater and boulder layers take one as a density map. It scales their density point by point, or gives a count or covered share to match. The field also gives its largest value, which bounds how many features are drawn before thinning. Here a field clears craters from a landing pad and lets them back in around it.

PythonC++ 
class LandingPad(terraingen.SurfaceField):
    """No craters within 60 m of the center, rising to the layer's own density at 100 m."""

    def value_at(self, x, y):
        return min(max((math.hypot(x, y) - 60.0) / 40.0, 0.0), 1.0)

    def max(self):
        return 1.0

density_map = terraingen.DensityMap()
density_map.field = LandingPad()
density_map.measure = terraingen.DensityMeasure.SCALE  # times the layer's own density
options = terraingen.CraterLayerOptions(
    seed=5, generation=terraingen.CraterGenerationOptions(min_diameter=4.0, max_diameter=40.0)
)
options.density_map = density_map
table = terraingen.CraterLayer(options=options).craters(REGION)

// No craters within 60 m of the center, rising to the layer's own density at 100 m.
class LandingPad final : public SurfaceField {
  public:
    double ValueAt(double x, double y) const override {
        return std::clamp((std::hypot(x, y) - 60.0) / 40.0, 0.0, 1.0);
    }

    double Max() const override {
        return 1.0;
    }
};

DensityMap densityMap;
densityMap.field = std::make_shared<LandingPad>();
densityMap.measure = DensityMeasure::Scale;  // times the layer's own density
CraterLayerOptions options;
options.seed = 5;
options.generation.minDiameter = 4.0;
options.generation.maxDiameter = 40.0;
options.densityMap = densityMap;
const CraterLayer craters(DefaultCraterModels(), options);
const CraterList list = craters.Craters({-200.0, -200.0, 200.0, 200.0});

The field, a density scale of 0 on the landing pad rising to 1 beyond it (left), and the craters it places, drawn to scale (right).

A map read from a GeoTIFF needs no class. RasterField wraps a raster, as in Vary Crater Density With a Map.

docs.title: Albedo sources
docs.text:
An albedo source gives the starting albedo. It defines its number of bands, 1 or 3, and the value at any point. It can be a map in a format of your own, an analytic pattern or another model's output. Albedo layers are laid over it as over a synthetic albedo. Here dark mare meets bright highlands along a winding contact, and a fresh crater's rays reach across it.

PythonC++ 
class MareContact(terraingen.AlbedoSource):
    """Dark mare at 0.09 in the west and bright highlands at 0.16 in the east, along a winding
    contact about 40 m wide."""

    def bands(self):
        return 1

    def value_at(self, x, y, context):
        share = 0.5 * (1.0 + math.tanh((x - 20.0 * math.sin(y / 60.0)) / 20.0))
        return 0.09 + 0.07 * share

craters = terraingen.CraterLayer.manual([terraingen.Crater(70.0, -60.0, 60.0, age_gyr=0.0)])
rays = terraingen.CraterAlbedo(craters, terraingen.CraterAlbedoOptions(seed=2))
albedo = terraingen.Albedo(MareContact(), [rays])
grid = terraingen.RasterGrid.centered((0.0, 0.0), (400.0, 400.0), PIXEL)  # meters
(values,) = terraingen.evaluate_albedo(albedo, grid)

// Dark mare at 0.09 in the west and bright highlands at 0.16 in the east, along a winding
// contact about 40 m wide.
class MareContact final : public AlbedoSource {
  public:
    std::size_t Bands() const override {
        return 1;
    }

    AlbedoSample ValueAt(double x, double y, const LayerContext& /*context*/) const override {
        const double share = 0.5 * (1.0 + std::tanh((x - 20.0 * std::sin(y / 60.0)) / 20.0));
        return {static_cast<float>(0.09 + 0.07 * share), 0.0f, 0.0f};
    }
};

CraterAlbedoOptions options;
options.seed = 2;
Albedo albedo;
albedo.source = std::make_shared<MareContact>();
albedo.layers = {std::make_shared<CraterAlbedo>(
    CraterLayer::Manual({ManualCrater(70.0, -60.0, 60.0)}), options)};
const RasterGrid grid = RasterGrid::Centered({0.0, 0.0}, {400.0, 400.0}, 2.0);  // meters
const std::vector<Raster<float>> bands = EvaluateAlbedo(albedo, grid, {});

Dark mare meeting bright highlands, from a source of your own, with a fresh crater's rays reaching across the contact.

Crater rays brighten by optical maturity, which leaves reflectance below 0.08 unchanged. Keep a source at or above that where craters should brighten it.

docs.title: Albedo layers
docs.text:
An albedo layer changes the albedo beneath it, one point at a time, from the value there and the point. It is laid over any albedo source with the built-in layers, in order. Here two rover wheel tracks along a winding path darken a synthetic albedo.

PythonC++ 
class RoverTracks(terraingen.AlbedoLayer):
    """Two wheel tracks 0.4 m wide and 1.8 m apart along a winding path, 20 percent darker."""

    def apply_at(self, value, bands, x, y, context):
        middle = 3.0 * math.sin(x / 8.0)
        if any(abs(y - middle - wheel) < 0.2 for wheel in (-0.9, 0.9)):
            return [band * 0.8 for band in value]
        return value

soil = terraingen.Fractal(seed=1, wavelength=10.0, amplitude=0.2, octaves=5)
albedo = terraingen.Albedo(terraingen.SyntheticAlbedo(value=0.11, value_noise=[soil]), [RoverTracks()])
grid = terraingen.RasterGrid.centered((0.0, 0.0), (40.0, 16.0), PIXEL)  # meters
(values,) = terraingen.evaluate_albedo(albedo, grid)

// Two wheel tracks 0.4 m wide and 1.8 m apart along a winding path, 20 percent darker.
class RoverTracks final : public AlbedoLayer {
  public:
    void ApplyAt(AlbedoSample& value, std::size_t bands, double x, double y,
                 const LayerContext& /*context*/) const override {
        const double middle = 3.0 * std::sin(x / 8.0);
        if (std::abs(y - middle + 0.9) < 0.2 || std::abs(y - middle - 0.9) < 0.2) {
            for (std::size_t band = 0; band < bands; ++band) {
                value[band] *= 0.8f;
            }
        }
    }
};

SyntheticAlbedoOptions options;
options.value = 0.11;
Fractal soil = Fractal::Fbm(1, 10.0, 0.2);
soil.octaves = 5;
options.valueNoise = {soil};
Albedo albedo;
albedo.source = std::make_shared<SyntheticAlbedo>(options);
albedo.layers = {std::make_shared<RoverTracks>()};
const RasterGrid grid = RasterGrid::Centered({0.0, 0.0}, {40.0, 16.0}, 0.05);  // meters
const std::vector<Raster<float>> bands = EvaluateAlbedo(albedo, grid, {});

Rover tracks darkening a synthetic albedo on 40 m by 16 m.

docs.title: Rock meshes
docs.text:
Boulder shapes can come from rock meshes, such as scans, in place of the procedural styles. Each boulder picks one by its shape seed, scaled to a long axis of 1 and then to its own size, and is posed, buried and settled like any other. read_mesh reads .obj, .gltf, .glb or .stl files, and a configuration names them as a boulder layer's shape_files. Here an octahedron stands in for a scanned rock.

PythonC++ 
# An octahedron stands in for a scanned rock; terraingen.read_mesh reads .obj, .gltf, .glb or .stl.
corners = np.array([[1, 0, 0], [-1, 0, 0], [0, 0.7, 0], [0, -0.7, 0], [0, 0, 0.5], [0, 0, -0.5]], float)
faces = np.array([[0, 2, 4], [2, 1, 4], [1, 3, 4], [3, 0, 4], [2, 0, 5], [1, 2, 5], [3, 1, 5], [0, 3, 5]])
rock = terraingen.SceneMesh(terraingen.TriangleMesh(corners, faces))

shapes = terraingen.BoulderShapeOptions()
shapes.library = [rock]  # each boulder picks one of these by its shape seed
shape = terraingen.generate_boulder_shape(7, shapes)  # scaled to a long axis of 1
shape.mesh.write(output_folder / "rock.obj")

TriangleMesh octahedron;
octahedron.positions = {{1, 0, 0},    {-1, 0, 0},  {0, 0.7, 0},
                        {0, -0.7, 0}, {0, 0, 0.5}, {0, 0, -0.5}};
octahedron.triangles = {{0, 2, 4}, {2, 1, 4}, {1, 3, 4}, {3, 0, 4},
                        {2, 0, 5}, {1, 2, 5}, {3, 1, 5}, {0, 3, 5}};

BoulderShapeOptions shapes;
shapes.library = {std::make_shared<const SceneMesh>(SceneMesh{octahedron, {}, {}})};
const BoulderShape shape = GenerateBoulderShape(7, shapes);  // scaled to a long axis of 1
WriteMesh(path, shape.mesh);

The rock mesh as a boulder shape.

Procedural shapes can be customized too, without meshes. A boulder style names the solid a shape starts from and the ranges of its axes, fractures, noise and worn edges, as in Design a Boulder Style of Your Own.

docs.title: Rules every part follows
docs.text:
• Deterministic. A part gives the same answer for the same input every time. Anything random is drawn from a seed or from the crater's or boulder's ID, never from a shared generator, so the same seed gives the same terrain on any grid, tile or thread count.
  • A function of position. A point gets the same height as a grid cell centered there, so terrains can be evaluated in tiles that join without seams, or queried at single points.
  • Thread-safe. Parts are called from every evaluation thread at once, so they must not change shared state.
  • Python or C++. Python parts are convenient for trying ideas, but they are called for every sample and Python calls take turns on the GIL, so terrains with them gain little from more threads. A C++ part runs on every thread at full speed, and is the way to go once an idea works.

docs.title: Class List
docs.text:
Here are the classes, structs, unions and interfaces with brief descriptions:

  • namespace std
  • namespace terraingen
    • struct Albedo An albedo as a composition: values from source , then each oflayers in order.
    • struct AlbedoDetail Detail below a map's resolution: fractal noise that continues the map's own measured roughness to finer scales, multiplying the albedo.
    • class AlbedoLayer A change to an albedo: bright ejecta around fresh craters, or a layer of your own.
    • class AlbedoSource Where an albedo starts: a map from orbit, a synthetic color, or a source of your own.
    • class AnchoredPlane The plane a layer lays its features out in: the surface itself on a plane, or on a body the tangent frame of anchor , true to scale near it and empty on the far hemisphere.
    • struct BackendStatus Whether a backend can run here, on which device, or why not.
    • class BandBuckets Indices bucketed per size band into cubes of a side set per band ( Surface::Bucket ), each bucket holding its indices in the order added.
    • struct BandScaling A band's scale and offset: a sample s stands fors * scale + offset , as GDAL's band SCALE and OFFSET metadata say.
    • struct BaseRoughness Self-affine roughness: the RMS height difference at a lag L is nu(L) = deviation (L /cellSize )^H, so the RMS slope over a baseline b is nu(b) / b = s(c) (b / c)^(H - 1) (Shepard et al.
    • class BedformLayer Fields of wind-blown bedforms, ripples or dunes, added to the terrain.
    • struct BedformOptions The bedform fields a BedformLayer scatters: their ripples, cover and wind.
    • struct BindsNativeTrait Whether IO declaresstatic constexpr bool kBindsNative = true .
    • struct BindsNativeTrait< IO, std::enable_if_t< IO::kBindsNative > >
    • struct BlastZone The blast zone around one lander (Clegg et al.
    • class BlastZoneAlbedo Blast zones around landers, changing the albedo by the relative reflectance they give; the same in any grid, tile or point.
    • struct Boulder One boulder: where it stands, how large it is and how it lies, in surface coordinates and meters.
    • struct BoulderAbundance How rich the boulders are at a point.
    • struct BoulderBackground The models of a layer's abundance between craters, each built once from valid options.
    • struct BoulderBedrock Boulders breaking out of bedrock: abundance scales from 1 on soil to abundance on bedrock, in proportion to the exposure.
    • struct BoulderClusters Boulders between craters gathered in clusters: share of them crowd within aboutradius of cluster centers aboutspacing apart and the rest stay scattered.
    • struct BoulderEjecta Blocks thrown out by craters that dug through the regolith, added to the boulders between craters: densest at the rim, thinning outward and with age; overlapping ejecta take the largest share.
    • struct BoulderFacet A plane that sand-laden wind has cut across a boulder's windward side: a ventifact facet.
    • struct BoulderFeatures Boulders, and those of them placed as their own 3D models.
    • struct BoulderFillet Regolith piled against each boulder's base, drawn into the heights around boulders drawn there and around boulder models alike: it meets the boulder's flank where the rock stands heightShare of the exposed height (FilletContact ), then falls as (1 - t)^2 to nothingwidthRatio diameters beyond the boulder's radius.
    • struct BoulderFragment One piece of a split boulder shape.
    • struct BoulderFragmentation Boulders broken by wear into pieces that replace them.
    • class BoulderLayer Boulders scattered over the ground, in patches and richer on bedrock, plus blocks around fresh craters; they depend only on position, so every grid, tile and point agrees.
    • struct BoulderLayerOptions How a BoulderLayer sizes, places, poses and draws its boulders.
    • class BoulderList Boulders stored as one array per field, as CraterList stores craters, so each column can be shared with NumPy or a GPU without copying.
    • class BoulderMapAbundance How a density map sets a boulder layer's abundance between craters: the abundance at which the boulder sizes measure what the map does, once the crater blocks there are taken out of it for a total map.
    • struct BoulderModel A boulder placed as a 3D model of its own.
    • struct BoulderModelThreshold Which boulders become 3D models of their own: those at or above either lower threshold and below every upper one set; no lower threshold means no models.
    • struct BoulderPatches Patches of richer and poorer boulder cover.
    • struct BoulderPlacement How a unit BoulderShape becomes a boulder in the world: scaled per axis byscale , then moved bypose .
    • class BoulderPlacer A layer that places boulders.
    • struct BoulderPose How each boulder stands, drawn per boulder uniformly between these.
    • struct BoulderReliefRange Which boulders are drawn into the heights: those from minDiameter up tomaxDiameter that are not models, and models too withmodels .
    • struct BoulderRendering How boulders are drawn: as relief in the heights or as 3D models, and with which shapes.
    • struct BoulderShape A boulder's shape in unit form, with the origin inside it.
    • struct BoulderShapeOptions Settings for GenerateBoulderShape .
    • struct BoulderSizes The sizes of the boulders between craters: distribution , or Golombek and Rapp (1997) boulders ofcoverage without one, fromminDiameter up tomaxDiameter .
    • struct BoulderStyle One kind of boulder: the solid it starts from and the ranges its shape is drawn from.
    • struct BoulderVentifacts Ventifacts: windward facets planed on boulders by sand-laden wind, set once the boulder has settled.
    • struct Bounds2d An axis-aligned box [ minX ,maxX ) x [minY ,maxY ) in surface coordinates (meters on a plane, the world coordinates a raster'sGeoTransform maps pixels to).
    • struct Box3d An axis-aligned box.
    • struct BucketIndex The integer coordinates of a cube of a 3D grid.
    • struct BuildInfo Build metadata captured when the linked library was last rebuilt (see cmake/BuildInfo.cmake); it describes the linked libraries, not the headers compiled against.

    • class SplotchAlbedo The splotches of SplotchAlbedoOptions on the context's surface, darkening and brightening the albedo; the same in any grid, tile or point.
    • struct SplotchAlbedoOptions Splotches after Speyerer et al.
    • struct SplotchSwarms Swarms of splotches thrown by new craters, the low-velocity secondaries of their ejecta (Robinson et al.
    • class SteadyStateAges Ages of craters on a surface ageGyr old where small craters are in equilibrium.
    • class Stopwatch Measures elapsed wall-clock time from construction, for timing log messages.
    • class StrataLayer Layered rock: the ground beneath terraced into dipping beds, each a bench below a cliff, so hills become buttes and mesas; it lays bedrock over the material map on the cliffs.
    • struct StrataOptions The beds a StrataLayer cuts. Lengths are in meters, angles in degrees.
    • class SummedSfd The sum of weighted distributions of one kind, N(>=D) = sum of weight * N_i(>=D), such as boulders between craters plus the blocks thrown out by them.
    • class Surface The plane or body a terrain lies on, measuring distances and directions between surface coordinates: meters on a plane, planetocentric longitude and latitude in degrees on a body.
    • class SurfaceCells Partitions a surface into cells so features can be generated per cell, each from its own random substream, identically however a region is tiled.
      • struct Sampling How to place features in a cell uniformly by area: draw a Poisson count over area m^2, place each atSamplePoint , and keep it with chanceWeight(point) / bound whenbound is positive.
    • class SurfaceField A scalar quantity over a surface, read at surface coordinates: meters on a plane, longitude and latitude in degrees on a sphere.
    • class SyntheticAlbedo An albedo for terrain without data: a base color with noise in each channel, the saturation and value clamped to [0, 1] after it.
    • struct SyntheticAlbedoOptions The color of a SyntheticAlbedo : a base color in hue, saturation and value, each varied by a stack of fractals (EvaluateFractals , with amplitudes in the channel's units).
    • class SyntheticSource Heights generated rather than loaded: elevation plus a stack of fractals (FractalStackAt , measured from the origin on a plane, in 3D on a body), with no bounds.
    • class TabulatedSfd A cumulative distribution given as a table of (D, N(>=D)) points, interpolated linearly in log D and log N, so each interval is a power law.
    • class Terrain A surface, a source (0 m without one) and layers applied in order.
    • struct TerrainBase The surface and source, the same as their Terrain 's, that crater, secondary crater and boulder layers derive their cells, caches and completeness from when built.
    • class TerrainGenConfig A terrain configuration: the body, source, layers, outputs, albedo and materials its JSON describes ( ParseConfig ,LoadConfig ), held as an immutable value that is cheap to copy.
    • struct TerrainReport A generated terrain's report: its grids' statistics, layer timings and how it was run.
    • class TerrainView The heights of a terrain over one grid, for loops that edit the terrain and evaluate it again.
    • struct TriangleMesh A triangle mesh of shared vertices; triangles are counter-clockwise seen from outside.
    • struct U32x2 Two 32-bit words: a Philox key.
    • struct U32x4 Four 32-bit words: a Philox counter or output block.
    • struct UVec3 Three 32-bit words.
    • class UniformAges Ages uniform over one lifetime for every diameter, so freshness is uniform in [0, 1].
    • struct UniformBand One band of a piecewise uniform distribution: density features with diameters spread uniformly over [min ,max ) meters.
    • struct UnresolvedCover The share of a sample's area covered by boulders too small to resolve in it.
    • class Upsampler How a source's posts become heights at any point and at any sample spacing in the posts' units: interpolation, or refinement that adds detail as the spacing shrinks.
    • struct ValueDistribution A distribution a parameter is drawn from, clamped to [ min ,max ].
    • struct ValueRange An interval to draw a value uniformly from.
    • struct Vec2d A 2D point or offset in double precision.
    • struct Vec3d A 3D point or vector in double precision.
    • struct WarpOffset2 A 2D domain warp offset.
    • struct WarpOffset3 A 3D domain warp offset.
    • struct WeightedSfd One term of a SummedSfd :distribution scaled byweight .
    • struct WorleyDistances Distances from a point to its nearest and second-nearest feature points, and the random value of the nearest point's Voronoi cell.
    • struct ZoneShadows Topographic shadows in the distal reflectance zones (Speyerer et al.
    • namespace detail
      • struct FractalSums The running sums of a fractal over its octaves.
      • struct IsSpanContainer Whether C is a contiguous container whosedata() points to elements convertible toT .
      • struct IsSpanContainer< T, C, std::void_t< decltype(std::data(std::declval< C & >())), decltype(std::size(std::declval< C & >()))> >
      • struct NoiseStack The height of a stack of fractals so far.
      • class RasterHeightsSource A source serving the upsampled heights of a window of a lattice: what RasterSource andGeoTiffSource share.
  • struct Band
  • struct BucketHash
  • struct FieldSum
  • struct BedrockCell A cell of the lattice bedrock means are taken over, on one ground.
  • struct BedrockCellHash
  • struct BreakStage How far a breaking boulder has come apart: its cracks' opening, 0 to 1 from splitWear torubbleWear , and its pieces' scatter, 0 to 1 beyond.
  • struct PieceFrame What every piece of a breaking boulder shares: its parent's shape placed at the origin on level ground, its stage and the shape's short axis.
  • struct Relief A boulder drawn into the heights: its weight at the spacing, whether its rock is drawn or only its fillet, its shape placed on level ground (for BoulderRelief::Shape ) and the box its relief covers.
  • struct ThinnedCandidate A candidate thinning keeps, with what it was kept by.
  • struct UnresolvedNode A diameter UnresolvedCoverAt integrates over, its plan area, and its quadrature weight times the share of it left unresolved.
  • struct BandCount A band's expected craters per square meter at the density of m_candidates .
  • struct Key
  • struct KeyHash
  • struct Table
  • struct Holder
  • struct Key
  • struct KeyHash
  • struct Entry
  • struct Shard
  • struct Level One crack octave: its plate size, crack and plate relief, and seed.
  • struct Plate The plate of one octave containing planar point q : its relief, how far it lies inside the plate rather than in its crack (0 on an edge, 1 past the shoulder), and an id that seeds the finer octave's plates within it.
  • struct Octave
  • struct Shadow One boulder's shadow, ready to draw.
  • class FacePosts One ICQ face's labels as posts, less the reference radius, numbered from face timeskFaceColumns columns.
  • struct Band One octave band of impulses.
  • struct Bed The bed holding stratigraphic level level : its bottom and top levels.
  • class NoisePosts The posts: the noise sampled pixelSize apart.
  • struct ExponentialChronology A chronology N1(T) = burst (e^(decay T) - 1) +linear T per km^2, the form of Neukum's (lunar) and Ivanov's (Martian): craters at least 1 km across on a surface T Gyr old.

docs.title: File List
docs.text:
Here is a list of all files with brief descriptions:

  • dir terraingen
    • file terraingen.h The whole TerrainGen library: includes every public header.
    • dir albedo
      • file albedo.h The albedo source and layer interfaces, albedo compositions and their evaluation.
      • file albedo_fields.h The field lists of the albedo options and Hapke parameters.
      • file blast_zones.h Blast zones: the regolith a lander's descent engine scoured, brighter than around it.
      • file crater_albedo.h Bright, immature ejecta, interiors and rays around fresh craters.
      • file crater_albedo_options.h The options of CraterAlbedo : retention, rays, oblique impacts, texture and the reflectance zones of new craters.
      • file maturity.h The reflectance at another optical maturity (Lucey et al.
      • file photometry.h Hapke photometry of surface materials, and the mix a material map gives.
      • file raster_albedo.h RasterAlbedo , an albedo map upscaled with fractal detail that continues its roughness.
      • file rock_albedo.h Rock albedo: boulders and the rocks too small to resolve, brighter than the regolith.
      • file slope_albedo.h Slope maturity: steep ground kept fresh, and bright, by regolith moving downslope.
      • file splotches.h Splotches: the dark and bright marks secondary impacts of loose regolith leave.
      • file synthetic.h Synthetic albedos: a base color with noise in hue, saturation and value.
    • dir analysis
      • file raster_stats.h Minimum, maximum, mean and standard deviation of a raster's valid cells, and slope statistics of a raster of heights.
      • file spectrum.h Power-law fits to the radially averaged power spectrum of a raster's heights.
      • file variogram.h Lag pairs of a raster's cells and log-log fits over lags, such as the deviogram.
    • dir config
      • file build.h Building a terrain's surface, terrain and albedo from a configuration.
      • file config.h TerrainGenConfig , a terrain configuration held as a value, and the limits configurations take.
      • file generate.h Generating the terrain a configuration describes and writing its outputs.
      • file json.h Configurations as JSON: parsing, loading, writing, catalog and schema.
      • file validate.h Checking a configuration before building it: everything parsing cannot catch.
    • dir distribution
      • file distribution_fields.h The field lists of distribution segments and bands and the names of the published distributions' variants.
      • file equilibrium.h The Trask (1966) and Hartmann (1984) lunar crater equilibrium densities.
      • file golombek_rapp.h Boulder sizes after Golombek and Rapp (1997), from the fraction of ground boulders cover.
      • file ivanov.h Ivanov's (2001) Martian chronology and production function.
      • file log_polynomial.h Size-frequency distributions given by a polynomial in log diameter.
      • file minimum.h The pointwise minimum of size-frequency distributions.
      • file moore.h Moore's lunar terrain crater distributions for Lunar Roving Vehicle trafficability.
      • file neukum.h The Neukum et al.
      • file piecewise_power_law.h Size-frequency distributions made of power-law segments.
      • file piecewise_uniform.h Size-frequency distributions made of bands with diameters spread uniformly.
      • file power_law.h Power-law size-frequency distributions and their segments.
      • file production_surface.h The crater density of a surface of a given age: a production function times a chronology.
      • file size_frequency.h The size-frequency distribution base class, its kinds and diameter ranges.
      • file sp8023.h NASA SP-8023 lunar block size distributions, digitized.
      • file spliced.h Size-frequency distributions spliced from others over consecutive diameter intervals.
      • file summed.h Weighted sums of size-frequency distributions.
      • file synthterrain.h The boulder size distributions synthterrain offers.
      • file tabulated.h Size-frequency distributions given as tables, interpolated in log-log space.
      • file viper.h The VIPER environmental specification's crater distribution.
    • dir geometry
      • file cells.h Surface cells for per-cell feature generation: planar squares and cube-sphere cells.
      • file geometry.h Small vector types, vector math and axis-aligned boxes.
      • file geometry_fields.h The field list of a box.
      • file plane_fit.h Plane andPlaneFit , a least-squares plane through points added one at a time.
      • file radial_shape.h RadialShape , a star-shaped body's radius along each direction from its center.
      • file surface.h Surface , the plane, sphere, triaxial ellipsoid or shape model a terrain lies on, with local frames and distances.
    • dir gpu
      • file backend.h Evaluation backends (the CPU, Vulkan, CUDA or Metal) and the process-wide default.
      • file program.h KernelProgram , a kernel compiled for each GPU backend, andCompiledKernel .
    • dir io
      • file feature_lists.h Reading and writing crater lists and writing boulder lists as CSV or JSON, and boulder models as 3D scenes.
      • file io_fields.h The names of list formats.
      • file report_json.h Terrain reports written as JSON.
    • dir layers
      • file anchored_plane.h AnchoredPlane , the tangent plane at an anchor that planar layers lay features out in.
      • file bedforms.h BedformLayer , fields of wind-blown ripples or dunes.
      • file bedforms_fields.h The field lists of bedforms, sand shadows and sand fill.
      • file density_map.h Density maps: how a map of feature counts or cover sets a layer's local density.
      • file dunes.h DuneLayer , dune fields of barchans, domes or crest-line dunes, with ripples on them.
      • file dunes_fields.h The field lists of dunes, their ripples and grainflows, and the names of dune shapes.
      • file evaluation_cache.h EvaluationCache , values one evaluation's batches of points share.
      • file exposure.h ExposureField , how far the ground is bare bedrock rather than soil, andPatchNoise .
      • file fade.h Falloff curves, and the fade of features too small to resolve at a sample spacing.
      • file field.h Scalar fields over a surface, such as density maps and catalog completeness limits.
      • file ground.h The terrain beneath a layer, readable at any point.
      • file layer.h Layer , relief added on top of a source, andFormulaLayer for point-wise layers.
      • file layer_fields.h Field lists shared by layers: fades, exposure, selections, anchors, raster fields, density maps, roughness and spectral continuation, and the names of their enums.
      • file masked.h MaskedLayer , another layer applied only inside a rectangle, circle or polygon.
      • file material.h Surface material classes, and MaterialSource , the layers that lay one down.
      • file noise_layer.h NoiseLayer , a stack of fractals added to the terrain.
      • file pavement.h PavementLayer , fractured bedrock: polygonal plates parted by cracks or raised ridges.
      • file pavement_fields.h The field lists of pavement and strata.
      • file roughness.h RoughnessLayer , fine self-affine roughness from octaves of Perlin noise.
      • file roughness_estimate.h Self-affine roughness of a base's heights by the variogram method, for layers that continue it below the base's resolution.
      • file sand_fill.h SandFillLayer , sand pooled in the lows of the ground beneath it.
      • file sand_shadow.h SandShadowLayer , sand tails in the lee of a boulder layer's boulders.
      • file source_resolved.h The feature size from which a source's measured data already holds a layer's features.
      • file spectral_continuation.h SpectralContinuationLayer , detail finer than a base DEM that continues the base's measured power-law spectrum (EstimatePowerLawSpectrum ).
      • file strata.h StrataLayer , layered rock: the ground beneath terraced into benches and cliffs.
      • file terrain_base.h TerrainBase , the surface and source crater and boulder layers are built on.
      • dir boulders
        • file boulder.h Boulder , the record of one placed boulder,BoulderList of many, andManualBoulder , one placed by hand.
        • file boulder_abundance.h How abundant a BoulderLayer 's boulders are: density maps, patches, crater blocks and the candidates thinning starts from.
        • file boulder_fields.h The field lists of boulder layers, boulder shapes and manual boulders, and the names of their enums.
        • file boulder_fragments.h Boulder shapes split into pieces that fit back together.
        • file boulder_layer.h BoulderLayer , boulders scattered over the ground and around fresh craters.
        • file boulder_models.h Boulders as 3D models: placing unit shapes on the ground, and their meshes.
        • file boulder_options.h How a BoulderLayer sizes, places, poses and draws its boulders.
        • file boulder_placer.h BoulderPlacer , a layer that lists the boulders it places.
        • file boulder_shape.h Procedural boulder meshes: styles, shape options and seeded shape generation.
        • file ejecta_index.h EjectaIndex , craters bucketed by the discs their ejecta reach.
      • dir craters
        • file band_buckets.h BandBuckets , indices bucketed by size band and surface position for neighbor searches.
        • file crater.h Crater andCraterList , andCraterSelection , which of them a model applies to.
        • file crater_fields.h The field lists of craters, their generation, shaping and secondaries, and the crater enum names.
        • file crater_layer.h CraterLayer , craters generated over the grid being evaluated and applied to it.
        • file crater_placer.h CraterPlacer , a layer that lists the craters it applies.
        • file rays.h The directions of a crater's rays, shared by its secondaries and its bright streaks.
        • file secondaries.h SecondaryCraterLayer , secondary craters around the craters of aCraterLayer .
        • file secondary_model.h The laws secondary craters follow, their options, and their density around a primary.
        • dir ages
          • file age_model.h CraterAgeModel , crater ages by diameter, and the simplest:FreshAges ,UniformAges .
          • file freshness_ages.h FreshnessAges , crater ages from a distribution of freshness.
          • file steady_state.h Crater ages on surfaces where small craters are in equilibrium.
        • dir degradation
          • file degradation_model.h DegradationModel , which maps craters to their degradation state, andNoDegradation .
          • file diffusion.h Crater degradation by topographic diffusion: DiffusedProfile ,DiffusionDegradation .
          • file diffusivities.h Lunar topographic diffusivities of Fassett and Thomson (2014) and Fassett et al.
          • file freshness_degradation.h FreshnessDegradation , craters degraded linearly with the share of their lifetime left.
          • file state.h A crater's shape measures and degradation state.
        • dir generation
          • file population.h Generating crater populations cell by cell, in size bands.
          • file spacing.h Keeping craters of similar size apart: conflicts, precedence and thinning.
        • dir profiles
          • file complex.h ComplexCraterProfile : flat floors, concave walls and central peaks;CraterTerraces steps the walls into slump terraces.
          • file fassett_thomson.h The fresh simple-crater profile of Fassett and Thomson (2014) and its rim variants.
          • file martin_parkes_dunstan.h The simple-crater profile of Martin, Parkes and Dunstan (2014).
          • file profile.h CraterProfile , a crater's height as a function of distance from its center.
        • dir shaping
          • file apply.h Applying a list of craters to heights, over a raster or at scattered points.
          • file apply_options.h How craters are applied to the terrain: their order, datum, blend, outlines and rims.
          • file attributes.h CraterAttributes , what a crater looks like in its current state.
          • file datum.h Crater datums, the surfaces crater interiors are cut to, fitted to the ground.
          • file irregularity.h Irregular, non-circular crater outlines: elongation and rough rims.
          • file morphometry.h Fresh crater morphometry and complex crater shapes fitted to the Moon and Mars.
          • file prepared.h PreparedCrater , a crater with everything needed to shape it at one sample spacing.
          • file slope.h Craters formed on slopes: floors offset downslope and raised rims lowered upslope.
      • dir kernels
        • file cell.h CellPosition , where a kernel evaluates; a kernel header for C++ and Slang.
        • file craters.h The kernel of crater shaping ( ApplyCraters ); a kernel header for C++ and Slang.
        • file noise_layer.h The kernel of NoiseLayer ; a kernel header for C++ and Slang.
      • file transforms.h Height transforms as layers: scale and offset, clamp, and a function of your own.
    • dir mesh
      • file mesh.h Triangle meshes, their measures, normals and rigid transforms.
      • file mesh_build.h BuildMesh , a grid of heights as a triangle mesh, andFillMesh into caller buffers.
      • file polyhedra.h Base solids for boulders and midpoint subdivision.
      • file shape_model.h ShapeModelFromMesh , a body's shape model mesh as aRadialShape .
      • dir io
        • file icq.h Gaskell's implicitly connected quadrilateral (ICQ) shape models: reading, writing and triangulating them.
        • file mesh_io.h Reading and writing triangle meshes and instanced scenes as OBJ with MTL, glTF and STL.
    • dir noise
      • file fractal.h Fractals (fBm, ridged, billow, hybrid) built from octaves of a basis noise.
      • file fractals.h Stacks of fractals with domain warps and blend modes.
      • file hash.h Stateless PCG hashes for the CPU and GPU backends ( portable.h ).
      • file lattice.h Points split into a lattice cell and a fraction, interpolation helpers, and the frozen lattice hash keys.
      • file noise_fields.h The field lists of fractals and the names of the noise enums.
      • file perlin.h Improved Perlin gradient noise in 2D and 3D.
      • file simplex.h Simplex noise in 2D and 3D.
      • file structure_function.h Structure functions of Perlin noise: the mean squared difference of values a lag apart.
      • file surface_noise.h Fractal stacks evaluated at points of a plane or a body's surface.
      • file validate.h Host-side checks of fractal parameters and fractal stacks before kernels use them.
      • file value.h Value noise in 2D and 3D.
      • file worley.h Worley cellular noise in 2D and 3D: feature-point distances and Voronoi cell values.
    • dir pipeline
      • file body_mesh.h BodyMesh andBodyIcq , the whole body a terrain on a sphere or ellipsoid lies on.
      • file materials.h Material maps of a terrain: the share of soil, sand, dust, bedrock and rock at each point.
      • file materials_fields.h The field list of material options.
      • file report.h Terrain reports: statistics of evaluated grids, layer timings and run details.
      • file terrain.h Terrain , a surface, optional starting heights and layers, evaluated over grids or at points, updated in place and reseeded.
      • file terrain_view.h TerrainView , a terrain's heights over one grid, updated as the terrain is edited.
    • dir random
      • file philox.h The Philox4x32-10 counter-based generator for the CPU and GPU backends.
      • file random_fields.h The field list of value distributions and the names of their kinds.
      • file samplers.h Samplers for Poisson and normal distributions.
      • file stream.h RandomStream , a counter-based random number stream, derived seeds and 64-bit IDs.
      • file streams.h Every random stream tag: the word that keys RandomStream andSubstreamSeed apart for one purpose.
      • file value_distribution.h ValueDistribution , a clamped distribution a parameter is drawn from.
    • dir raster
      • file cell_loops.h Parallel loops over a raster's cells: every cell, or the windows around features.
      • file geo_transform.h The affine pixel-to-world transform of a georeferenced raster.
      • file grid.h Raster grids without values, and resampled grids and spacings derived from them.
      • file raster.h A single-band georeferenced grid of values.
      • file raster_fields.h The names of the interpolation methods and TIFF compressions.
      • file resample.h Interpolation of rasters: nearest, bilinear, cubic, Lanczos and B-spline.
      • dir geotiff
        • file geotiff.h Reading and writing GeoTIFF rasters, with their projection keys and band scaling.
    • dir sources
      • file diamond_square.h DiamondSquareUpsampler , random midpoint displacement (diamond-square) refinement of a source's posts, as Martin, Parkes and Dunstan (2014) expand DEMs.
      • file flat_source.h A source of constant elevation, the start of a fully synthetic terrain.
      • file geotiff_source.h Heights read from a band of a GeoTIFF DEM.
      • file raster_source.h Heights from a raster held in memory.
      • file sample_block.h Positions a source or layer evaluates and their heights: a raster's cells or scattered points.
      • file shape_model_source.h ShapeModelSource , a shape-model body's own labels refined by an upsampler.
      • file source.h The source interface: where a terrain's heights come from.
      • file source_chain.h Sources tried in order, each filling the gaps of those before it.
      • file sources_fields.h The field lists of diamond-square options, chain seams and GeoTIFF band reads, and the names of their enums.
      • file synthetic_source.h SyntheticSource , heights generated from a stack of fractals over an unbounded plane or a whole body.
      • file upsampling.h Upsamplers: how a source's posts become heights at any point and sample spacing.
    • dir util
      • file bits.h Pi, bit casts, byte order and integer arithmetic, in C++17.
      • file build_info.h Build metadata of the linked library.
      • file log.h Leveled logging to a replaceable sink, and timing helpers for log messages.
      • file lru_cache.h LruCache , a sharded thread-safe least-recently-used cache.
      • file option_fields.h Field lists of option structs: ranges, enum names and the range check they share.
      • file parallel.h A parallel for loop over a shared thread pool.
      • file portable.h Prelude that compiles kernel headers, written in the subset of C++ that Slang accepts, both as C++ (CPU) and as Slang (GPU); KERNEL_IN(T) passes a struct by reference in C++ only.
      • file span.h Span , a non-owning view of contiguous elements that keeps the library at C++17.
      • file special_functions.h Special functions the models need: the exponential integral.

map's own measured roughness to finer scales, multiplying the albedo. class AlbedoLayer A change to an albedo: bright ejecta around fresh craters, or a layer of your own. class AlbedoSource Where an albedo starts: a map from orbit, a synthetic color, or a source of your own. class AnchoredPlane The plane a layer lays its features out in: the surface itself on a plane, or on a body the tangent frame of anchor , true to scale near it and empty on the far hemisphere. struct BackendStatus Whether a backend can run here, on which device, or why not. class BandBuckets Indices bucketed per size band into cubes of a side set per band ( Surface::Bucket ), each bucket holding its indices in the order added. struct BandScaling A band's scale and offset: a sample s stands fors * scale + offset , as GDAL's band SCALE and OFFSET metadata say. struct BaseRoughness Self-affine roughness: the RMS height difference at a lag L is nu(L) = deviation (L /cellSize )^H, so the RMS slope over a baseline b is nu(b) / b = s(c) (b / c)^(H - 1) (Shepard et al. class BedformLayer Fields of wind-blown bedforms, ripples or dunes, added to the terrain. struct BedformOptions The bedform fields a BedformLayer IO::kBindsNative > > <typename IO> struct BlastZone The blast zone around one lander (Clegg et al. class BlastZoneAlbedo Blast zones around landers, changing the albedo by the relative reflectance they give; the same in any grid, tile or point. struct Boulder One boulder: where it stands, how large it is and how it lies, in surface coordinates and meters. struct BoulderAbundance How rich the boulders are at a point. struct BoulderBackground The models of a layer's abundance between craters, each built once from valid options. struct BoulderBedrock Boulders breaking out of bedrock: abundance scales from 1 on soil to abundance on bedrock, in proportion to the exposure. struct BoulderClusters Boulders between craters gathered in clusters: share of them crowd within aboutradius of cluster centers aboutspacing apart and the rest stay scattered. struct BoulderEjecta Blocks thrown out by craters that dug through the regolith, added to the boulders between craters: densest at the rim, thinning outward and with age; overlapping ejecta take the largest share. struct BoulderFacet A plane that sand-laden wind has cut across a boulder's windward side: a ventifact facet. struct BoulderFeatures Boulders, and those of them placed as their own 3D models. struct BoulderFillet Regolith piled against each boulder's base, drawn into the heights around boulders drawn there and around boulder models alike: it meets the boulder's flank where the rock stands heightShare of the exposed height (FilletContact ), then falls as (1 - t)^2 to nothingwidthRatio diameters beyond the boulder's radius. struct BoulderFragment One piece of a split boulder shape. struct BoulderFragmentation Boulders broken by wear into pieces that replace them. class BoulderLayer Boulders scattered over the ground, in patches and richer on bedrock, plus blocks around fresh craters; they depend only on position, so every grid, tile and point agrees. struct BoulderLayerOptions How a BoulderLayer sizes, places, poses and draws its boulders. class BoulderList Boulders stored as one array per field, as CraterList stores craters, so each column can be shared with NumPy or a GPU without copying. docs.text:
Writes the mesh BuildMesh makes ofheights into caller buffers, bit for bit:positions as x, y, z triples andtriangles as vertex index triples, inBuildMesh 's order.

    Span < std::int32_t > triangles,
    const Surface & surface={},
    const Vec2d & site={},
    const BuildMeshOptions & options={}
)

The layout matches an array of Chrono's ChVector3d and ChVector3i, or NumPy arrays of shape (N, 3) float64 and (M, 3) int32, so callers resize those to GetMeshSize and pass their data with no copy.

Parameters:

  • positions 3 * GetMeshSize(heights, options).vertices doubles, in meters.
  • triangles 3 * GetMeshSize(heights, options).triangles indices into the vertices.
  • site Surface coordinates of the site; unused on a plane.

  • std::invalid_argument as GetMeshSize, for a buffer of another size, or for a mesh of more than INT32_MAX vertices.

docs.title: function MarsDesiccationRidges
docs.text:
The desiccation ridges of the Old Soaker slab in Gale crater (Stein et al. 

PavementOptions terraingen::MarsDesiccationRidges ()

2018): 2 cm polygons parted by 5 mm high ridges about 2 mm wide (from ridges covering about 20 % of the slab), flat and untilted. The polygons there are mostly four-sided with T-junctions; Voronoi plates meet at Y-junctions.

docs.title: function MarsDuneGrainflows
docs.text:
The grainflows of Namib Dune's lee slope (Ewing et al. 

DuneGrainflows terraingen::MarsDuneGrainflows ()

2017, Table 1): scarps 0.54 to 0.67 m wide and 1.0 to 1.6 m long, lobes 0.57 to 0.66 m wide and 2.9 to 6 m long. Their thickness is not measured on Mars; 0.015 m is that of a Namibian barchan's grainflows (Nield et al. 2017, in Ewing et al. 2017). Every cell holds one, as palimpsest grainflows are abundant on that slope.

How a SourceChain joins each source to the gaps of those before it.More...

docs.title: Public Attributes
docs.text: Type Name double decayLength = 50.0Decay length L of Height andSlope , in the sources' units; positive and finite. ChainSeamMode mode = ChainSeamMode::None double width = 50.0Width of Feather 's band, in the sources' units (meters on a plane, degrees on a body); positive and finite.

docs.title: Public Functions
docs.text: Type Name bool operator!= (const ChainSeams & other) const bool operator== (const ChainSeams & other) constMemberwise equality.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text: Along the edge of each gap the earlier source's height minus the later one's is measured at the earlier source's posts. Feather adds that difference, carried from the nearest edge post, to the later source and fades it to 0 over width. Height spreads it into the gap as the solution of (Laplacian - 1/L^2) d = 0 with L the decayLength, so the later source keeps its relief and only its level shifts; Slope solves (Laplacian - 1/L^2)^2 d = 0, matching slopes as well. In a hole the shift spans the hole; beyond a source's edge it fades out over L and is 0 from kSeamReachDecays L on.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text: The file is decoded a tile or strip at a time as heights are asked of them and kept in a cache of cacheBytes, so a small area of a file too large to hold in memory reads only the blocks around it; a crop gives the same bits over its grid as the whole file. A file in longitude and latitude whose columns span 360 degrees wraps in longitude as a RasterSource does.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text: The heights are used as given, with the raster's no-data value. On the source's own lattice at its cell size or coarser Fill copies cells exactly; elsewhere, and at finer spacings, the upsampler gives each cell from the raster's cells, its posts. Cells beyond the raster are no-data. With geographic keys and columns spanning 360 degrees the raster wraps in longitude, so a file from 0 to 360 also serves -180 to 0.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text: Each of the six ICQ faces is a lattice of (Q + 1)^2 posts, the label radii, in degrees: Q intervals span the face's 90 degrees. Posts beyond a face's edge are read from the shape where the face's lattice extends onto its neighbors, so kernel upsamplers agree along the edges. Each face's posts are numbered apart from the others', so diamond-square displaces each face differently, and within half a post of an edge the faces' heights are blended. A height is the refined radius less the body's, 0 at every label: the shape gives the labels and the source what an upsampler makes between them.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
The sources must share coordinates; the chain takes its grid and reference point from the first.

With seams (ChainSeams) each source is matched to the chain of those before it where it fills their gaps. The match is solved once, on first use, on the posts of the source before it (SeamLattice, at the cell size of its grid), and read between the posts by Catmull-Rom interpolation, so points, tiles and grids still agree. A source without bounds gives no lattice and the source after it is not matched. On a body the lattice's degrees of longitude count as degrees of latitude. No-data inside the later source stays no-data.

#pragma once

#include "terraingen/geometry/geometry.h"

#include <array>
#include <cstddef>
#include <functional>
#include <memory>
#include <vector>

namespace terraingen {

inline constexpr std::size_t kMaxAlbedoBands = 3;

using AlbedoSample = std::array<float, kMaxAlbedoBands>;

void ValidateAlbedoContext(const LayerContext& context);

class AlbedoSource {
  public:
    virtual ~AlbedoSource() = default;

    virtual std::size_t Bands() const = 0;

    virtual AlbedoSample ValueAt(double x, double y, const LayerContext& context) const = 0;

    virtual void Fill(std::vector<Raster<float>>& bands, const LayerContext& context) const;
};

class AlbedoLayer {
  public:
    virtual ~AlbedoLayer() = default;

    virtual void ApplyAt(AlbedoSample& value, std::size_t bands, double x, double y,
                         const LayerContext& context) const = 0;

    virtual void Apply(std::vector<Raster<float>>& bands, const LayerContext& context) const;
};

struct Albedo {
    std::shared_ptr<const AlbedoSource> source;              
    std::vector<std::shared_ptr<const AlbedoLayer>> layers;  
    Surface surface{};
};

std::vector<Raster<float>> EvaluateAlbedo(const Albedo& albedo, const RasterGrid& grid,
                                          LayerContext context);

AlbedoSample EvaluateAlbedoAt(const Albedo& albedo, double x, double y, LayerContext context);

using AlbedoCellVisitor = std::function<void(AlbedoSample& value, double x, double y)>;

void ForEachAlbedoCell(std::vector<Raster<float>>& bands, unsigned threads,
                       const AlbedoCellVisitor& visit);

using AlbedoPixelVisitor =
    std::function<void(AlbedoSample& value, std::size_t col, std::size_t row)>;

void ForEachAlbedoPixel(std::vector<Raster<float>>& bands, unsigned threads,
                        const AlbedoPixelVisitor& visit);

void ForEachAlbedoBlock(
    std::vector<Raster<float>>& bands, unsigned threads, std::size_t blockRows,
    const std::function<AlbedoCellVisitor(std::size_t rowBegin, std::size_t rowEnd)>& makeVisitor);

}  // namespace terraingen

// SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause

#pragma once

#include "terraingen/raster/raster.h"

#include <cmath>
#include <cstddef>

namespace terraingen {

template <typename Visit>
void ForEachLagPair(const Raster<float>& heights, std::size_t lag, const Visit& visit) {
    const auto pair = [&](std::size_t col, std::size_t row, std::size_t col2, std::size_t row2) {
        if (!heights.IsMissing(heights(col, row)) && !heights.IsMissing(heights(col2, row2))) {
            visit(static_cast<double>(heights(col, row)), static_cast<double>(heights(col2, row2)));
        }
    };
    for (std::size_t row = 0; row < heights.Height(); ++row) {
        for (std::size_t col = 0; col < heights.Width(); ++col) {
            if (col + lag < heights.Width()) {
                pair(col, row, col + lag, row);
            }
            if (row + lag < heights.Height()) {
                pair(col, row, col, row + lag);
            }
        }
    }
}

struct DeviogramFit {
    int lags = 0;            
    double slope = 0.0;      
    double intercept = 0.0;  
    double cellRms = 0.0;    
};

template <typename Statistic>
DeviogramFit FitLagLine(std::size_t maxLag, const Statistic& statistic) {
    double sumX = 0.0;
    double sumY = 0.0;
    double sumXX = 0.0;
    double sumXY = 0.0;
    DeviogramFit fit;
    for (std::size_t lag = 1; lag <= maxLag; lag *= 2) {
        const double value = statistic(lag);
        if (!(value > 0.0)) {
            break;
        }
        fit.cellRms = lag == 1 ? value : fit.cellRms;
        const double x = std::log2(static_cast<double>(lag));
        const double y = std::log2(value);
        sumX += x;
        sumY += y;
        sumXX += x * x;
        sumXY += x * y;
        ++fit.lags;
    }
    if (fit.lags >= 2) {
        fit.slope = (fit.lags * sumXY - sumX * sumY) / (fit.lags * sumXX - sumX * sumX);
        fit.intercept = (sumY - fit.slope * sumX) / fit.lags;
    }
    return fit;
}

DeviogramFit FitDeviogram(const Raster<float>& heights);

}  // namespace terraingen

// SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause

#pragma once

#include "terraingen/distribution/size_frequency.h"

#include <cmath>

namespace terraingen {

struct PowerLawSegment {
    double start = 0.0;        
    double coefficient = 1.0;  
    double exponent = 2.0;     

    double Cumulative(double diameter) const {
        return coefficient * std::pow(diameter, -exponent);
    }

    double Incremental(double diameter) const {
        return coefficient * exponent * std::pow(diameter, -exponent - 1.0);
    }

    double Invert(double target) const {
        return std::pow(target / coefficient, -1.0 / exponent);
    }

    bool operator==(const PowerLawSegment& other) const {
        return start == other.start && coefficient == other.coefficient &&
               exponent == other.exponent;
    }
    bool operator!=(const PowerLawSegment& other) const {
        return !(*this == other);
    }
};

class PowerLawSfd final : public SizeFrequencyDistribution {
  public:
    PowerLawSfd(double coefficient, double exponent, SfdKind kind = SfdKind::Density,
                DiameterRange range = {});

    double Coefficient() const {
        return m_law.coefficient;

    double IncrementalAt(double diameter) const override;
    double InvertCumulative(double target, double minDiameter, double maxDiameter) const override;

  private:

};
