#pragma once

#include <limits>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

namespace terraingen {

class RandomStream;

struct ValueDistribution {
    enum class Kind {
        Constant,   
        Uniform,    
        Normal,     
        LogNormal,  
        Piecewise,  
    };
    Kind kind = Kind::Constant;                             
    double a = 0.0;                                         
    double b = 0.0;                                         
    double min = -std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();  
    double max = std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();   
    std::vector<double> edges{};    
    std::vector<double> weights{};  

    static ValueDistribution Constant(double value) {
        return {Kind::Constant, value};
    }
    static ValueDistribution Uniform(double low, double high) {
        return {Kind::Uniform, low, high};
    }
    static ValueDistribution Normal(double mean, double sd) {
        return {Kind::Normal, mean, sd};
    }
    static ValueDistribution LogNormal(double median, double logSd) {
        return {Kind::LogNormal, median, logSd};
    }
    static ValueDistribution Piecewise(std::vector<double> edges, std::vector<double> weights) {
        ValueDistribution distribution{Kind::Piecewise};
        distribution.edges = std::move(edges);
        distribution.weights = std::move(weights);
        return distribution;
    }

    ValueDistribution Clamped(double low, double high) const {
        ValueDistribution clamped = *this;
        clamped.min = low;
        clamped.max = high;
        return clamped;
    }

    double Sample(double u1, double u2) const;

    double Draw(RandomStream& random) const;

    double Lowest() const;

    double Highest() const;

    bool operator==(const ValueDistribution& other) const {
        return kind == other.kind && a == other.a && b == other.b && min == other.min &&
               max == other.max && edges == other.edges && weights == other.weights;
    }
    bool operator!=(const ValueDistribution& other) const {
        return !(*this == other);
    }
};

void ValidateValueDistribution(const ValueDistribution& distribution);

}  // namespace terraingen

struct PixelWindow {
    std::size_t colBegin = 0;  
    std::size_t colEnd = 0;    
    std::size_t rowBegin = 0;  
    std::size_t rowEnd = 0;    

    bool Empty() const {
        return colBegin >= colEnd || rowBegin >= rowEnd;
    }

    std::size_t Width() const {
        return colEnd > colBegin ? colEnd - colBegin : 0;
    }

    std::size_t Height() const {
        return rowEnd > rowBegin ? rowEnd - rowBegin : 0;
    }

    bool operator==(const PixelWindow& other) const {
        return colBegin == other.colBegin && colEnd == other.colEnd && rowBegin == other.rowBegin &&
               rowEnd == other.rowEnd;
    }
    bool operator!=(const PixelWindow& other) const {
        return !(*this == other);
    }
};

PixelWindow PixelWindowIn(const RasterGrid& grid, const Bounds2d& box);

inline PixelWindow WholeWindow(const RasterGrid& grid) {
    return {0, grid.width, 0, grid.height};
}

RasterGrid Subgrid(const RasterGrid& grid, const PixelWindow& cells);

inline PixelWindow TileWindow(std::size_t tx, std::size_t ty, std::size_t tileWidth,
                              std::size_t tileHeight, const PixelWindow& window) {
    return {
        std::max(window.colBegin, tx * tileWidth), std::min(window.colEnd, (tx + 1) * tileWidth),
        std::max(window.rowBegin, ty * tileHeight), std::min(window.rowEnd, (ty + 1) * tileHeight)};
}

template <typename Visit>
void ForEachTileIn(const PixelWindow& window, std::size_t tileWidth, std::size_t tileHeight,
                   const Visit& visit) {
    for (std::size_t ty = window.rowBegin / tileHeight; ty <= (window.rowEnd - 1) / tileHeight;
         ++ty) {
        for (std::size_t tx = window.colBegin / tileWidth; tx <= (window.colEnd - 1) / tileWidth;
             ++tx) {
            visit(tx, ty, TileWindow(tx, ty, tileWidth, tileHeight, window));
        }
    }
}

template <typename Visit>
void ForEachTile(std::size_t width, std::size_t height, std::size_t side, unsigned threads,
                 const Visit& visit) {
    const std::size_t tilesX = CeilDiv(width, side);
    ParallelFor(tilesX * CeilDiv(height, side), threads, [&](std::size_t tile) {
        visit(TileWindow(tile % tilesX, tile / tilesX, side, side, {0, width, 0, height}));
    });
}

std::vector<PixelWindow> PixelWindowsIn(const RasterGrid& grid, const Bounds2d& box,
                                        const Surface& surface);

struct FeatureCell {
    std::size_t feature = 0;  
    std::size_t col = 0;      
    std::size_t row = 0;      
    Vec2d center{};           
};

inline constexpr std::size_t kFeatureTileCells = 32;

template <typename T, typename Visit>
void ForEachFeatureCell(Raster<T>& raster, unsigned threads, const std::vector<Bounds2d>& boxes,
                        const Surface& surface, const Visit& visit) {
    constexpr std::size_t kSide = kFeatureTileCells;
    const RasterGrid& grid = raster.Grid();
    const std::size_t tilesX = CeilDiv(raster.Width(), kSide);
    std::vector<std::vector<std::pair<std::size_t, PixelWindow>>> tiles(
        tilesX * CeilDiv(raster.Height(), kSide));
    for (std::size_t n = 0; n < boxes.size(); ++n) {
        for (const PixelWindow& window : PixelWindowsIn(grid, boxes[n], surface)) {
            ForEachTileIn(window, kSide, kSide,
                          [&](std::size_t tx, std::size_t ty, const PixelWindow& cells) {
                              tiles[ty * tilesX + tx].emplace_back(n, cells);
                          });
        }
    }
    ParallelFor(tiles.size(), threads, [&](std::size_t tile) {
        for (const auto& [feature, cells] : tiles[tile]) {
            for (std::size_t row = cells.rowBegin; row < cells.rowEnd; ++row) {
                for (std::size_t col = cells.colBegin; col < cells.colEnd; ++col) {
                    T& cell = raster(col, row);
                    if (!raster.IsNoData(cell)) {
                        visit(cell, FeatureCell{feature, col, row, raster.CellCenter(col, row)});
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    });
}

template <typename T, typename Map>
void MapCells(Raster<T>& raster, unsigned threads, const Map& map) {
    ParallelFor(raster.Height(), threads, [&](std::size_t row) {
        for (std::size_t col = 0; col < raster.Width(); ++col) {
            T& cell = raster(col, row);
            if (!raster.IsNoData(cell)) {
                cell = static_cast<T>(map(cell, raster.CellCenter(col, row)));
            }
        }
    });
}

}  // namespace terraingen

// SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause

#pragma once

#include "terraingen/geometry/geometry.h"

#include <array>
#include <cmath>
#include <stdexcept>

namespace terraingen {

struct GeoTransform {
    double originX = 0.0;      
    double pixelWidth = 1.0;   
    double rowRotation = 0.0;  
    double originY = 0.0;      
    double colRotation = 0.0;  
    double pixelHeight = 1.0;  

    static GeoTransform NorthUp(double originX, double originY, double pixelSize) {
        return GeoTransform{originX, pixelSize, 0.0, originY, 0.0, -pixelSize};
    }

    static GeoTransform FromGdal(const std::array<double, 6>& c) {
        return GeoTransform{c[0], c[1], c[2], c[3], c[4], c[5]};
    }

    std::array<double, 6> ToGdal() const {
        return {originX, pixelWidth, rowRotation, originY, colRotation, pixelHeight};
    }

    bool IsRotated() const {
        return rowRotation != 0.0 || colRotation != 0.0;
    }

    double CellWidth() const {
        return std::hypot(pixelWidth, colRotation);
    }

    double CellHeight() const {
        return std::hypot(rowRotation, pixelHeight);
    }

    Vec2d PixelToWorld(double col, double row) const {
        return {originX + col * pixelWidth + row * rowRotation,
                originY + col * colRotation + row * pixelHeight};
    }

    Vec2d WorldToPixel(double x, double y) const {
        const double det = pixelWidth * pixelHeight - rowRotation * colRotation;
        if (det == 0.0) {
            throw std::domain_error("GeoTransform is not invertible");
        }
        const double dx = x - originX;
        const double dy = y - originY;
        return {(dx * pixelHeight - dy * rowRotation) / det,
                (dy * pixelWidth - dx * colRotation) / det};
    }

    bool operator==(const GeoTransform& other) const {
        return originX == other.originX && pixelWidth == other.pixelWidth &&
               rowRotation == other.rowRotation && originY == other.originY &&
               colRotation == other.colRotation && pixelHeight == other.pixelHeight;
    }
    bool operator!=(const GeoTransform& other) const {
        return !(*this == other);
    }
};

}  // namespace terraingen

#pragma once

#include "terraingen/raster/geo_transform.h"
#include "terraingen/raster/grid.h"
#include "terraingen/util/span.h"

#include <cassert>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstddef>
#include <optional>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <type_traits>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

namespace terraingen {

template <typename T> class Raster {
  public:
    Raster() = default;

    Raster(std::size_t width, std::size_t height, T fill = T{})
        : Raster(RasterGrid{width, height, GeoTransform{}}, fill) {}

    explicit Raster(const RasterGrid& grid, T fill = T{})
        : m_grid(grid), m_owned(grid.width * grid.height, fill), m_cells(m_owned.data()) {}

    Raster(const RasterGrid& grid, Span<T> cells) : m_grid(grid), m_cells(cells.data()) {
        if (cells.size() != grid.width * grid.height) {
            throw std::invalid_argument("A raster borrowing cells needs one value per cell");
        }
    }

    Raster(const Raster& other)
        : m_grid(other.m_grid), m_owned(other.m_cells, other.m_cells + other.Size()),
          m_cells(m_owned.data()), m_noData(other.m_noData) {}

    Raster(Raster&& other) noexcept
        : m_grid(other.m_grid), m_owned(std::move(other.m_owned)), m_cells(other.m_cells),
          m_noData(other.m_noData) {
        other.m_grid.width = 0;
        other.m_grid.height = 0;
        other.m_cells = nullptr;
    }

    Raster& operator=(Raster other) noexcept {
        std::swap(m_grid, other.m_grid);
        std::swap(m_owned, other.m_owned);
        std::swap(m_cells, other.m_cells);
        std::swap(m_noData, other.m_noData);
        return *this;
    }

    ~Raster() = default;

    const RasterGrid& Grid() const {
        return m_grid;
    }

    std::size_t Width() const {
        return m_grid.width;
    }

    std::size_t Height() const {
        return m_grid.height;
    }

    std::size_t Size() const {
        return m_grid.width * m_grid.height;
    }

    bool Empty() const {
        return Size() == 0;
    }

    T& operator()(std::size_t col, std::size_t row) {
        assert(col < m_grid.width && row < m_grid.height);
        return m_cells[row * m_grid.width + col];
    }

    const T& operator()(std::size_t col, std::size_t row) const {
        assert(col < m_grid.width && row < m_grid.height);
        return m_cells[row * m_grid.width + col];
    }

    T& At(std::size_t col, std::size_t row) {
        CheckBounds(col, row);
        return m_cells[row * m_grid.width + col];
    }

    const T& At(std::size_t col, std::size_t row) const {
        CheckBounds(col, row);
        return m_cells[row * m_grid.width + col];
    }

    Span<T> Values() {
        return {m_cells, Size()};
    }

    Span<const T> Values() const {
        return {m_cells, Size()};
    }

    Span<T> Row(std::size_t row) {
        assert(row < m_grid.height);
        return {m_cells + row * m_grid.width, m_grid.width};
    }

    Span<const T> Row(std::size_t row) const {
        assert(row < m_grid.height);
        return {m_cells + row * m_grid.width, m_grid.width};
    }

    const GeoTransform& Transform() const {
        return m_grid.transform;
    }

    bool IsNoData(const T& value) const {
        if (!m_noData) {
            return false;
        }
        if constexpr (std::is_floating_point_v<T>) {
            if (std::isnan(*m_noData)) {
                return std::isnan(value);
            }
        }
        return value == *m_noData;
    }

    bool IsMissing(const T& value) const {
        if constexpr (std::is_floating_point_v<T>) {
            if (!std::isfinite(value)) {
                return true;
            }
        }
        return IsNoData(value);
    }

    const std::optional<T>& NoData() const {
        return m_noData;
    }

    void SetNoData(std::optional<T> value) {
        m_noData = value;
    }

    Vec2d CellCenter(std::size_t col, std::size_t row) const {
        return m_grid.transform.PixelToWorld(static_cast<double>(col) + 0.5,
                                             static_cast<double>(row) + 0.5);
    }

  private:
    void CheckBounds(std::size_t col, std::size_t row) const {
        if (col >= m_grid.width || row >= m_grid.height) {
            throw std::out_of_range("Raster cell out of range");
        }
    }

    RasterGrid m_grid;
    std::vector<T> m_owned;
    T* m_cells = nullptr;
    std::optional<T> m_noData;
};

}  // namespace terraingen

#include <vector>

namespace terraingen {

class SampleBlock {
  public:
    explicit SampleBlock(Raster<float>& heights);

    SampleBlock(Span<const Vec2d> positions, Span<float> heights);

    std::size_t Size() const {
        return m_heights.size();
    }

    bool IsGrid() const {
        return m_grid != nullptr;
    }

    Raster<float>* Grid() const {
        return m_grid;
    }

    Span<const Vec2d> Points() const {
        return m_positions;
    }

    Span<float> Heights() const {
        return m_heights;
    }

    Vec2d Position(std::size_t i) const;

    std::vector<Vec2d> Positions() const;

    float& Height(std::size_t i) const {
        return m_heights[i];
    }

    bool IsNoData(std::size_t i) const;

    Bounds2d Bounds() const;

    double ResolvedSpacing(double spacing, const Surface& surface) const;

  private:
    Raster<float>* m_grid = nullptr;
    Span<const Vec2d> m_positions;
    Span<float> m_heights;
};

template <typename Map> void MapPoints(SampleBlock& samples, const Map& map) {
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < samples.Size(); ++i) {
        if (!samples.IsNoData(i)) {
            samples.Height(i) = map(samples.Height(i), samples.Position(i));
        }
    }
}

template <typename Map> void MapSamples(SampleBlock& samples, unsigned threads, const Map& map) {
    if (Raster<float>* grid = samples.Grid()) {
        MapCells(*grid, threads, map);
        return;
    }
    MapPoints(samples, map);
}

template <typename Draw>
void DrawFeatures(SampleBlock& samples, unsigned threads, const std::vector<Bounds2d>& boxes,
                  const Surface& surface, const Draw& draw) {
    if (Raster<float>* grid = samples.Grid()) {
        const Span<const float> values = static_cast<const Raster<float>&>(*grid).Values();
        const std::vector<float> base(values.begin(), values.end());
        const std::size_t width = grid->Width();
        ForEachFeatureCell(*grid, threads, boxes, surface, [&](float& cell, const FeatureCell& at) {
            cell = draw(cell, base[at.row * width + at.col], at.center, at.feature);
        });
        return;
    }
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < samples.Size(); ++i) {
        if (samples.IsNoData(i)) {
            continue;
        }
        const Vec2d p = samples.Position(i);
        const float base = samples.Height(i);
        for (std::size_t n = 0; n < boxes.size(); ++n) {
            if (surface.Contains(boxes[n], p)) {
                samples.Height(i) = draw(samples.Height(i), base, p, n);
            }
        }
    }
}

}  // namespace terraingen

// SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause

#pragma once

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstddef>
#include <functional>
#include <list>
#include <memory>
#include <mutex>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

namespace terraingen {

template <typename Key, typename Value, typename Hash = std::hash<Key>> class LruCache {
  public:
    using Cost = std::function<std::size_t(const Value&)>;
    using OnEvict = std::function<void(std::size_t evicted)>;

    LruCache(std::size_t capacity, Cost cost, OnEvict onEvict = {},
             std::size_t shards = kDefaultShards)
        : m_capacity(capacity), m_cost(std::move(cost)), m_onEvict(std::move(onEvict)),
          m_shards(shards) {
        if (m_capacity == 0 || shards == 0) {
            throw std::invalid_argument("A cache needs a positive capacity and shards");
        }
    }

    std::shared_ptr<const Value> Find(const Key& key) {
        return Lookup(ShardHolding(key), key);
    }

    std::shared_ptr<const Value> Get(const Key& key, const std::function<Value()>& compute) {
        Shard& shard = ShardHolding(key);
        if (auto held = Lookup(shard, key)) {
            return held;
        }
        auto value = std::make_shared<const Value>(compute());
        const std::size_t cost = m_cost(*value);
        const std::size_t budget = std::max<std::size_t>(1, m_capacity / m_shards.size());
        std::size_t evicted = 0;
        {
            const std::lock_guard lock(shard.mutex);
            if (const auto found = shard.entries.find(key); found != shard.entries.end()) {
                return found->second.value;
            }
            shard.recency.push_front(key);
            shard.entries.emplace(key, Entry{value, cost, shard.recency.begin()});
            shard.cost += cost;
            while (shard.cost > budget && shard.recency.size() > 1) {
                const auto oldest = shard.entries.find(shard.recency.back());
                shard.cost -= oldest->second.cost;
                shard.entries.erase(oldest);
                shard.recency.pop_back();
                ++evicted;
            }
        }
        if (evicted > 0 && m_onEvict) {
            m_onEvict(evicted);
        }
        return value;
    }

    std::size_t Size() const {
        std::size_t total = 0;
        for (const Shard& shard : m_shards) {
            const std::lock_guard lock(shard.mutex);
            total += shard.cost;
        }
        return total;
    }

  private:
    struct Entry {
        std::shared_ptr<const Value> value;
        std::size_t cost = 0;
        typename std::list<Key>::iterator recent;
    };
    struct Shard {
        mutable std::mutex mutex;
        std::list<Key> recency;
        std::unordered_map<Key, Entry, Hash> entries;
        std::size_t cost = 0;
    };
    static constexpr std::size_t kDefaultShards = 16;

    Shard& ShardHolding(const Key& key) {
        return m_shards[Hash{}(key) % m_shards.size()];
    }

    static std::shared_ptr<const Value> Lookup(Shard& shard, const Key& key) {
        const std::lock_guard lock(shard.mutex);
        const auto found = shard.entries.find(key);
        if (found == shard.entries.end()) {
            return nullptr;
        }
        shard.recency.splice(shard.recency.begin(), shard.recency, found->second.recent);
        return found->second.value;
    }

    std::size_t m_capacity;
    Cost m_cost;
    OnEvict m_onEvict;
    std::vector<Shard> m_shards;
};

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
Each option struct has a Fields(IO& io, Struct& value) beside it that calls io(key, member, description, unit, range) for each field in order. The same list checks ranges (CheckRanges), reads and writes configurations, describes their schema and binds the Python options classes, each by passing its own IO. Rules that tie fields together stay in each struct's validation function.

struct FieldRange {
    std::optional<double> minimum;           
    std::optional<double> maximum;           
    bool exclusiveMinimum = false;           
    bool exclusiveMaximum = false;           
    std::optional<std::size_t> minLength{};  
    std::optional<std::size_t> maxLength{};  
    bool lengthAtBounds = false;
    bool required = false;

    FieldRange Required() const {
        FieldRange range = *this;
        range.required = true;
        return range;
    }
    FieldRange Length(std::size_t count) const {
        return Length(count, count);
    }
    FieldRange Length(std::size_t fewest, std::size_t most) const {
        FieldRange range = *this;
        range.minLength = fewest;
        range.maxLength = most;
        return range;
    }
    FieldRange MinLength(std::size_t fewest) const {
        FieldRange range = *this;
        range.minLength = fewest;
        return range;
    }
    FieldRange LengthEither(std::size_t fewer, std::size_t more) const {
        FieldRange range = Length(fewer, more);
        range.lengthAtBounds = true;
        return range;
    }
    FieldRange Items() const {
        return {minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum, exclusiveMaximum};
    }
    bool Bounded() const {
        return minimum || maximum;
    }
    bool Counted() const {
        return minLength || maxLength;
    }
};

inline FieldRange Required() {
    return FieldRange{}.Required();
}

inline FieldRange Length(std::size_t count) {
    return FieldRange{}.Length(count);
}

inline FieldRange Length(std::size_t fewest, std::size_t most) {
    return FieldRange{}.Length(fewest, most);
}

inline FieldRange MinLength(std::size_t fewest) {
    return FieldRange{}.MinLength(fewest);
}

inline FieldRange LengthEither(std::size_t fewer, std::size_t more) {
    return FieldRange{}.LengthEither(fewer, more);
}

inline FieldRange AtLeast(double minimum) {
    return {minimum, std::nullopt};
}

inline FieldRange Above(double minimum) {
    return {minimum, std::nullopt, true, false};
}

inline FieldRange Between(double minimum, double maximum) {
    return {minimum, maximum};
}

inline FieldRange FromBelow(double minimum, double maximum) {
    return {minimum, maximum, false, true};
}

inline FieldRange AboveUpTo(double minimum, double maximum) {
    return {minimum, maximum, true, false};
}

inline FieldRange Inside(double minimum, double maximum) {
    return {minimum, maximum, true, true};
}

inline FieldRange UnitInterval() {
    return Between(0.0, 1.0);
}

std::string RangeRule(const FieldRange& range, std::string_view unit = {});

template <typename IO, typename = void> struct BindsNativeTrait : std::false_type {};
template <typename IO>
struct BindsNativeTrait<IO, std::enable_if_t<IO::kBindsNative>> : std::true_type {};

template <typename IO> inline constexpr bool BindsNative = BindsNativeTrait<IO>::value;

template <typename IO>
void OptionalBound(IO& io, std::string_view key, double& bound, std::string_view description,
                   std::string_view unit = {},
                   double unset = std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity(),
                   const FieldRange& range = {}) {
    if constexpr (BindsNative<IO>) {
        io.Bound(key, bound, description, unit, unset, range);
        return;
    }
    std::optional<double> value;
    if (std::isfinite(bound)) {
        value = bound;
    }
    io(key, value, description, unit, range);
    bound = value.value_or(unset);
}

inline std::string FieldPath(const std::string& path, std::string_view key) {
    return path.empty() ? std::string(key) : path + "." + std::string(key);
}

inline std::string ItemPath(const std::string& path, std::size_t index) {
    return path + "[" + std::to_string(index) + "]";
}

class FieldRangeError : public std::invalid_argument {
  public:
    FieldRangeError(std::string path, std::string rule)
        : std::invalid_argument(path.empty() ? rule : path + ": " + rule), m_path(std::move(path)),
          m_rule(std::move(rule)) {}

    const std::string& Path() const {
        return m_path;
    }
    const std::string& Rule() const {
        return m_rule;
    }

  private:
    std::string m_path;
    std::string m_rule;
};

void CheckRange(double value, const FieldRange& range, std::string_view unit,
                const std::string& path);

void CheckLength(std::size_t count, const FieldRange& range, const std::string& path);

class RangeChecker;

template <typename T, typename = void> struct HasRangedFieldsTrait : std::false_type {};
template <typename T>
struct HasRangedFieldsTrait<
    T, std::void_t<decltype(Fields(std::declval<RangeChecker&>(), std::declval<T&>()))>>
    : std::true_type {};

template <typename T> inline constexpr bool HasRangedFields = HasRangedFieldsTrait<T>::value;

template <typename T>
void CheckValueRanges(T& value, const std::string& path, std::string_view unit,
                      const FieldRange& range);
template <typename T>
void CheckValueRanges(std::optional<T>& value, const std::string& path, std::string_view unit,
                      const FieldRange& range);
template <typename T>
void CheckValueRanges(std::vector<T>& value, const std::string& path, std::string_view unit,
                      const FieldRange& range);
template <typename... Ts>
void CheckValueRanges(std::variant<Ts...>& value, const std::string& path, std::string_view unit,
                      const FieldRange& range);
void CheckValueRanges(std::array<double, 2>& value, const std::string& path, std::string_view unit,
                      const FieldRange& range);

class RangeChecker {
  public:
    explicit RangeChecker(std::string path = {}) : m_path(std::move(path)) {}

    template <typename T>
    void operator()(std::string_view key, T& value, std::string_view /*description*/ = {},
                    std::string_view unit = {}, const FieldRange& range = {}) {
        CheckValueRanges(value, FieldPath(m_path, key), unit, range);
    }

  private:
    std::string m_path;
};

template <typename T>
void CheckValueRanges(T& value, const std::string& path, std::string_view unit,
                      const FieldRange& range) {
    if constexpr (std::is_arithmetic_v<T> && !std::is_same_v<T, bool>) {
        CheckRange(static_cast<double>(value), range, unit, path);
    } else if constexpr (HasRangedFields<T>) {
        RangeChecker checker(path);
        Fields(checker, value);
    }
}

template <typename T>
void CheckValueRanges(std::optional<T>& value, const std::string& path, std::string_view unit,
                      const FieldRange& range) {
    if (value) {
        CheckValueRanges(*value, path, unit, range);
    } else if (range.required) {
        throw FieldRangeError(path, "required");
    }
}

template <typename T>
void CheckValueRanges(std::vector<T>& value, const std::string& path, std::string_view unit,
                      const FieldRange& range) {
    CheckLength(value.size(), range, path);
    const FieldRange items = range.Items();
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < value.size(); ++i) {
        CheckValueRanges(value[i], ItemPath(path, i), unit, items);
    }
}

template <typename... Ts>
void CheckValueRanges(std::variant<Ts...>& value, const std::string& path, std::string_view unit,
                      const FieldRange& range) {
    std::visit([&](auto& alternative) { CheckValueRanges(alternative, path, unit, range); }, value);
}

inline void CheckValueRanges(std::array<double, 2>& value, const std::string& path,
                             std::string_view unit, const FieldRange& range) {
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < value.size(); ++i) {
        CheckRange(value[i], range, unit, ItemPath(path, i));
    }
}

template <typename T> void CheckRanges(const T& options) {
    T copy = options;
    RangeChecker checker;
    Fields(checker, copy);
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause

#pragma once

#include <cassert>
#include <cstddef>
#include <iterator>
#include <type_traits>
#include <utility>

namespace terraingen {

namespace detail {

template <typename T, typename C, typename = void> struct IsSpanContainer : std::false_type {};

template <typename T, typename C>
struct IsSpanContainer<
    T, C,
    std::void_t<decltype(std::data(std::declval<C&>())), decltype(std::size(std::declval<C&>()))>>
    : std::is_convertible<std::remove_pointer_t<decltype(std::data(std::declval<C&>()))> (*)[],
                          T (*)[]> {};

}  // namespace detail

template <typename T> class Span {
  public:
    using element_type = T;
    using value_type = std::remove_cv_t<T>;
    using size_type = std::size_t;
    using pointer = T*;
    using reference = T&;
    using iterator = T*;

    constexpr Span() noexcept = default;
    constexpr Span(T* data, std::size_t size) noexcept : m_data(data), m_size(size) {}
    constexpr Span(T* first, T* last) noexcept
        : m_data(first), m_size(static_cast<std::size_t>(last - first)) {}

    template <std::size_t N> constexpr Span(T (&array)[N]) noexcept : m_data(array), m_size(N) {}

    template <typename C, typename = std::enable_if_t<!std::is_same_v<std::decay_t<C>, Span> &&
                                                      detail::IsSpanContainer<T, C>::value>>
    constexpr Span(C&& container) noexcept
        : m_data(std::data(container)), m_size(std::size(container)) {}

    constexpr T* data() const noexcept {
        return m_data;
    }
    constexpr std::size_t size() const noexcept {
        return m_size;
    }
    constexpr std::size_t size_bytes() const noexcept {
        return m_size * sizeof(T);
    }
    constexpr bool empty() const noexcept {
        return m_size == 0;
    }

    constexpr T* begin() const noexcept {
        return m_data;
    }
    constexpr T* end() const noexcept {
        return m_data + m_size;
    }

    constexpr T& operator[](std::size_t index) const {
        assert(index < m_size);
        return m_data[index];
    }
    constexpr T& front() const {
        return (*this)[0];
    }
    constexpr T& back() const {
        return (*this)[m_size - 1];
    }

    constexpr Span first(std::size_t count) const {
        assert(count <= m_size);
        return {m_data, count};
    }
    constexpr Span last(std::size_t count) const {
        assert(count <= m_size);
        return {m_data + (m_size - count), count};
    }
    constexpr Span subspan(std::size_t offset,
                           std::size_t count = static_cast<std::size_t>(-1)) const {
        assert(offset <= m_size);
        const std::size_t rest = m_size - offset;
        assert(count == static_cast<std::size_t>(-1) || count <= rest);
        return {m_data + offset, count == static_cast<std::size_t>(-1) ? rest : count};
    }

  private:
    T* m_data = nullptr;
    std::size_t m_size = 0;
};

template <typename T, std::size_t N> Span(T (&)[N]) -> Span<T>;
template <typename C>
Span(C&) -> Span<std::remove_pointer_t<decltype(std::data(std::declval<C&>()))>>;
template <typename C>
Span(const C&) -> Span<std::remove_pointer_t<decltype(std::data(std::declval<const C&>()))>>;
template <typename T> Span(T*, std::size_t) -> Span<T>;

template <typename T> Span<const std::byte> AsBytes(Span<T> span) noexcept {
    return {reinterpret_cast<const std::byte*>(span.data()), span.size_bytes()};
}

template <typename T, typename = std::enable_if_t<!std::is_const_v<T>>>
Span<std::byte> AsWritableBytes(Span<T> span) noexcept {
    return {reinterpret_cast<std::byte*>(span.data()), span.size_bytes()};
}

docs.title: Class Hierarchy
docs.text:
This inheritance list is sorted roughly, but not completely, alphabetically:

  • class terraingen::AlbedoLayer A change to an albedo: bright ejecta around fresh craters, or a layer of your own.
    • class terraingen::BlastZoneAlbedo Blast zones around landers, changing the albedo by the relative reflectance they give; the same in any grid, tile or point.
    • class terraingen::CraterAlbedo The bright ejecta, interiors and rays of the craters of a CraterLayer , asCraterAlbedoOptions describes, shaped by the craters' irregular outlines where the layer has them.
    • class terraingen::RockAlbedo The albedo brightened by the rock of boulder layers: each band times 1 + share (reflectanceRatio - 1), for the share of each sample rock covers over every layer.
    • class terraingen::SlopeAlbedo The albedo of steep ground moved toward fresher material: slopes are read on the ground at the nodes of a lattice baseline meters apart, fixed to the surface, and interpolated between them, so grids, tiles and points agree.
    • class terraingen::SplotchAlbedo The splotches of SplotchAlbedoOptions on the context's surface, darkening and brightening the albedo; the same in any grid, tile or point.
  • class terraingen::AlbedoSource Where an albedo starts: a map from orbit, a synthetic color, or a source of your own.
    • class terraingen::RasterAlbedo An albedo map, such as a normal albedo mosaic from orbit, upscaled to the grid: interpolated with method (SampleRaster ), then given sub-cell detail (AlbedoDetail ).
    • class terraingen::SyntheticAlbedo An albedo for terrain without data: a base color with noise in each channel, the saturation and value clamped to [0, 1] after it.
  • class terraingen::AnchoredPlane The plane a layer lays its features out in: the surface itself on a plane, or on a body the tangent frame of anchor , true to scale near it and empty on the far hemisphere.
  • class terraingen::BandBuckets Indices bucketed per size band into cubes of a side set per band ( Surface::Bucket ), each bucket holding its indices in the order added.
  • class terraingen::Layer Relief added on top of a source: noise, craters, or a layer of your own.
    • class terraingen::BoulderLayer Boulders scattered over the ground, in patches and richer on bedrock, plus blocks around fresh craters; they depend only on position, so every grid, tile and point agrees.
    • class terraingen::CraterLayer Craters generated over the grid being evaluated ( GenerateCraters ) and applied to it (ApplyCraters ) at the evaluation's spacing.
    • class terraingen::FormulaLayer A layer whose height at a point depends only on the height there and the point (noise, roughness, transforms); the base applies HeightAt to every sample in parallel.
      • class terraingen::BedformLayer Fields of wind-blown bedforms, ripples or dunes, added to the terrain.
      • class terraingen::ClampLayer Clamps the heights so far to [ min ,max ], either bound optional.
      • class terraingen::DuneLayer Wind-blown dunes added to the terrain, barchan crescents or crest-line dunes with slip faces at slipFaceAngle ; overlapping dunes join as their upper envelope.
      • class terraingen::FunctionLayer A layer from a function of position, sample spacing and the height so far.
      • class terraingen::PavementLayer Fractured bedrock pavement added to the terrain: Voronoi plates, each flat with its own tilt and height step, parted by cracks (or ridges) with rounded shoulders, and split again by finer octaves of cracks that end at the cracks before them; each octave fades out where too fine for the spacing.
      • class terraingen::RoughnessLayer Fine roughness: octaves of Perlin noise from maxWavelength tominWavelength , amplitudes growing as wavelength^H and scaled tormsSlope overbaseline ; unresolved octaves fade.
      • class terraingen::SandFillLayer Sand pooled in the lows of the ground beneath it, filling fill of the depth below the mean height on two rings, up tomaxThickness ; it lays sand over the material map.
      • class terraingen::ScaleLayer Scales and shifts the heights so far: height * scale +offset .
      • class terraingen::StrataLayer Layered rock: the ground beneath terraced into dipping beds, each a bench below a cliff, so hills become buttes and mesas; it lays bedrock over the material map on the cliffs.
    • class terraingen::MaskedLayer Another layer applied only inside a region, blended back to the unchanged height over feather meters outside it.
    • class terraingen::NoiseLayer A stack of fractals added to the terrain, rolling relief on a flat source or detail on a DEM, measured from the context's ReferencePoint .
    • class terraingen::SandShadowLayer Sand shadows: a pyramidal sand tail in the lee of each boulder of a boulder layer, as wide as the boulder and lengthRatio widths long (Hesp 1981); place it after the boulder layer.
    • class terraingen::SecondaryCraterLayer Secondary craters around the craters of a CraterLayer , applied additively withApplyCraters .
    • class terraingen::SpectralContinuationLayer Detail finer than a base DEM that continues its power-law spectrum with random phases (Saupe 1988), as sparse Gabor noise (Lagae et al.
  • class terraingen::MaterialSource A layer that lays a material over the surface beneath it, such as sand from dunes.
    • class terraingen::BedformLayer Fields of wind-blown bedforms, ripples or dunes, added to the terrain.
    • class terraingen::BoulderLayer Boulders scattered over the ground, in patches and richer on bedrock, plus blocks around fresh craters; they depend only on position, so every grid, tile and point agrees.
    • class terraingen::DuneLayer Wind-blown dunes added to the terrain, barchan crescents or crest-line dunes with slip faces at slipFaceAngle ; overlapping dunes join as their upper envelope.
    • class terraingen::PavementLayer Fractured bedrock pavement added to the terrain: Voronoi plates, each flat with its own tilt and height step, parted by cracks (or ridges) with rounded shoulders, and split again by finer octaves of cracks that end at the cracks before them; each octave fades out where too fine for the spacing.
    • class terraingen::SandFillLayer Sand pooled in the lows of the ground beneath it, filling fill of the depth below the mean height on two rings, up tomaxThickness ; it lays sand over the material map.
    • class terraingen::SandShadowLayer Sand shadows: a pyramidal sand tail in the lee of each boulder of a boulder layer, as wide as the boulder and lengthRatio widths long (Hesp 1981); place it after the boulder layer.
    • class terraingen::StrataLayer Layered rock: the ground beneath terraced into dipping beds, each a bench below a cliff, so hills become buttes and mesas; it lays bedrock over the material map on the cliffs.
  • class terraingen::BoulderPlacer A layer that places boulders.
    • class terraingen::BoulderLayer Boulders scattered over the ground, in patches and richer on bedrock, plus blocks around fresh craters; they depend only on position, so every grid, tile and point agrees.
    • class terraingen::MaskedLayer Another layer applied only inside a region, blended back to the unchanged height over feather meters outside it.
  • class terraingen::BoulderList Boulders stored as one array per field, as CraterList stores craters, so each column can be shared with NumPy or a GPU without copying.
  • class terraingen::BoulderMapAbundance How a density map sets a boulder layer's abundance between craters: the abundance at which the boulder sizes measure what the map does, once the crater blocks there are taken out of it for a total map.
  • class terraingen::CraterProfile The topography of a crater: height relative to the pre-impact surface by distance from the center, for a degradation state.
    • class terraingen::ComplexCraterProfile Simple craters below a transition diameter, complex ones from it: a flat floor, a concave wall, a central peak lowered as the crater wears, and a power-law exterior.
    • class terraingen::DiffusedProfile A fresh crater profile worn by topographic diffusion, tabulated in the diffusion age tau = kappa t / D^2 from 1e-5 to 0.5; older craters keep the last shape.
    • class terraingen::FassettThomsonProfile Fresh simple-crater profile of Fassett and Thomson (2014, eq.
    • class terraingen::MartinParkesDunstanProfile Simple-crater profile of Martin, Parkes and Dunstan (2014): bowl, inner rim, outer rim and ejecta polynomials joined continuously; degradation rounds the rim.
  • class terraingen::SurfaceField A scalar quantity over a surface, read at surface coordinates: meters on a plane, longitude and latitude in degrees on a sphere.
    • class terraingen::ConstantField The same value everywhere.
    • class terraingen::MinimumField The smaller of two fields at each point, the one that has a value where the other is NaN: a completeness limit that two limits give, such as a catalog's and a DEM's ( SourceResolvedLimit ).
    • class terraingen::RasterField A field interpolated from a raster in the surface's coordinates.
  • class terraingen::CraterAgeModel Assigns ages to craters by diameter, within a visible lifetime per diameter.
    • class terraingen::FreshAges Every crater is fresh: age and lifetime zero.
    • class terraingen::FreshnessAges Ages from a freshness f in [0, 1] drawn per crater: age = (1 - f) * lifetime, with one lifetime for every diameter, so RemainingLifetime gives back f.
    • class terraingen::SteadyStateAges Ages of craters on a surface ageGyr old where small craters are in equilibrium.
    • class terraingen::UniformAges Ages uniform over one lifetime for every diameter, so freshness is uniform in [0, 1].
  • class terraingen::CraterPlacer A layer that places craters.
    • class terraingen::CraterLayer Craters generated over the grid being evaluated ( GenerateCraters ) and applied to it (ApplyCraters ) at the evaluation's spacing.
    • class terraingen::MaskedLayer Another layer applied only inside a region, blended back to the unchanged height over feather meters outside it.
    • class terraingen::SecondaryCraterLayer Secondary craters around the craters of a CraterLayer , applied additively withApplyCraters .
  • class terraingen::CraterList Craters stored as one array per field, so each column can be shared with NumPy or a GPU without copying.
  • class terraingen::SurfaceCells Partitions a surface into cells so features can be generated per cell, each from its own random substream, identically however a region is tiled.
    • class terraingen::CubeSphereCells Near-square cells on a body, in longitude and latitude degrees: each face of a cube split into n x n cells along equiangular coordinates of the direction from the center.
    • class terraingen::PlanarCells Square cells on a plane: cell (i, j) of side L covers [i L, (i + 1) L) x [j L, (j + 1) L).
  • class terraingen::DegradationModel Maps each crater to its degradation state, from its diameter and age.
    • class terraingen::DiffusionDegradation Craters worn by topographic diffusion, shaped with its DiffusedProfile .
    • class terraingen::FreshnessDegradation Scales fresh depth and rim height by e = c + (1 - c) * RemainingLifetime , with c making a crater at the end of its lifetime exactlycutoffDepthRatio deep; a crater already shallower than that when fresh, such as a large basin, keeps its fresh shape.
    • class terraingen::NoDegradation Every crater stays as fresh makes it, optionally with one depth/diameter ratio for all.
  • class terraingen::DensityScale The local scale a density map gives a size distribution: the map's value over its measure of the distribution, 1 where the map has no value.
  • class terraingen::Upsampler How a source's posts become heights at any point and at any sample spacing in the posts' units: interpolation, or refinement that adds detail as the spacing shrinks.
    • class terraingen::DiamondSquareUpsampler Random midpoint displacement of a source's posts (Martin, Parkes and Dunstan 2014; Peitgen and Saupe 1988): each level halves the node spacing and displaces new nodes by a Gaussian that shrinks by 2^-((3 - F) / 2) per step, keyed by node and level so grids, tiles and points agree.
    • class terraingen::KernelUpsampler Interpolation of the posts with a kernel ( ResampleMethod ), at every spacing alike:Cubic , the default, gives the same bits asSampleRaster of the posts.
  • class terraingen::EjectaIndex Craters bucketed by the discs their ejecta reach ( BandBuckets , one band per power of two of reach), so the craters able to reach a point are found without visiting all of them.
  • class terraingen::EvaluationCache Thread-safe values that depend only on the terrain beneath a layer, such as crater datums, shared by point queries; use one cache per generator and renew it after changing its layers.
  • class terraingen::ExposureField How far the ground at a point is bedrock rather than soil, from its shape alone.
  • class terraingen::Source Where a terrain's heights come from: a DEM, synthetic noise, or your own.
    • class terraingen::FlatSource A level datum at elevation over awidth xheight north-up grid of squarepixelSize cells centered oncenter : the start of a fully synthetic terrain.
    • class terraingen::ShapeModelSource The heights a shape model's labels give when an upsampler refines them, over the body made from it ( Surface::ShapeModel ), whose radius interpolates the same labels bilinearly.
    • class terraingen::SourceChain Sources tried in order, each filling where those before it have no data, such as a site DEM over a regional one or a DEM over a flat datum.
    • class terraingen::SyntheticSource Heights generated rather than loaded: elevation plus a stack of fractals (FractalStackAt , measured from the origin on a plane, in 3D on a body), with no bounds.
    • class terraingen::detail::RasterHeightsSource A source serving the upsampled heights of a window of a lattice: what RasterSource andGeoTiffSource share.
      • class terraingen::GeoTiffSource Heights from one band of a GeoTIFF in a projected CRS, or in longitude and latitude (a geographic CRS) for a terrain on a body, served as a RasterSource serves its raster; samples take the band's scale and offset, orscale andoffset .
      • class terraingen::RasterSource Heights from a raster held in memory, in a projected CRS or the surface's coordinates.
  • class terraingen::GeoTiffBlockReader One band of a GeoTIFF's first image read a block at a time from the file held open, a block being a tile or a strip spanning every column; blocks hold the samples ReadGeoTiff reads.
  • class terraingen::SizeFrequencyDistribution A cumulative size-frequency distribution N(>=D) of craters or boulders.
    • class terraingen::GolombekRappSfd Boulder densities whose cumulative fractional area is F(D) = k exp(-q D), with q =qa +qb / k per meter and k the fraction of ground the boulders cover (coverage ); N(>=D) = (4 k q / pi) E2(q D) / D per m^2.
    • class terraingen::LogPolynomialSfd N(>=D) = 10^P(x) / areaUnit with P(x) = sum_i a_i x^i and x = log10(D /diameterUnit ), the form of the Neukum et al.
    • class terraingen::MinimumSfd The pointwise minimum of distributions of one kind, such as the DSNE crater density: the lesser of the production surface and the equilibrium density at every diameter.
    • class terraingen::PiecewisePowerLawSfd A cumulative distribution of power-law segments, each applying from its start to the next.
    • class terraingen::PiecewiseUniformSfd A distribution of diameter bands, each holding features per m^2 with diameters uniform across it; overlapping bands add.
    • class terraingen::PowerLawSfd N(>=D) = coefficient * D^(-exponent ), with D in meters and N per m^2 (or per m^2 per Gyr).
    • class terraingen::ProductionSurface The cumulative crater density on a surface of a given age: a production function scaled so that N(>=1 km) follows a chronology, N(D, T) = Phi(D) * N1(T) / Phi(1 km).
    • class terraingen::SplicedSfd A cumulative distribution made of other distributions over consecutive diameter intervals, such as a production function extended below its fitted range by a power law.
    • class terraingen::SummedSfd The sum of weighted distributions of one kind, N(>=D) = sum of weight * N_i(>=D), such as boulders between craters plus the blocks thrown out by them.
    • class terraingen::TabulatedSfd A cumulative distribution given as a table of (D, N(>=D)) points, interpolated linearly in log D and log N, so each interval is a power law.
  • class terraingen::Ground The terrain beneath a layer (its source and the layers before it), readable anywhere.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
A configuration is a JSON file the terraingen command, GenerateFromConfig and terraingen.load_config read. This reference is generated from the same field lists the parser reads, so it always matches the library; the raw schema is the same information as JSON, for editors and tools.

Each description ends with what the field accepts on its own, its range, length and whether it is required; validation also checks the rules that tie fields together.

docs.title: Top level
docs.text:
schema_version

integer, fixed · default 1

Version of the configuration format, which this library reads. Required.

body

bodies · default {"type": "plane", ...}

What the terrain lies on: a plane in meters, or a whole body (a sphere, ellipsoid or shape model) in longitude and latitude degrees.

source

sources, optional · default null

Where the heights come from: a GeoTIFF, a chain of sources or synthetic noise, with its upsampling; unset is fBm noise 400 m in wavelength and 12 m in amplitude at the datum.

layers

list of layers · default []

Relief and features added to the source's heights, applied in order: noise, craters, boulders and more.

outputs

list of outputs · default []

What to produce, at what resolution and where, each over its own extent or the whole body: heightmaps, crater and boulder lists, boulder models, albedo, meshes and reports. Each is returned, and written to its path when it has one.

albedo: The terrain's albedo: a source and the layers that change it, written by albedo outputs; none when unset. source

albedo sources · default {"type": "synthetic", ...}

Base albedo of the terrain, before its layers: a synthetic color or a raster map.

layers

list of albedo layers · default []

Layers applied to the source's albedo in order, such as bright crater ejecta and rays.

materials: The material map: soil, sand, dust, bedrock and rock shares, and their Hapke parameters, written by materials and photometry outputs; none when unset. dust_cover

number · default 0.0

About the share of the surface under bright dust patches. Must be from 0 to below 1.

dust_patch_m

number · default 50.0 · unit m

Typical width of a dust patch, in meters. Must be positive.

seed

integer · default 0

Seed of the dust patches.

exposure: Thresholds marking bare ground as bedrock, read on the ground beneath the first layer that lays a material; unset for no bedrock. reach_m

number · default 12.0 · unit m

Distance in meters around a point at which its surroundings are read, to tell rises from lows. Must be positive.

rise_soil

number · default 0.01

Height above the surroundings, as a share of the reach, at or below which the ground is soil.

rise_boulder

number · default 0.035

Height above the surroundings, as a share of the reach, at or above which the ground is bedrock; above the soil threshold.

slope_soil

number · default 0.2

Slope, as rise over run, at or under which soil holds.

slope_boulder

number · default 0.4

Slope, as rise over run, at or over which no soil holds and the ground is bedrock; above the soil threshold.

floor_cover

number · default 0.0

Share of level ground that is bedrock too, in noise patches, as on a swept lava floor; 0 for none. Must be from 0 to below 1.

floor_patch_m

number · default 60.0 · unit m

Width of the bedrock patches on level ground, in meters. Must be positive.

seed

integer · default 0

Seed of the bedrock patches on level ground.

photometry: Hapke parameters of each material class, which photometry outputs mix. reference

one of none, mars_pancam · default "none"

Published Hapke parameters to start from; each class given below replaces its own.

soil: Hapke parameters of soil; unset keeps the reference's. albedo

number · default 0.0

Single-scattering albedo w. Must be from 0 to 1.

b

number · default 0.0

Asymmetry b of the two-term Henyey-Greenstein phase function. Must be from 0 to 1.

c

number · default 0.0

docs.title: Bodies
docs.text:
Chosen by "type" in body.

Type Description plane A flat projected frame in meters, for local sites. sphere A whole body such as a planet or moon: positions in longitude and latitude (degrees) and features generated over the whole body. ellipsoid A whole body shaped as a triaxial ellipsoid, such as an elongated moon or asteroid: planetocentric longitude and latitude (degrees), heights along the direction from the center, and features generated over the whole body. shape_model A whole star-shaped body such as an asteroid from a shape model, resampled along rays from its origin; heights are radial, in longitude and latitude degrees.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
Chosen by "type" in source, sources.

Type Description raster A heightmap read from a GeoTIFF in its own projected coordinates, its cells upsampled to finer spacings, to add relief to a real DEM. chain Several sources tried in order, each filling where those before it have no data; its grid is the first one's. synthetic Heights generated from a stack of fractal noise layers over an unbounded plane or the whole body; outputs give their own extents and pixel sizes. shape_model The shape-model body's own labels refined by an upsampler; the default source on such a body.

docs.title: raster
docs.text:
A heightmap read from a GeoTIFF in its own projected coordinates, its cells upsampled to finer spacings, to add relief to a real DEM.

path

string · default ""

GeoTIFF to read the heights from; relative paths resolve against the configuration's folder. Required.

band

integer · default 0

Band of the file to read, counting from 0.

scale

number, optional · default null

Factor each sample is multiplied by, replacing the band's scale from the file's GDAL metadata. Unset keeps the file's.

offset_m

number, optional · default null · unit m

Added to each scaled sample, replacing the band's offset from the file's GDAL metadata. Unset keeps the file's.

effective_pixel_size_m

number, optional · default null · unit m

Cell size in meters the heights truly resolve, for a DEM that was upsampled or smoothed before it was saved; it replaces the cell size as the scale below which the source resolves no features. Unset uses the cell size. Must be positive.

upsampling

upsampling · default "cubic"

How the posts are refined between them and at finer spacings: a kernel name such as cubic or lanczos3, or an object with a "type" and its settings, such as {"type": "diamond_square"} for fractal detail.

crop: Box in the raster's CRS units to use; unset uses the whole file. min_x

number · default 0.0

Lower edge along x.

min_y

number · default 0.0

Lower edge along y.

max_x

number · default 0.0

Upper edge along x; above min_x.

max_y

number · default 0.0

Upper edge along y; above min_y.

Every key with its default 
{
    "type": "raster",
    "path": "",
    "band": 0,
    "scale": null,
    "offset_m": null,
    "crop": null,
    "effective_pixel_size_m": null,
    "upsampling": "cubic"
}

docs.title: chain
docs.text:
Several sources tried in order, each filling where those before it have no data; its grid is the first one's.

sources

list of sources · default []

Sources tried in order, each filling where those before it have no data, each upsampled as it says; the chain's grid is the first one's. Holds at least 1 item.

seams: How each source is matched to the sources before it where it fills their gaps; by default each switches outright. mode

one of none, feather, height, slope · default "none"

How each source meets the gaps of those before it: none switches outright, feather fades the edge's height difference out across the gap, height shifts the later source to meet the earlier one's heights (C0) and slope to meet its heights and slopes (C1). The match is solved on the posts of the source before each gap.

width_m

number · default 50.0 · unit m

Width in meters of the band inside a gap over which feather fades the height difference at the edge to 0. Must be positive.

decay_length_m

number · default 50.0 · unit m

Length in meters over which height and slope fade the shift out where a gap is open, beyond a source's edge; it is 0 from three decay lengths on. A hole much narrower than it takes the whole shift. Must be positive.

Every key with its default 
{
    "type": "chain",
    "sources": [],
    "seams": {
        "mode": "none",
        "width_m": 50.0,
        "decay_length_m": 50.0
    }
}

docs.title: synthetic
docs.text:
Heights generated from a stack of fractal noise layers over an unbounded plane or the whole body; outputs give their own extents and pixel sizes.

elevation_m

number · default 0.0 · unit m

Height in meters added everywhere.

pixel_size_m

number, optional · default null · unit m

Spacing in meters of posts the noise is sampled at, as for a DEM of that cell size, which upsampling refines. Unset evaluates the noise at every point, at any spacing. Must be positive.

upsampling

upsampling, optional · default null

How the posts are refined between them and at finer spacings: a kernel name such as cubic or lanczos3, or an object with a "type" and its settings, such as {"type": "diamond_square"} for fractal detail. Needs pixel_size_m; unset is cubic.

stack[]: Noise layers, combined in order: the first enabled layer sets the height and each later one is combined with it by its blend mode. Unset is one layer of fBm noise 400 m in wavelength and 12 m in amplitude; an empty stack gives a flat source. Holds 0 to 8 items. enabled

boolean · default true

Includes this layer in the stack; disabled layers are skipped.

basis

one of perlin, simplex, value, worley_f1, worley_f2, worley_f2_minus_f1, voronoi · default "perlin"

Single-octave noise the fractal is built from.

fractal

one of fbm, ridged, billow, hybrid_multifractal · default "fbm"

How the octaves of the basis noise are combined.

blend

one of add, max, min, mask · default "add"

How this layer combines with the height of the layers before it; the first enabled layer sets the height instead.

seed

integer · default 0

Seed of the noise; changing it gives a different pattern of the same character.

wavelength_m

number · default 1000.0 · unit m

Wavelength of the first, broadest octave, in meters; sets the size of the largest features. Must be positive.

amplitude_m

number, optional · default null · unit m

Largest height of the layer above or below 0, in meters; unset is 0.1 times the wavelength, near the lunar highland median slope at any wavelength.

octaves

integer · default 8

Number of octaves; each one adds detail at a shorter wavelength. Must be from 1 to 32.

lacunarity

number · default 2.0

Frequency ratio between successive octaves. Must be above 1.

gain

number · default 0.5

Weight ratio between successive octaves; higher values give rougher terrain. Unused when the Hurst exponent is set. Must be positive.

hurst

number, optional · default null

Hurst exponent that sets the octave gain to lacunarity^-hurst: near 1 is smooth, lower is rougher at short baselines. Unset uses the gain.

offset

number · default 1.0

Ridge offset of the ridged and hybrid multifractal types. Must be positive.

warp_amplitude_m

number · default 0.0 · unit m

Domain warp displacement in meters, which bends the noise into swirled shapes; 0 disables warping. Must not be negative.

warp_wavelength_m

number · default 500.0 · unit m

Wavelength of the warp field, in meters. Must be positive.

Every key with its default 
{
    "type": "synthetic",
    "elevation_m": 0.0,
    "stack": [
        {
            "enabled": true,
            "basis": "perlin",
            "fractal": "fbm",
            "blend": "add",
            "seed": 2,
            "wavelength_m": 400.0,
            "amplitude_m": 12.0,
            "octaves": 8,
            "lacunarity": 2.0,
            "gain": 0.5,
            "hurst": null,
            "offset": 1.0,
            "warp_amplitude_m": 0.0,
            "warp_wavelength_m": 500.0
        }
    ],
    "pixel_size_m": null,
    "upsampling": null
}

docs.title: Layers
docs.text:
Relief and features added to the source, applied in order.

Type Description noise A stack of fractal noise layers added to the terrain, for hills, ridges and rolling relief. craters Impact craters generated from a density and age model, or placed by hand, and cut into the terrain. boulders Boulders scattered over the ground from a size distribution, in patches and around fresh craters, as relief or 3D models. roughness Fine roughness from octaves of noise, scaled to a given RMS slope over a baseline. bedforms Fields of wind-blown ripples or dunes added to the terrain. scale Scales and shifts the heights so far, for vertical exaggeration or a datum shift. clamp Clamps the heights so far between optional bounds, to flatten a basin floor or cap peaks. masked Another layer applied only inside a rectangle, circle or polygon, feathered outside it: to confine craters to an area or flatten a landing pad. secondaries Secondary craters around the craters of the last crater layer before this one, after Singer et al. dunes Wind-blown dunes added to the terrain: isolated barchans or domes, or fields of transverse, barchanoid or linear crests, with slip faces and optional ripples on them. sand_fill Sand pooled in the lows of the ground beneath: cracks, troughs and hollows between rises, laying sand over the material map. pavement Fractured bedrock: polygonal plates, each tilted and stepped, parted by cracks or raised ridges, split again by finer octaves of cracks; lays bedrock over the material map. strata Layered rock: the ground beneath terraced into dipping beds, each a flat bench below a cliff, so hills become stepped buttes and mesas; lays bedrock over the cliffs. sand_shadow Sand shadows: a tapering sand tail in the lee of each boulder of the nearest boulder layer before this one; lays sand over the material map. spectral_continuation Detail finer than the source continuing its measured power-law spectrum to shorter wavelengths with random phases, as sparse Gabor noise: an alternative to diamond-square upsampling without lattice artifacts.

docs.title: noise
docs.text:
A stack of fractal noise layers added to the terrain, for hills, ridges and rolling relief.

estimate_from_source

boolean · default false

Takes each layer's unset hurst and amplitude from the source's variogram, continued to the layer's wavelength; for wavelengths at or below the source's cell size. Needs a source with posts.

source_resolves_px

number, optional · default null · unit px

Source cells across from which the source's data already holds the noise layers of the stack, by their wavelength, the longest of each layer's octaves: only smaller ones are added, each raster of a chain giving its own limit. Ignored on synthetic sources and where no raster has data; null adds them all. Must be positive.

stack[]: Noise layers, combined in order: the first enabled layer sets the height and each later one is combined with it by its blend mode. Holds 1 to 8 items. enabled

boolean · default true

Includes this layer in the stack; disabled layers are skipped.

basis

one of perlin, simplex, value, worley_f1, worley_f2, worley_f2_minus_f1, voronoi · default "perlin"

Single-octave noise the fractal is built from.

fractal

one of fbm, ridged, billow, hybrid_multifractal · default "fbm"

How the octaves of the basis noise are combined.

blend

one of add, max, min, mask · default "add"

How this layer combines with the height of the layers before it; the first enabled layer sets the height instead.

seed

integer · default 0

Seed of the noise; changing it gives a different pattern of the same character.

wavelength_m

number · default 1000.0 · unit m

Wavelength of the first, broadest octave, in meters; sets the size of the largest features. Must be positive.

amplitude_m

number, optional · default null · unit m

Largest height of the layer above or below 0, in meters; unset is 0.1 times the wavelength, near the lunar highland median slope at any wavelength.

octaves

integer · default 8

Number of octaves; each one adds detail at a shorter wavelength. Must be from 1 to 32.

lacunarity

number · default 2.0

Frequency ratio between successive octaves. Must be above 1.

gain

number · default 0.5

Weight ratio between successive octaves; higher values give rougher terrain. Unused when the Hurst exponent is set. Must be positive.

hurst

number, optional · default null

Hurst exponent that sets the octave gain to lacunarity^-hurst: near 1 is smooth, lower is rougher at short baselines. Unset uses the gain.

offset

number · default 1.0

Ridge offset of the ridged and hybrid multifractal types. Must be positive.

warp_amplitude_m

number · default 0.0 · unit m

Domain warp displacement in meters, which bends the noise into swirled shapes; 0 disables warping. Must not be negative.

warp_wavelength_m

number · default 500.0 · unit m

Wavelength of the warp field, in meters. Must be positive.

Every key with its default

    "type": "noise",
    "stack": [
        {
            "enabled": true,

docs.title: craters
docs.text:
Impact craters generated from a density and age model, or placed by hand, and cut into the terrain.

morphometry

one of lunar, mars · default "lunar"

Published fits of fresh crater depth, rim height and complex crater shape the craters are shaped with.

generate_random

boolean · default true

Draws random craters from the size distribution; off places only the manual craters.

seed

integer · default 1

Seed the craters are generated with; changing it gives a different crater field of the same statistics.

density

crater densities · default {"type": "minimum", ...}

Size-frequency distribution of the generated craters: how many of each diameter per unit area.

ages

crater ages, optional · default null

How generated craters are given ages, which the degradation model wears them down by; unset gives steady-state ages on the density's production surface and equilibrium.

min_diameter_m

number · default 2.5 · unit m

Smallest crater generated, in meters; lower values add many more small craters. Must be positive.

max_diameter_m

number · default 250.0 · unit m

Largest crater generated, in meters; above the smallest. Must be positive.

max_craters

integer, optional · default null

Most generated craters kept, the largest first; unset keeps all. Manual craters are always kept, and a cap means tiles no longer match the whole grid.

profile

crater profiles · default {"type": "martin_parkes_dunstan", ...}

Shape of a fresh crater's cross-section, scaled to each crater's diameter.

degradation

crater degradation · default {"type": "diffusion", ...}

How craters wear down from their fresh shape with age.

source_resolves_px

number, optional · default 4.0 · unit px

Source cells across from which the source's data already holds the craters (the smaller of this and completeness when both are set), by their diameter: only smaller ones are added, each raster of a chain giving its own limit. Ignored on synthetic sources and where no raster has data; null adds them all. Must be positive.

spacing: Keeps craters of similar size apart by removing conflicting ones, which lowers the density below the model's. diameter_ratio

number · default 1.5

Largest ratio of two craters' diameters for them to count as similar in size and be kept apart. Must be at least 1.

separation

number · default 0.0

Least distance between the centers of similar-size craters, in larger diameters; 0 disables spacing. Must not be negative.

manual[]: Craters placed by hand in the surface's coordinates, added to any generated ones. x

number · default 0.0

Center along x in the surface's coordinates; the longitude in degrees on a sphere.

y

number · default 0.0

Center along y in the surface's coordinates; the latitude in degrees on a sphere.

diameter_m

number · default 0.0 · unit m

Rim-to-rim diameter, in meters. Must be positive.

age_gyr

number · default 0.0 · unit Gyr

Age in Gyr; older craters are more degraded under a degradation model and are applied earlier in oldest-first order. Must not be negative.

id

integer · default 0

Stable ID that seeds the crater's outline; 0 derives one from its position and diameter.

depth_m

number, optional · default null · unit m

Rim-to-floor depth in meters, in place of the one the degradation model and age give; unset keeps the model's. Must be positive.

rim_height_m

number, optional · default null · unit m

Height of the rim crest above the surface the crater formed on, in meters; needs a depth. Unset lowers the fresh rim in proportion to the depth. Must not be negative.

replace

boolean · default false

Replaces whatever the terrain holds there with a sharp crater of this diameter and depth, cut into a plane fitted around it, such as a crater a DEM holds blurred; apply.replacement sets how far. It takes the irregular outline, secondaries and albedo generated craters get.

apply: How craters are cut into the terrain: their order, datum, blending, fading and irregular outlines. order

one of oldest_first, largest_first · default "oldest_first"

Order in which overlapping craters are applied; later craters overprint earlier ones.

fade_px

list of number · default [...] · unit px

How craters too small to resolve fade out, by output samples (pixels) across their diameter: absent up to the first count, whole from the second. Each must not be negative.

fade_shape

one of linear, smoothstep, smootherstep, gaussian · default "smoothstep"

Curve of the fade between the two sample counts of fade_px.

datum

one of none, plane, mean_height, center_height · default "none"

Reference surface each crater's interior is cut relative to, fitted to the ground beneath it; none adds craters onto the terrain everywhere.

datum_fit_radii

number · default 1.0

Radius of the footprint the datum is fitted over, in crater radii. Must be positive.

interior_replacement

number · default 0.0

Share of the interior replaced by datum plus profile: 1 erases older relief inside the crater for a clean cut, 0 keeps it on the floor and walls. Must be from 0 to 1.

blend: Where and how a crater's replaced interior blends into the surrounding terrain. start_radii

number · default 0.8

Distance from the center, in crater radii, up to which the interior is fully replaced. Must not be negative.

end_radii

number · default 1.2

Distance from the center, in crater radii, from which the surrounding terrain is draped unchanged. Must be positive.

shape

one of linear, smoothstep, smootherstep, gaussian · default "smootherstep"

Curve of the transition from the replaced interior to the exterior.

replacement: How manual craters with replace set replace the terrain beneath them, whatever the datum: in full to start_radii, blending out to end_radii, on a plane fitted on a ring beyond. start_radii

number · default 1.0

Distance from the center, in crater radii, up to which a replacing crater replaces the terrain in full. Must be positive.

end_radii

number, optional · default null

Distance from the center, in crater radii, from which nothing is replaced; at most the profile's reach, and unset for that reach, so the replaced crater's rim goes too. Must be positive.

fit_width_radii

number · default 1.0

Width, in crater radii, of the ring outside end_radii that the replacing crater's plane datum is fitted on. Must be positive.

irregularity: Irregular, non-circular crater outlines: which craters have them and how their shapes are drawn. enabled

boolean · default false

Gives eligible craters irregular, non-circular outlines; off keeps every crater round.

seed

integer, optional · default null

Seed the outlines are drawn with, along with each crater's ID; changing it reshapes every irregular crater. Unset follows the layer's seed.

min_diameter_m

number · default 0.0 · unit m

Smallest diameter, in meters, of craters made irregular. Must not be negative.

max_diameter_m

number, optional · default null · unit m

Largest diameter, in meters, of craters made irregular; unset has no upper limit. Must not be negative.

min_age_gyr

number · default 0.0 · unit Gyr

Youngest age, in Gyr, of craters made irregular. Must not be negative.

max_age_gyr

number, optional · default null · unit Gyr

Oldest age, in Gyr, of craters made irregular; unset has no upper limit. Must not be negative.

manual

boolean · default false

Makes manual craters irregular too; otherwise only generated and replacing craters are.

rough_share

number · default 1.0

Share of eligible craters given rough, wavy rims. Must be from 0 to 1.

model

one of power_law, du_2024 · default "power_law"

How rough rims are drawn.

scatter

boolean · default true

With du_2024, scatters each crater's spectrum by the fits' measured misfits and noise.

max_deviation

number · default 0.3

With du_2024, the largest deviation of a rim from a circle, in radii; outlines beyond it are scaled down to it. Must be above 0 and at most 0.5.

min_harmonic

integer · default 2

With power_law, the lowest harmonic of the rim's waviness. Must be from 1 to 64.

max_harmonic

integer · default 12

With power_law, the highest harmonic of the rim's waviness; higher harmonics add finer wiggles. Must be from 1 to 64.

elongated_share

number · default 0.054

Share of eligible craters made elliptical, keeping their area. Must be from 0 to 1.

heading_deg

number, optional · default null · unit deg

Heading of elliptical craters' long axes, in degrees counter-clockwise from +x (local east on a body); unset gives random headings.

heading_spread_deg

number · default 0.0 · unit deg

Largest random turn of a long axis either way from the heading, in degrees. Must not be negative.

marks_share

number · default 0.0

Share of eligible craters given radial marks: ridges and grooves down the wall, strongest where it is steepest. Must be from 0 to 1.

marks_knots

integer · default 45

Random shifts around the crater the marks pass through; more knots give narrower marks. Must be from 3 to 1024.

marks_inner_radii

number · default 0.3

Distance from the center, in crater radii, where the marks reach full strength. Must be above 0 and below 1.

marks_outer_radii

number · default 0.9

Distance from the center, in crater radii, where the marks start to fade; at most 1 minus marks_fade_radii. Must be above 0 and below 1.

marks_fade_radii

number · default 0.1

Width, in crater radii, over which the marks fade in and out. Must be above 0 and at most 0.5.

roughness: With power_law, the RMS deviation of a rough rim from a circle, in crater radii, drawn per crater. kind

one of constant, uniform, normal, log_normal, piecewise · default "constant"

Kind of distribution the value is drawn from.

a

number · default 0.0

The constant value, the uniform's lower bound, the normal's mean or the log-normal's median.

b

number · default 0.0

The uniform's upper bound, or the standard deviation (of the natural logarithm for a log-normal); unused for a constant.

min

number, optional · default null

Lower bound drawn values are clamped to; unset leaves them unbounded below.

max

number, optional · default null

Upper bound drawn values are clamped to; unset leaves them unbounded above, which normal and log-normal kinds do not allow.

edges

list of number · default []

rim_smoothing: Rounded rims: each crater's profile smoothed across distance near its rim; off unless sigma_radii is set. sigma_radii

number · default 0.0

Deviation of the Gaussian the profile is smoothed with across distance, in crater radii; larger values round rims more, and 0 leaves them sharp. Must not be negative.

inner_radii

number · default 0.8

Inner edge of the smoothed band around the rim, in crater radii. Must be from 0 to below 1.

outer_radii

number · default 1.2

Outer edge of the smoothed band around the rim, in crater radii. Must be above 1.

shape

one of linear, smoothstep, smootherstep, gaussian · default "smootherstep"

How the smoothing fades from full at the rim to none at the band's edges.

strength

number · default 1.0

Share of the smoothed height used at the rim; lower values keep more of the sharp crest. Must be from 0 to 1.

noise: Fractal noise over each crater's footprint and around its rim, keyed to the crater; off unless an amplitude is set. amplitude

number · default 0.0

Amplitude of the noise over the whole footprint, as a share of the crater diameter; it fades out beyond the rim to the profile's reach, and 0 adds none. Must not be negative.

wavelength_radii

number · default 0.5

Wavelength of the footprint noise's first octave, in crater radii. Must be positive.

octaves

integer · default 4

Octaves of both noises. Must be from 1 to 12.

gain

number · default 0.5

Weight ratio between successive octaves. Must be positive.

rim_amplitude

number · default 0.0

Amplitude of the extra noise in the band around the rim, as a share of the crater diameter; 0 adds none. Must not be negative.

rim_wavelength_radii

number · default 0.1

Wavelength of the rim noise's first octave, in crater radii. Must be positive.

rim_inner_radii

number · default 0.8

rim_outer_radii

number · default 1.2
