docs.title: Enumerations
docs.text: The named values fields choose between.

docs.title: aging
docs.text: Value Meaning freshness Blocks wear away with the crater's freshness (current over fresh depth): all when fresh, none at or below the minimum freshness. age Blocks wear away with the crater's age as (1 - age / lifetime)^exponent, synthterrain's form.

docs.title: basis
docs.text: Value Meaning perlin Improved Perlin gradient noise: smooth, general-purpose relief. simplex Simplex gradient noise: smooth relief, an alternative to Perlin. value Value noise: random values interpolated over a lattice; blockier than gradient noise. worley_f1 Cellular noise from the distance to the nearest feature point: cones and basins. worley_f2 Cellular noise from the distance to the second-nearest feature point. worley_f2_minus_f1 Cellular noise F2 - F1: ridges along cell borders, like cracked ground. voronoi Voronoi cells, each at one random height: flat polygonal plateaus and terraces.

docs.title: blend
docs.text: Value Meaning add Adds the layer to the height so far. max Keeps the higher of the height so far and the layer. min Keeps the lower of the height so far and the layer. mask Multiplies the height so far by (layer / amplitude + 1) / 2, so the layer modulates roughness by region.

docs.title: chronology
docs.text: Value Meaning neukum Neukum et al. (2001) lunar chronology, for surfaces 0 to 4.6 Gyr old. ivanov Ivanov (2001) Martian chronology, for surfaces 0 to 4.6 Gyr old.

docs.title: compression
docs.text: Value Meaning none Uncompressed: the largest files. lzw Lossless LZW compression, widely supported. deflate Lossless Deflate (zlib) compression. packbits PackBits run-length compression; read only, so outputs cannot use it.

docs.title: curve
docs.text: Value Meaning minimum The model's minimum curve: the fewest boulders. nominal The model's nominal curve. maximum The model's maximum curve: the most boulders.

docs.title: datum
docs.text: Value Meaning none No datum: the crater profile is added onto the terrain everywhere. plane Interior cut relative to a least-squares plane over the fit footprint, keeping regional slopes. mean_height Interior cut relative to a flat datum at the mean height over the fit footprint. center_height Interior cut relative to a flat datum at the terrain height under the crater center.

docs.title: diffusivity
docs.text: Value Meaning matched With steady-state ages, the diffusivity that wears each crater to Fassett et al.'s (2022) visibility cutoff, depth 0.04 of the diameter, at the end of its equilibrium lifetime, as they derive it, for the layer's own profile; fassett_2022_hartmann for other ages. fassett_2022_hartmann Lunar size-dependent diffusivity of Fassett et al. (2022) for the Hartmann equilibrium, 3.6 D^0.87 m^2/Myr with D in km. fassett_2022_trask Lunar size-dependent diffusivity of Fassett et al. (2022) for the Trask equilibrium, 3.1 D^1.05 m^2/Myr with D in km. fassett_thomson_2014 Lunar diffusivity of Fassett and Thomson (2014), 5.5 m^2/Myr for every crater size; it erases craters below a few hundred meters within a small share of their lifetimes. fassett_thomson_2014_calibration Fassett and Thomson's (2014) lunar diffusion age against crater age, independent of size; suits kilometer-scale craters. power_law A diffusivity of your own, coefficient (D / 1 km)^exponent m^2/Myr, from the power_law settings.

docs.title: equilibrium
docs.text: Value Meaning trask Trask (1966) lunar equilibrium, N(>=D) = 10^-1.1 D^-2, as the DSNE uses. hartmann Hartmann (1984) lunar equilibrium, N(>=D) = 10^-1.14 D^-1.83 per km^2 with D in km.

docs.title: fade_shape
docs.text: Value Meaning linear Straight ramp: continuous, with kinks at both ends. smoothstep Cubic 3t^2 - 2t^3: continuous slope across the transition. smootherstep Quintic 6t^5 - 15t^4 + 10t^3: continuous slope and curvature, the smoothest join. gaussian Gaussian falloff with sigma a third of the band, rescaled to end at zero.

docs.title: format
docs.text: Value Meaning csv Comma-separated values, one row per item. json A JSON document.

docs.title: fractal
docs.text: Value Meaning fbm Fractional Brownian motion: a weighted sum of octaves, the general-purpose choice. ridged Ridged multifractal: sharp crests from inverted absolute noise, like eroded ridges. billow Sum of absolute-value octaves: rounded, puffy forms. hybrid_multifractal Hybrid multifractal: smooth lowlands and rough highlands.

docs.title: interp
docs.text: Value Meaning bilinear Square nodes the mean of their four corners, diamond nodes the mean of their four neighbors, samples bilinear between nodes. catmull_rom Catmull-Rom splines over four nodes along each axis, as the VIPER terrain expansion does: smoother, with fewer lattice creases.

docs.title: kind
docs.text: Value Meaning constant Always a. uniform Uniform between a and b. normal Normal with mean a and standard deviation b. log_normal Log-normal with median a and standard deviation b of the natural logarithm. piecewise Uniform within each bin between edges, each bin drawn in proportion to its weight.

docs.title: measure
docs.text: Value Meaning scale The local density over the layer's own; 1 keeps it as the size distribution gives it. count Features with diameters in the map's range per area unit, such as boulders per km^2. areal_fraction Share of the ground covered by features in the map's range, such as rock abundance.

docs.title: measure
docs.text: Value Meaning exponent The cumulative exponent alpha, counts falling as D^-alpha. mean_diameter The mean diameter in meters of the features from the reference diameter up, from which alpha = mean / (mean - D0).

docs.title: method
docs.text: Value Meaning nearest The value of the nearest cell center: blocky, but never mixes values. bilinear Linear in each axis over the four surrounding cells. cubic Keys cubic convolution (a = -0.5) over the sixteen surrounding cells: smooth, for upscaling DEMs. catmull_rom Another name for cubic: the Catmull-Rom spline is the same kernel. lanczos3 The three-lobe Lanczos kernel over the 36 surrounding cells: sharper than cubic, with slight ringing at steps. cubic_bspline The cubic B-spline over the sixteen surrounding cells: the smoothest, but it smooths the cells themselves.

docs.title: mode
docs.text: Value Meaning none Each cell takes the first source with data, unchanged: a step where a gap begins. feather Adds the height difference at the nearest edge post to the later source, fading it to 0 across width_m of the gap: the cheapest, without a solve. height Shifts the later source by the edge's height difference spread smoothly into the gap, fading out over decay_length_m beyond an open edge: heights meet (C0), keeping the later source's relief. slope As height, with a biharmonic spread that matches slopes at the edge as well (C1).

docs.title: model
docs.text: Value Meaning power_law Rim harmonics with amplitudes falling as a power of the harmonic number, of a given RMS: a simple, configurable spectrum. du_2024 The fitted rim-crest spectra of fresh lunar craters of Du et al. (2024), from each crater's diameter.

docs.title: model
docs.text: Value Meaning intercrater 0.0001 D^-1.75457 per m^2 with D in meters: synthetic_moon's "low blockiness". haworth 0.002 D^-2.6607 per m^2 with D in meters: synthetic_moon's "high blockiness". viper_specification 0.0003 D^-2.482 per m^2 with D in meters: the VIPER Environmental Specification.

docs.title: model
docs.text: Value Meaning nearest One center per cell of a jittered lattice, each point weighted by its nearest center only. thomas A Thomas cluster process: Poisson-scattered centers whose Gaussian clusters add where they overlap.

docs.title: morphometry
docs.text: Value Meaning lunar Fresh lunar craters: Fassett et al. (2022) depth and rim height below 15 km, Pike's (1977) complex crater fits above. mars Fresh Martian craters: depth and rim height capped for small craters, Garvin et al.'s (2003) fits for large and complex craters from 7 km.

docs.title: order
docs.text: Value Meaning oldest_first Oldest craters first, then larger first: the physical order, so younger craters overprint older ones. largest_first Largest craters first, then older first, so smaller craters overprint larger ones.

docs.title: production
docs.text: Value Meaning neukum Neukum et al. (2001) lunar production function, valid from 10 m to 300 km. extended_neukum The Neukum production function continued below 10 m as a power law of slope -2.85, valid from 2.5 m to 300 km. ivanov Ivanov (2001) Martian production function, valid from 15 m to 362 km.

docs.title: profile
docs.text: Value Meaning smoothstep Every block inside the rim, falling along a smoothstep to none at the reach. exponential Exponential decay outside the rim, a fixed share on the floor and none beyond the reach: synthterrain's crater probability map.

docs.title: reference
docs.text: Value Meaning none No parameters: each class present must be given. mars_pancam Pancam fits at 753 nm (Johnson et al. 2006a, b, tabulated by Fernando et al. 2013): soil, sand, dust, bedrock (Eagle crater outcrop, Johnson et al. 2006b) and rock.

docs.title: relief
docs.text: Value Meaning dome Each boulder's exposed part drawn as a dome: cheap, and enough for small boulders. shape The top surface of each boulder's 3D boulder shape drawn into the heights. none No rock relief in the heights, only fillets when set, for programs that place every boulder as a model of its own.

docs.title: rest
docs.text: Value Meaning face On its broadest face: its short axis up. side On a side: its intermediate axis up. end On an end: its long axis up.

docs.title: rim
docs.text: Value Meaning original The published fits, whose interior and exterior meet at 0.98 radii. at_one_radius Interior fit extended to 1.0 radii so the rim lies at the stated diameter, as synthterrain's FT_Crater; leaves a small step at the rim. plateau A flat rim at the fresh rim height from 0.98 to 1.02 radii, after Fassett et al. (2022), as synthterrain's FTmod_Crater.

docs.title: shape
docs.text: Value Meaning barchan Isolated crescents with a slip face and horns downwind; domes below min_width_m. dome Isolated rounded heaps without a slip face. transverse Continuous crests across the wind, each with a slip face. barchanoid Transverse crests bent into linked crescents, as where sand supply rises. linear Symmetric crests along the wind, as under two winds on scarce sand.

docs.title: solid
docs.text: Value Meaning icosahedron Boulders start from an icosahedron, twenty triangles on the unit sphere: rounder shapes. cube Boulders start from a cube: blocky shapes. pyramid Boulders start from a square-based pyramid. prism Boulders start from a triangular prism, a wedge. tetrahedron Boulders start from a regular tetrahedron: angular shapes.

docs.title: terrain
docs.text: Value Meaning rough_mare Moore's rough mare crater distribution: 10^-1 D^-2 per m^2 below 100 m, 10 D^-3 above. smooth_mare Moore's smooth mare crater distribution: 10^-1 D^-2 per m^2 below 40 m, then D^-3, D^-1.68 from 100 m and D^-3 from 200 m. uplands Moore's uplands crater distribution: 10^-1 D^-2 per m^2 below 1 km, 10^2 D^-3 above. heavily_cratered Moore's heavily cratered distribution: 10^-1 D^-2 per m^2 up to 10 km.

The structure of a configuration as JSON, from the same field lists the parser reads: each object's fields with their descriptions, units, defaults and ranges, and each choice's alternatives. terraingen.config_schema() and terraingen schema give it too.

  • schema.json: this document.
  • catalog.json: every type with its defaults, as terraingen.config_catalog() gives it.
schema.json 
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "root": {
    "kind": "object",
    "fields": [
      {
        "name": "schema_version",
        "description": "Version of the configuration format, which this library reads. Required.",
        "unit": "",
        "schema": {
          "kind": "integer",
          "fixed": true
        },
        "default": 1,
        "required": true
      },
      {
        "name": "body",
        "description": "What the terrain lies on: a plane in meters, or a whole body (a sphere, ellipsoid or shape model) in longitude and latitude degrees.",
        "unit": "",
        "schema": {
          "kind": "ref",
          "ref": "d0"
        },
        "default": {
          "type": "plane"
        }
      },
      {
        "name": "source",
        "description": "Where the heights come from: a GeoTIFF, a chain of sources or synthetic noise, with its upsampling; unset is fBm noise 400 m in wavelength and 12 m in amplitude at the datum.",
        "unit": "",
        "schema": {
          "kind": "optional",
          "of": {
            "kind": "ref",
            "ref": "d1"
          },
          "default": {
            "type": "raster",
            "path": "",
            "band": 0,
            "scale": null,
            "offset_m": null,
            "crop": null,
            "effective_pixel_size_m": null,
            "upsampling": "cubic"
          }
        },
        "default": null
      },
      {
        "name": "layers",
        "description": "Relief and features added to the source's heights, applied in order: noise, craters, boulders and more.",
        "unit": "",
        "schema": {
          "kind": "array",
          "of": {
            "kind": "ref",
            "ref": "d6"
          },
          "default": {
            "type": "noise",
            "stack": [
              {
                "enabled": true,
                "basis": "perlin",
                "fractal": "fbm",
                "blend": "add",
                "seed": 0,
                "wavelength_m": 1000.0,
                "amplitude_m": null,
                "octaves": 8,
                "lacunarity": 2.0,
                "gain": 0.5,
                "hurst": null,
                "offset": 1.0,
                "warp_amplitude_m": 0.0,
                "warp_wavelength_m": 500.0
              }
            ],
            "estimate_from_source": false,
            "source_resolves_px": null
          }
        },
        "default": []
      },
      {
        "name": "outputs",
        "description": "What to produce, at what resolution and where, each over its own extent or the whole body: heightmaps, crater and boulder lists, boulder models, albedo, meshes and reports. Each is returned, and written to its path when it has one.",
        "unit": "",
        "schema": {
          "kind": "array",
          "of": {
            "kind": "ref",
            "ref": "d52"
          },
          "default": {
            "type": "heightmap",
            "path": "",
            "pixel_size_m": null,
            "extent_m": null,
            "extent_deg": null,
            "compression": "lzw",
            "tile_size_px": 256
          }
        },
        "default": []
      },
      {
        "name": "albedo",
        "description": "The terrain's albedo: a source and the layers that change it, written by albedo outputs; none when unset.",
        "unit": "",
        "schema": {
          "kind": "optional",
          "of": {
            "kind": "ref",
            "ref": "d54"
          },
          "default": {
            "source": {
              "type": "synthetic",
              "rgb": false,
              "hue_deg": 0.0,
              "saturation": 0.0,
              "value": 0.11,
              "hue_noise_deg": [],
              "saturation_noise": [],
              "value_noise": []
            },
            "layers": []
          }
        },
        "default": null
      },
      {
        "name": "materials",
        "description": "The material map: soil, sand, dust, bedrock and rock shares, and their Hapke parameters, written by materials and photometry outputs; none when unset.",
        "unit": "",
        "schema": {
          "kind": "optional",
          "of": {
            "kind": "ref",
            "ref": "d68"
          },
          "default": {
            "exposure": {
              "reach_m": 12.0,
              "rise_soil": 0.01,
              "rise_boulder": 0.035,
              "slope_soil": 0.2,
              "slope_boulder": 0.4,
              "floor_cover": 0.0,
              "floor_patch_m": 60.0,
              "seed": 0
            },
            "dust_cover": 0.0,
            "dust_patch_m": 50.0,
            "seed": 0,
            "photometry": {
              "reference": "none",
              "soil": null,
              "sand": null,
              "dust": null,
              "bedrock": null,
              "rock": null
            }
          }
        },
        "default": null
      }
    ]
  },
  "definitions": {
    "d0": {
      "kind": "choice",
      "alternatives": [
        {
          "type": "plane",
          "description": "A flat projected frame in meters, for local sites.",
          "fields": [],
          "default": {
            "type": "plane"
          }
        },
        {
          "type": "sphere",
          "description": "A whole body such as a planet or moon: positions in longitude and latitude (degrees) and features generated over the whole body.",
          "fields": [
            {
              "name": "radius_m",
              "description": "Radius of the body's datum sphere, in meters. Must be positive. Required.",
              "unit": "m",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "number"
              },
              "default": 0.0,
              "minimum": 0.0,
              "exclusive_minimum": true,
              "required": true
            }
          ],
          "default": {
            "type": "sphere",
            "radius_m": 0.0
          }
        },
        {
          "type": "ellipsoid",
          "description": "A whole body shaped as a triaxial ellipsoid, such as an elongated moon or asteroid: planetocentric longitude and latitude (degrees), heights along the direction from the center, and features generated over the whole body.",
          "fields": [
            {
              "name": "radii_m",
              "description": "Semi-axes a, b and c of the datum ellipsoid in meters, along x (longitude 0), y (longitude 90) and z (the north pole). Holds exactly 3 items. Each must be positive. Required.",
              "unit": "m",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "array",
                "of": {
                  "kind": "number"
                },
                "default": 0.0
              },
              "default": [],
              "minimum": 0.0,
              "exclusive_minimum": true,
              "min_length": 3,
              "max_length": 3,
              "required": true
            }
          ],
          "default": {
            "type": "ellipsoid",
            "radii_m": []
          }
        },
        {
          "type": "shape_model",
          "description": "A whole star-shaped body such as an asteroid from a shape model, resampled along rays from its origin; heights are radial, in longitude and latitude degrees.",
          "fields": [
            {
              "name": "path",
              "description": "Shape model in body-fixed coordinates around its origin: a Gaskell ICQ model (.icq) or a closed mesh (.obj, .gltf, .glb or .stl); relative paths resolve against the configuration's folder. Required.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "string"
              },
              "default": "",
              "required": true
            },
            {
              "name": "q",
              "description": "Intervals per cube face edge of the radial grid the model is resampled on; unset keeps an ICQ model's own Q and uses 256 for a mesh. Must be from 1 to 4096.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "optional",
                "of": {
                  "kind": "integer",
                  "minimum": 0
                },
                "default": 0
              },
              "default": null,
              "minimum": 1.0,
              "exclusive_minimum": false,
              "maximum": 4096.0,
              "exclusive_maximum": false
            },
            {
              "name": "meters_per_unit",
              "description": "Meters per unit of the file's coordinates; unset is 1000 for an ICQ model, whose coordinates are kilometers, and 1 for a mesh. Must be positive.",
              "unit": "m/unit",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "optional",
                "of": {
                  "kind": "number"
                },
                "default": 0.0
              },
              "default": null,
              "minimum": 0.0,
              "exclusive_minimum": true
            }
          ],
          "default": {
            "type": "shape_model",
            "path": "",
            "q": null,
            "meters_per_unit": null
          }
        }
      ]
    },
    "d2": {
      "kind": "object",
      "fields": [
        {
          "name": "min_x",
          "description": "Lower edge along x.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.0
        },
        {
          "name": "min_y",
          "description": "Lower edge along y.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.0
        },
        {
          "name": "max_x",
          "description": "Upper edge along x; above min_x.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.0
        },
        {
          "name": "max_y",
          "description": "Upper edge along y; above min_y.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.0
        }
      ]
    },
    "d3": {
      "kind": "choice",
      "alternatives": [
        {
          "type": "nearest",
          "description": "The value of the nearest cell center: blocky, but never mixes values.",
          "fields": [],
          "default": "nearest"
        },
        {
          "type": "bilinear",
          "description": "Linear in each axis over the four surrounding cells.",
          "fields": [],
          "default": "bilinear"
        },
        {
          "type": "cubic",
          "description": "Keys cubic convolution (a = -0.5) over the sixteen surrounding cells: smooth, for upscaling DEMs.",
          "fields": [],
          "default": "cubic"
        },
        {
          "type": "catmull_rom",
          "description": "Another name for cubic: the Catmull-Rom spline is the same kernel.",
          "fields": [],
          "default": "catmull_rom"
        },
        {
          "type": "lanczos3",
          "description": "The three-lobe Lanczos kernel over the 36 surrounding cells: sharper than cubic, with slight ringing at steps.",
          "fields": [],
          "default": "lanczos3"
        },
        {
          "type": "cubic_bspline",
          "description": "The cubic B-spline over the sixteen surrounding cells: the smoothest, but it smooths the cells themselves.",
          "fields": [],
          "default": "cubic_bspline"
        },
        {
          "type": "diamond_square",
          "description": "Random midpoint displacement: each level halves the node spacing down to the sample spacing, adding fractal detail without changing the posts.",
          "fields": [
            {
              "name": "fractal_dimension",
              "description": "Fractal dimension, 2 smooth and 3 rough: each square or diamond step scales the displacement by 2^-((3 - F) / 2). Unset estimates it from the median height differences of the posts at lags of 1 to 8 posts. Must be from 2 to 3.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "optional",
                "of": {
                  "kind": "number"
                },
                "default": 0.0
              },
              "default": null,
              "minimum": 2.0,
              "exclusive_minimum": false,
              "maximum": 3.0,
              "exclusive_maximum": false
            },
            {
              "name": "scale_m",
              "description": "Displacement standard deviation in meters at the posts' last step; unset estimates it per fit_window_px window. Must not be negative.",
              "unit": "m",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "optional",
                "of": {
                  "kind": "number"
                },
                "default": 0.0
              },
              "default": null,
              "minimum": 0.0,
              "exclusive_minimum": false
            },
            {
              "name": "fit_window_px",
              "description": "Side in posts of the overlapping windows, centered every half side, that an unset scale_m is fitted over; each node's scale is bilinear between the windows around it. 0 fits one scale to a sample of the posts; else at least 4. Must be from 0 to 1024 px.",
              "unit": "px",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "integer",
                "minimum": 0
              },
              "default": 32,
              "minimum": 0.0,
              "exclusive_minimum": false,
              "maximum": 1024.0,
              "exclusive_maximum": false
            },
            {
              "name": "interp",
              "description": "How new nodes are filled from the coarser ones and samples read between the finest nodes.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "enum",
                "choices": [
                  "bilinear",
                  "catmull_rom"
                ],
                "descriptions": [
                  "Square nodes the mean of their four corners, diamond nodes the mean of their four neighbors, samples bilinear between nodes.",
                  "Catmull-Rom splines over four nodes along each axis, as the VIPER terrain expansion does: smoother, with fewer lattice creases."
                ]
              },
              "default": "bilinear"
            },
            {
              "name": "min_pixel_size_m",
              "description": "Finest node spacing in meters the posts are refined to; 0 refines down to the sample spacing. Must not be negative.",
              "unit": "m",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "number"
              },
              "default": 0.0,
              "minimum": 0.0,
              "exclusive_minimum": false
            },
            {
              "name": "seed",
              "description": "Seed of the displacements.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "integer",
                "minimum": 0
              },
              "default": 1
            }
          ],
          "default": {
            "type": "diamond_square",
            "fractal_dimension": null,
            "scale_m": null,
            "fit_window_px": 32,
            "interp": "bilinear",
            "min_pixel_size_m": 0.0,
            "seed": 1
          }
        }
      ],
      "named": true
    },
    "d4": {
      "kind": "object",
      "fields": [
        {
          "name": "mode",
          "description": "How each source meets the gaps of those before it: none switches outright, feather fades the edge's height difference out across the gap, height shifts the later source to meet the earlier one's heights (C0) and slope to meet its heights and slopes (C1). The match is solved on the posts of the source before each gap.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "enum",
            "choices": [
              "none",
              "feather",
              "height",
              "slope"
            ],
            "descriptions": [
              "Each cell takes the first source with data, unchanged: a step where a gap begins.",
              "Adds the height difference at the nearest edge post to the later source, fading it to 0 across width_m of the gap: the cheapest, without a solve.",
              "Shifts the later source by the edge's height difference spread smoothly into the gap, fading out over decay_length_m beyond an open edge: heights meet (C0), keeping the later source's relief.",
              "As height, with a biharmonic spread that matches slopes at the edge as well (C1)."
            ]
          },
          "default": "none"
        },
        {
          "name": "width_m",
          "description": "Width in meters of the band inside a gap over which feather fades the height difference at the edge to 0. Must be positive.",
          "unit": "m",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 50.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        },
        {
          "name": "decay_length_m",
          "description": "Length in meters over which height and slope fade the shift out where a gap is open, beyond a source's edge; it is 0 from three decay lengths on. A hole much narrower than it takes the whole shift. Must be positive.",
          "unit": "m",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 50.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        }
      ]
    },
    "d5": {
      "kind": "object",
      "fields": [
        {
          "name": "enabled",
          "description": "Includes this layer in the stack; disabled layers are skipped.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "boolean"
          },
          "default": true
        },
        {
          "name": "basis",
          "description": "Single-octave noise the fractal is built from.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "enum",
            "choices": [
              "perlin",
              "simplex",
              "value",
              "worley_f1",
              "worley_f2",
              "worley_f2_minus_f1",
              "voronoi"
            ],
            "descriptions": [
              "Improved Perlin gradient noise: smooth, general-purpose relief.",
              "Simplex gradient noise: smooth relief, an alternative to Perlin.",
              "Value noise: random values interpolated over a lattice; blockier than gradient noise.",
              "Cellular noise from the distance to the nearest feature point: cones and basins.",
              "Cellular noise from the distance to the second-nearest feature point.",
              "Cellular noise F2 - F1: ridges along cell borders, like cracked ground.",
              "Voronoi cells, each at one random height: flat polygonal plateaus and terraces."
            ]
          },
          "default": "perlin"
        },
        {
          "name": "fractal",
          "description": "How the octaves of the basis noise are combined.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "enum",
            "choices": [
              "fbm",
              "ridged",
              "billow",
              "hybrid_multifractal"
            ],
            "descriptions": [
              "Fractional Brownian motion: a weighted sum of octaves, the general-purpose choice.",
              "Ridged multifractal: sharp crests from inverted absolute noise, like eroded ridges.",
              "Sum of absolute-value octaves: rounded, puffy forms.",
              "Hybrid multifractal: smooth lowlands and rough highlands."
            ]
          },
          "default": "fbm"
        },
        {
          "name": "blend",
          "description": "How this layer combines with the height of the layers before it; the first enabled layer sets the height instead.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "enum",
            "choices": [
              "add",
              "max",
              "min",
              "mask"
            ],
            "descriptions": [
              "Adds the layer to the height so far.",
              "Keeps the higher of the height so far and the layer.",
              "Keeps the lower of the height so far and the layer.",
              "Multiplies the height so far by (layer / amplitude + 1) / 2, so the layer modulates roughness by region."
            ]
          },
          "default": "add"
        },
        {
          "name": "seed",
          "description": "Seed of the noise; changing it gives a different pattern of the same character.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "integer",
            "minimum": 0
          },
          "default": 0
        },
        {
          "name": "wavelength_m",
          "description": "Wavelength of the first, broadest octave, in meters; sets the size of the largest features. Must be positive.",
          "unit": "m",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 1000.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        },
        {
          "name": "amplitude_m",
          "description": "Largest height of the layer above or below 0, in meters; unset is 0.1 times the wavelength, near the lunar highland median slope at any wavelength.",
          "unit": "m",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "optional",
            "of": {
              "kind": "number"
            },
            "default": 0.0
          },
          "default": null
        },
        {
          "name": "octaves",
          "description": "Number of octaves; each one adds detail at a shorter wavelength. Must be from 1 to 32.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "integer"
          },
          "default": 8,
          "minimum": 1.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false,
          "maximum": 32.0,
          "exclusive_maximum": false
        },
        {
          "name": "lacunarity",
          "description": "Frequency ratio between successive octaves. Must be above 1.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 2.0,
          "minimum": 1.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        },
        {
          "name": "gain",
          "description": "Weight ratio between successive octaves; higher values give rougher terrain. Unused when the Hurst exponent is set. Must be positive.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.5,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        },
        {
          "name": "hurst",
          "description": "Hurst exponent that sets the octave gain to lacunarity^-hurst: near 1 is smooth, lower is rougher at short baselines. Unset uses the gain.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "optional",
            "of": {
              "kind": "number"
            },
            "default": 0.0
          },
          "default": null
        },
        {
          "name": "offset",
          "description": "Ridge offset of the ridged and hybrid multifractal types. Must be positive.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 1.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        },
        {
          "name": "warp_amplitude_m",
          "description": "Domain warp displacement in meters, which bends the noise into swirled shapes; 0 disables warping. Must not be negative.",
          "unit": "m",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false
        },
        {
          "name": "warp_wavelength_m",
          "description": "Wavelength of the warp field, in meters. Must be positive.",
          "unit": "m",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 500.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        }
      ]
    },
    "d1": {
      "kind": "choice",
      "alternatives": [
        {
          "type": "raster",
          "description": "A heightmap read from a GeoTIFF in its own projected coordinates, its cells upsampled to finer spacings, to add relief to a real DEM.",
          "fields": [
            {
              "name": "path",
              "description": "GeoTIFF to read the heights from; relative paths resolve against the configuration's folder. Required.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "string"
              },
              "default": "",
              "required": true
            },
            {
              "name": "band",
              "description": "Band of the file to read, counting from 0.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "integer",
                "minimum": 0
              },
              "default": 0
            },
            {
              "name": "scale",
              "description": "Factor each sample is multiplied by, replacing the band's scale from the file's GDAL metadata. Unset keeps the file's.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "optional",
                "of": {
                  "kind": "number"
                },
                "default": 0.0
              },
              "default": null
            },
            {
              "name": "offset_m",
              "description": "Added to each scaled sample, replacing the band's offset from the file's GDAL metadata. Unset keeps the file's.",
              "unit": "m",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "optional",
                "of": {
                  "kind": "number"
                },
                "default": 0.0
              },
              "default": null
            },
            {
              "name": "crop",
              "description": "Box in the raster's CRS units to use; unset uses the whole file.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "optional",
                "of": {
                  "kind": "ref",
                  "ref": "d2"
                },
                "default": {
                  "min_x": 0.0,
                  "min_y": 0.0,
                  "max_x": 0.0,
                  "max_y": 0.0
                }
              },
              "default": null
            },
            {
              "name": "effective_pixel_size_m",
              "description": "Cell size in meters the heights truly resolve, for a DEM that was upsampled or smoothed before it was saved; it replaces the cell size as the scale below which the source resolves no features. Unset uses the cell size. Must be positive.",
              "unit": "m",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "optional",
                "of": {
                  "kind": "number"
                },
                "default": 0.0
              },
              "default": null,
              "minimum": 0.0,
              "exclusive_minimum": true
            },
            {
              "name": "upsampling",
              "description": "How the posts are refined between them and at finer spacings: a kernel name such as cubic or lanczos3, or an object with a \"type\" and its settings, such as {\"type\": \"diamond_square\"} for fractal detail.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "ref",
                "ref": "d3"
              },
              "default": "cubic"
            }
          ],
          "default": {
            "type": "raster",
            "path": "",
            "band": 0,
            "scale": null,
            "offset_m": null,

            "kind": "enum",

              "perlin",

            ],

              "Cellular noise from the distance to the second-nearest feature point.",

          "name": "fractal",

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Rocks. Boulders brighten the albedo, on a 40 m square of SP-8023 maximum boulders. The left three, at 0.1 m, make rock 1.5, 2.5 (the default) and 4 times as bright as the regolith. The right two show the same square at 1 m, where most boulders are too small to resolve, without and with their unresolved cover drawn as a speckle of the right mean and variance.

Code

Slopes. Steep slopes stay fresh. Downslope creep keeps exposing immature soil, so slopes past an onset grow brighter by their optical maturity (Ikeda et al. 2022). On 400 m of hills with a fresh 90 m crater, the panels show the slopes, then the albedo with the onset at 10, 20 (the default) and 30 degrees.

Code

Splotches. Surface splotches, the small dark and bright patches Speyerer et al. (2016) found forming between LROC images, on 100 m squares. From left to right the panels show the measured mix (nine in ten dark), half of them bright, sharp round edges, and soft ragged ones.

Code

Synthetic base. The synthetic albedo base on 400 m squares is a mature mare value of 0.11 at 750 nm, multiplied by 1 plus fractal value noise, here 150 m noise with amplitudes of 0, 0.2 and 0.5, then finer 30 m noise of 0.5, and last as three bands, tinted a warm hue with noise in hue and saturation too. The gray panels share one scale.

Code

docs.title: Impacts and landers
docs.text:
Blast zones. Lander blast zones, where rocket exhaust scoured and brightened the soil (Clegg et al. 2014), on 400 m squares. From left to right the panels show an Apollo-sized zone, a smaller, more elongated one like Chang'e-3's, the Apollo zone with a dark core where the exhaust dug in, and profiles west to east through each.

Code

Crater rays. A 400 m crater's bright interior, ejecta and rays on a 3 km square, in optical maturity. The top row shows the crater fresh, then 1, 3 and 6 Myr old, its rays fading over their retention time and its ejecta after them. The bottom row, all fresh, shows smooth rays, fully patchy rays, and ejecta broken into radial streaks and into lobes.

Code

Oblique impacts. Rays of a fresh 400 m crater struck from the west, on a 3 km square. The first panel shows radial rays from a vertical impact. The others show the patterns of ever lower impact angles, with rays reaching farther downrange, a forbidden zone uprange with no rays, and a butterfly of rays to either side. The angle thresholds are set here so this one crater falls in each regime.

Code

Reflectance zones. Reflectance zones around a new 20 m crater, as LROC before-and-after images show them (Robinson et al. 2015, Speyerer et al. 2016). They are a bright proximal zone, a dark one beyond it, and faint, finger-like distal zones, bright and dark, reaching 2 km out. On a 4.4 km square of hills, the left panel shows the zones alone. The middle one adds shadows, where low-angle jets miss the ground behind rises. The right one shows profiles west to east.

Code

docs.title: Blast zones
docs.text:
Lander blast zones, where rocket exhaust scoured and brightened the soil (Clegg et al. 2014), on 400 m squares. From left to right the panels show an Apollo-sized zone, a smaller, more elongated one like Chang'e-3's, the Apollo zone with a dark core where the exhaust dug in, and profiles west to east through each.

Made by docs/gallery/albedo/blast_zones.py; back to the figure in Albedo.

# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause

"""Lander blast zones, where rocket exhaust scoured and brightened the soil (Clegg et al. 2014), on
400 m squares. From left to right the panels show an Apollo-sized zone, a smaller, more elongated one
like Chang'e-3's, the Apollo zone with a dark core where the exhaust dug in, and profiles west to east
through each."""

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

import terraingen

WIDE = True
SECTION = "Impacts and landers"

SIZE_M = 400.0

    ("Apollo", terraingen.BlastZone(seed=1)),

A 400 m crater's bright interior, ejecta and rays on a 3 km square, in optical maturity. The top row shows the crater fresh, then 1, 3 and 6 Myr old, its rays fading over their retention time and its ejecta after them. The bottom row, all fresh, shows smooth rays, fully patchy rays, and ejecta broken into radial streaks and into lobes.

Made by docs/gallery/albedo/crater_rays.py; back to the figure in Albedo.

# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause

"""A 400 m crater's bright interior, ejecta and rays on a 3 km square, in optical maturity. The top row
shows the crater fresh, then 1, 3 and 6 Myr old, its rays fading over their retention time and its
ejecta after them. The bottom row, all fresh, shows smooth rays, fully patchy rays, and ejecta broken
into radial streaks and into lobes."""

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import terraingen

WIDE = True
SECTION = "Impacts and landers"

SIZE_M = 3000.0
DIAMETER = 400.0


def figure(quick=False):
    pixel = 20.0 if quick else 5.0
    size = int(SIZE_M / pixel) + 1
    terrain = terraingen.Terrain(source=terraingen.FlatSource(size, size, pixel))
    grid = terrain.evaluate().grid
    base = terraingen.SyntheticAlbedo(value=0.11)

    def options(patchiness=None, streaks=0.0, lobes=0.0):
        settings = terraingen.CraterAlbedoOptions(seed=2)
        rays = settings.rays
        rays.oblique.enabled = False
        oblique = rays.oblique
        oblique.enabled = False
        rays.oblique = oblique
        if patchiness is not None:
            rays.patchiness = patchiness
        settings.rays = rays
        texture = settings.texture
        texture.streaks = streaks
        texture.lobes = lobes
        settings.texture = texture
        return settings

    panels = [
        (f"{age * 1000:g} Myr old" if age else "Fresh", age, options()) for age in (0.0, 0.001, 0.003, 0.006)
    ]
    panels += [
        ("Smooth rays", 0.0, options(patchiness=0.0)),
        ("Patchy rays", 0.0, options(patchiness=1.0)),
        ("Streaked ejecta", 0.0, options(streaks=0.6)),
        ("Lobed ejecta", 0.0, options(lobes=0.6)),
    ]

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 4, figsize=(15, 8.2), layout="constrained")
    for ax, (title, age, settings) in zip(axes.flat, panels, strict=True):
        crater = terraingen.CraterLayer.manual([terraingen.Crater(0.0, 0.0, DIAMETER, age_gyr=age)])
        albedo = terraingen.Albedo(base, [terraingen.CraterAlbedo(crater, settings)])
        values = terraingen.evaluate_albedo(albedo, grid)[0].values
        image = ax.imshow(values, cmap="gray", vmin=0.1, vmax=0.15)
        ax.set_axis_off()
        ax.set_title(title)
    fig.colorbar(image, ax=axes, label="Albedo", shrink=0.85)
    return fig

Rays of a fresh 400 m crater struck from the west, on a 3 km square. The first panel shows radial rays from a vertical impact. The others show the patterns of ever lower impact angles, with rays reaching farther downrange, a forbidden zone uprange with no rays, and a butterfly of rays to either side. # SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause

"""Rays of a fresh 400 m crater struck from the west, on a 3 km square. The first panel shows radial
rays from a vertical impact. The others show the patterns of ever lower impact angles, with rays
reaching farther downrange, a forbidden zone uprange with no rays, and a butterfly of rays to either
side. The angle thresholds are set here so this one crater falls in each regime."""

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import terraingen

WIDE = True
SECTION = "Impacts and landers"

SIZE_M = 3000.0
DIAMETER = 400.0
PANELS = [
    ("Radial", None),
    ("Asymmetric", (90.0, 1.0, 0.5)),
    ("Forbidden zone", (90.0, 89.5, 0.5)),
    ("Butterfly", (90.0, 89.9, 89.8)),
]


def figure(quick=False):
    pixel = 20.0 if quick else 5.0
    size = int(SIZE_M / pixel) + 1
    terrain = terraingen.Terrain(source=terraingen.FlatSource(size, size, pixel))
    grid = terrain.evaluate().grid
    base = terraingen.SyntheticAlbedo(value=0.11)
    crater = terraingen.CraterLayer.manual([terraingen.Crater(0.0, 0.0, DIAMETER, age_gyr=0.0)])

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(PANELS), figsize=(16, 4.3), layout="constrained")
    for ax, (title, thresholds) in zip(axes, PANELS, strict=True):
        settings = terraingen.CraterAlbedoOptions(seed=2)
        rays = settings.rays
        oblique = rays.oblique
        oblique.enabled = thresholds is not None
        oblique.heading_deg = 0.0
        if thresholds is not None:
            oblique.asymmetric_deg, oblique.forbidden_deg, oblique.butterfly_deg = thresholds
        rays.oblique = oblique
        settings.rays = rays
        albedo = terraingen.Albedo(base, [terraingen.CraterAlbedo(crater, settings)])
        values = terraingen.evaluate_albedo(albedo, grid)[0].values
        image = ax.imshow(values, cmap="gray", vmin=0.1, vmax=0.15)
        ax.set_axis_off()
        ax.set_title(title)
    fig.colorbar(image, ax=axes, label="Albedo", shrink=0.85)
    return fig

Reflectance zones around a new 20 m crater, as LROC before-and-after images show them (Robinson et al. 2015, Speyerer et al. 2016). They are a bright proximal zone, a dark one beyond it, and faint, finger-like distal zones, bright and dark, reaching 2 km out. On a 4.4 km square of hills, the left panel shows the zones alone. The middle one adds shadows, where low-angle jets miss the ground behind rises. The right one shows profiles west to east.

# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause

"""Reflectance zones around a new 20 m crater, as LROC before-and-after images show them (Robinson et
al. 2015, Speyerer et al. 2016). They are a bright proximal zone, a dark one beyond it, and faint,
finger-like distal zones, bright and dark, reaching 2 km out. On a 4.4 km square of hills, the left
panel shows the zones alone. The middle one adds shadows, where low-angle jets miss the ground behind
rises. The right one shows profiles west to east."""

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

import terraingen

WIDE = True
SECTION = "Impacts and landers"

SIZE_M = 4400.0
DIAMETER = 20.0


def figure(quick=False):
    pixel = 20.0 if quick else 5.0
    size = int(SIZE_M / pixel) + 1
    relief = terraingen.NoiseLayer(seed=3, wavelength=700.0, amplitude=40.0, octaves=5)
    crater = terraingen.CraterLayer.manual([terraingen.Crater(0.0, 0.0, DIAMETER, age_gyr=0.0)])
    terrain = terraingen.Terrain(source=terraingen.FlatSource(size, size, pixel), layers=[relief, crater])
    grid = terrain.evaluate().grid
    base = terraingen.SyntheticAlbedo(value=0.11)
    x = (np.arange(size) - 0.5 * (size - 1)) * pixel

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 4.6), layout="constrained", width_ratios=[1, 1, 1.4])
    for ax, (title, shadows) in zip(axes[:2], (("Zones", False), ("Zones with shadows", True)), strict=True):
        options = terraingen.CraterAlbedoOptions(seed=2)
        zones = options.zones
        zones.enabled = True
        zone_shadows = zones.shadows
        zone_shadows.enabled = shadows
        zones.shadows = zone_shadows
        options.zones = zones
        albedo = terraingen.Albedo(base, [terraingen.CraterAlbedo(crater, options)])
        values = terraingen.evaluate_albedo(albedo, grid, ground=terrain)[0].values
        image = ax.imshow(values, cmap="gray", vmin=0.095, vmax=0.125)
        ax.set_axis_off()
        ax.set_title(title)
        axes[2].plot(x, values[size // 2], lw=1.2, label=title)
    fig.colorbar(image, ax=axes[:2], label="Albedo", shrink=0.85)
    axes[2].set_xlabel("x (m)")
    axes[2].set_ylabel("Albedo")
    axes[2].legend()
    return fig

# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause

"""Boulders brighten the albedo, on a 40 m square of SP-8023 maximum boulders. The left three, at
0.1 m, make rock 1.5, 2.5 (the default) and 4 times as bright as the regolith. The right two show the
same square at 1 m, where most boulders are too small to resolve, without and with their unresolved
cover drawn as a speckle of the right mean and variance."""

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import terraingen

WIDE = True
SECTION = "Background"

SIZE_M = 40.0
PANELS = [
    ("Ratio 1.5", 1.5, 0.1, True),
    ("Ratio 2.5", 2.5, 0.1, True),
    ("Ratio 4", 4.0, 0.1, True),
    ("1 m, resolved only", 2.5, 1.0, False),
    ("1 m, unresolved speckle", 2.5, 1.0, True),
]


def figure(quick=False):
    options = terraingen.BoulderLayerOptions(seed=4)
    sizes = options.sizes
    sizes.distribution = terraingen.sp8023_intercrater_blocks(terraingen.SpecificationCurve.MAXIMUM)
    options.sizes = sizes
    boulders = terraingen.BoulderLayer(options)
    base = terraingen.SyntheticAlbedo(value=0.11)

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(PANELS), figsize=(19, 4.2), layout="constrained")
    for ax, (title, ratio, pixel, unresolved) in zip(axes, PANELS, strict=True):
        pixel = max(pixel, 0.4) if quick else pixel
        size = int(SIZE_M / pixel) + 1
        terrain = terraingen.Terrain(source=terraingen.FlatSource(size, size, pixel), layers=[boulders])
        grid = terrain.evaluate().grid
        rocks = terraingen.RockAlbedo(
            terraingen.RockAlbedoOptions(seed=1, reflectance_ratio=ratio, unresolved=unresolved), terrain, [0]
        )
        values = terraingen.evaluate_albedo(terraingen.Albedo(base, [rocks]), grid, ground=terrain)[0].values
        image = ax.imshow(values, cmap="gray", vmin=0.1, vmax=0.3)
        ax.set_axis_off()
        ax.set_title(title)
    fig.colorbar(image, ax=axes, label="Albedo", shrink=0.85)
    return fig

# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause

"""Steep slopes stay fresh. Downslope creep keeps exposing immature soil, so slopes past an onset grow
brighter by their optical maturity (Ikeda et al. 2022). On 400 m of hills with a fresh 90 m crater,
the panels show the slopes, then the albedo with the onset at 10, 20 (the default) and 30 degrees."""

import gallery
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import terraingen

WIDE = True
SECTION = "Background"

SIZE_M = 400.0
ONSETS = [10.0, 20.0, 30.0]


def figure(quick=False):
    pixel = 2.0 if quick else 0.5
    size = int(SIZE_M / pixel) + 1
    hills = terraingen.NoiseLayer(seed=2, wavelength=250.0, amplitude=45.0, octaves=6)
    crater = terraingen.CraterLayer.manual([terraingen.Crater(-60.0, 40.0, 90.0, age_gyr=0.0)])
    terrain = terraingen.Terrain(source=terraingen.FlatSource(size, size, pixel), layers=[hills, crater])
    heights = terrain.evaluate()
    grid = heights.grid
    base = terraingen.SyntheticAlbedo(value=0.11)

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(ONSETS) + 1, figsize=(17, 4.3), layout="constrained")
    gallery.show_slopes(axes[0], heights.values, pixel, vmax=40.0)
    axes[0].set_title("Slope")
    for ax, onset in zip(axes[1:], ONSETS, strict=True):
        layer = terraingen.SlopeAlbedo(terraingen.SlopeAlbedoOptions(onset_deg=onset))
        values = terraingen.evaluate_albedo(terraingen.Albedo(base, [layer]), grid, ground=terrain)[0].values
        image = ax.imshow(values, cmap="gray", vmin=0.09, vmax=0.15)
        ax.set_axis_off()
        ax.set_title(f"Onset {onset:g} degrees")

docs.title: Synthetic base
docs.text:
The synthetic albedo base on 400 m squares is a mature mare value of 0.11 at 750 nm, multiplied by 1 plus fractal value noise, here 150 m noise with amplitudes of 0, 0.2 and 0.5, then finer 30 m noise of 0.5, and last as three bands, tinted a warm hue with noise in hue and saturation too. The gray panels share one scale.

Made by docs/gallery/albedo/synthetic_base.py; back to the figure in Albedo.

# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause

"""The synthetic albedo base on 400 m squares is a mature mare value of 0.11 at 750 nm, multiplied by
1 plus fractal value noise, here 150 m noise with amplitudes of 0, 0.2 and 0.5, then finer 30 m noise
of 0.5, and last as three bands, tinted a warm hue with noise in hue and saturation too. The gray
panels share one scale."""

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

import terraingen

WIDE = True
SECTION = "Background"

SIZE_M = 400.0


def noise(seed, wavelength, amplitude):
    return [terraingen.Fractal(seed=seed, wavelength=wavelength, amplitude=amplitude, octaves=6)]


def figure(quick=False):
    pixel = 4.0 if quick else 1.0
    size = int(SIZE_M / pixel) + 1
    terrain = terraingen.Terrain(source=terraingen.FlatSource(size, size, pixel))
    grid = terrain.evaluate().grid
    panels = [
        ("Plain 0.11", terraingen.SyntheticAlbedo(value=0.11)),
        ("150 m noise, 0.2", terraingen.SyntheticAlbedo(value=0.11, value_noise=noise(8, 150.0, 0.2))),
        ("150 m noise, 0.5", terraingen.SyntheticAlbedo(value=0.11, value_noise=noise(8, 150.0, 0.5))),
        ("30 m noise, 0.5", terraingen.SyntheticAlbedo(value=0.11, value_noise=noise(8, 30.0, 0.5))),
        (
            "Tinted, three bands",
            terraingen.SyntheticAlbedo(
                value=0.11,
                value_noise=noise(8, 150.0, 0.3),
                rgb=True,
                hue_deg=30.0,
                saturation=0.25,
                hue_noise_deg=noise(9, 200.0, 15.0),
                saturation_noise=noise(10, 200.0, 0.1),
            ),
        ),
    ]

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(panels), figsize=(19, 4.2), layout="constrained")
    for ax, (title, source) in zip(axes, panels, strict=True):
        bands = [band.values for band in terraingen.evaluate_albedo(terraingen.Albedo(source), grid)]
        if len(bands) == 3:
            ax.imshow(np.clip(np.dstack(bands) / 0.16, 0.0, 1.0))
        else:
            image = ax.imshow(bands[0], cmap="gray", vmin=0.08, vmax=0.14)
        ax.set_axis_off()
        ax.set_title(title)
    fig.colorbar(image, ax=axes[:-1], label="Albedo", shrink=0.85)
    return fig

docs.title: Placement
docs.text:
Size distributions. Cumulative boulder size-frequency distributions for NASA SP-8023's intercrater blocks between its minimum and maximum curves and its blocks near craters, Golombek and Rapp's model at 2%, 5% and 10% rock cover, and synthterrain's three power laws.

Code

Clustering. Boulders of 0.3 m and up on 80 m squares at the same mean abundance, from NASA SP-8023's maximum intercrater curve, drawn to scale and colored by their wear. On the left they are scattered. In the middle 90% gather around the nearest of a jittered lattice of centers 20 m apart. On the right 90% lie in Thomas clusters, Gaussian clumps around Poisson centers that overlap and add.

Code

Density map. A patchy rock-abundance map setting boulder cover point by point, as orbital thermal inertia maps give it. Boulders of 0.3 m to 5 m on a 60 m square, sized by NASA SP-8023's nominal intercrater curve, cover from none to about 7% of the ground in fractal patches. The left panel shows the map and the middle one the boulders it places, drawn to scale and colored by height. The right plot shows the rock cover the boulders give in each 10 m cell against the map's mean over the cell.

Code

Patches. Patchiness varying boulder abundance across the ground in fractal patches 30 m across. Boulders of 0.3 m and up from NASA SP-8023's maximum intercrater curve on 80 m squares are drawn to scale and colored by diameter. From left to right the abundance is even (spread 1), then ranges from a third to three times the layer's own (spread 3) and from a tenth to ten times (spread 10). On their own the patches raise the mean, by 1.19 and 2.06 times here. Under a density map they are divided by that mean so the map's abundance holds.

Code

Slope map. A size-slope map varying the boulder size-frequency distribution point by point. Boulders of 0.2 m to 5 m on a 60 m square have a cumulative power-law exponent rising from 1.5 in the west to 4 in the east, with the count of boulders 1 m and larger held to the layer's own everywhere. The steeper the slope, the more small boulders for each large one, so the east swarms with small boulders while the west has few. The left panel shows the map and the middle one the boulders, drawn to scale and colored by diameter. The right plot shows the boulders of the western and eastern thirds as cumulative size-frequency distributions.

Code

Slopes. Boulders on the steep walls of a fresh 100 m crater on fractal relief, which throws blocks of its own, drawn to scale over the crater's hillshade and colored by the slope of the ground beneath them. On the left boulders rest wherever they land. In the middle none stay on ground steeper than 20 degrees. On the right those instead roll up to 40 m downhill and stop where the wall eases below 20 degrees, gathering in a ring partway down it.

Code

docs.title: Crater ejecta
docs.text:
Crater ejecta aging. Crater blocks fade as their craters age. A 60 m crater (gray rim) is shown 0, 10 and 30 Myr old, with blocks of 0.3 m and up sized by Golombek and Rapp's model at 15% rock cover, drawn to scale and colored by the height they stand above the ground. The top row thins them by freshness, falling toward 0.7, below which a crater keeps no blocks. The middle row thins them by age, as (1 - age / 40 Myr) cubed. The bottom plot shows the abundance at 1.5 radii against crater age for both.

Code

Crater ejecta coverage. How rocky a crater's rim is. A fresh 60 m crater (gray rim) has blocks, on top of the background boulders, sized by Golombek and Rapp's model at 5%, 15% and 30% rock cover at the rim, falling smoothly to nothing at three radii. Blocks of 0.4 m and up are drawn to scale and colored by the height they stand above the ground. The bottom plot shows the cumulative number of blocks per square meter within 1.5 radii against diameter, the rockier rims richer in large blocks as well as small.

Code

Crater ejecta decay. How fast a crater's blocks thin beyond the rim. A fresh 60 m crater (gray rim) has blocks, on top of the background boulders, that fall exponentially with an e-folding distance of 0.3, 0.7 (the default) and 1.5 radii, out to 5 radii. Blocks of 0.5 m and up sized by Golombek and Rapp's model at 15% rock cover are drawn to scale and colored by the height they stand above the ground. The bottom plot shows the ejecta abundance against distance from the center for each.

Code

Crater ejecta floor. Blocks left on a crater's floor. A fresh 60 m crater (gray rim) has blocks, on top of the background boulders, that fall exponentially beyond the rim and keep none, 5% (the default) and 40% of the rim's abundance on the floor. Blocks of 0.4 m and up sized by Golombek and Rapp's model at 15% rock cover are drawn to scale and colored by the height they stand above the ground. The bottom plot shows the ejecta abundance against distance from the center for each.

Code

Crater ejecta profiles. Blocks thrown out of a fresh 60 m crater (gray rim) on top of the background boulders, blocks of 0.3 m and up sized by Golombek and Rapp's model at 15% rock cover, drawn to scale and colored by the height they stand above the ground. On the left the abundance falls smoothly to nothing at three radii. In the middle it falls exponentially beyond the rim, with a few blocks left on the floor, as in synthterrain. The right plot shows the two profiles against distance from the crater's center.

Code

Crater ejecta reach. How far a crater's blocks reach. A fresh 60 m crater (gray rim) has blocks, on top of the background boulders, that fall smoothly to nothing at 2, 3 (the default) and 5 radii, blocks of 0.8 m and up sized by Golombek and Rapp's model at 15% rock cover, drawn to scale and colored by the height they stand above the ground. The bottom plot shows the ejecta abundance against distance from the center for each.

Code

Crater ejecta regolith. Only craters that dig through the regolith throw blocks. Fresh craters 20 to 60 m across (gray rims) each dig a tenth of their diameter deep, with blocks of 0.3 m and up sized by Golombek and Rapp's model at 15% rock cover, drawn to scale and colored by the height they stand above the ground. From left to right the panels show no regolith limit, then 3 m and 5 m of regolith, through which only the larger craters reach bedrock.

Code

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
Models axes. Axis ratios, with the angular style from the same seed stretched to intermediate and short axes, over a long axis of 1, of 0.9 and 0.25 (a slab), 0.75 and 0.55 (near the default), 0.5 and 0.45 (an elongate rod) and 0.95 and 0.9 (equant). The short axis stands vertical, so it sets how tall a boulder is for its width.

Code

Models fractures. Fracture planes cutting the angular style from the same seed, with none, 3, 8 and 16 planes. Each plane slices off what lies beyond it to leave a flat face, and more planes give a more faceted, blockier rock. The top row cuts at 0.55 to 0.85 of the shape's reach (the default) and the bottom row makes shallower cuts at 0.8 to 0.95.

Code

Models fragments. Boulders splitting as they wear. One block model is broken into 3, 6 and 10 pieces that fit back together, each piece pulled a fifth of its distance out from the center so the cracks show. The top row has radial cracks, near-vertical and running out from the middle like slices. The bottom row has slab cracks, parallel sheets as a layered rock splits. The pieces become boulders of their own, opening apart and then scattering as rubble with more wear.

Code

Models noise. Surface noise, with the angular style from the same seed having its radius changed by fractal noise of up to none, 6% (the default), 15% and 30%, from clean facets to lumpy, knobbly rock. The top row uses 4 octaves from a wavelength of 0.9 long axes (the default) and the bottom row a finer first wavelength of 0.3 long axes.

Code

Models rounding. Rounding, with the block style from the same seed pulled toward its ellipsoid by none, a third, two thirds and all of the way, from a sharp-cornered cube to a smooth ovoid. Fractures and noise are applied after, so even a fully rounded block keeps its flat cuts.

Code

Models settle. Settling four boulder models 2 m long, leaned 35 degrees and placed on level ground (gray), seen from low to the side. The top row shows them as drawn, propped on an edge or a corner at the lean and standing tall. In the bottom row each has tipped over until it rests stably on a face, its lowest point at the ground, and the platy rock falls flat. Each title gives the height of the top above the ground. Burial and tilt are left out here so the resting face shows.

Code

Models solids. What boulder models start from. The top row shows the five base solids before any stretching, cutting or noise. They are an icosahedron (refined toward a sphere, the start of most styles), a cube, a pyramid, a prism and a tetrahedron. The bottom row shows the angular style from one seed with its solid split into four triangles 1, 2, 3 (the default) and 5 times, each title giving the triangle count.

Code

Models styles. The nine default boulder styles, one model of each drawn from the same seed, a long axis of 1. They are polyhedra cut from a sphere (angular, platy, subrounded) that most boulders are, rounded boulders, blocks from a cube, wedges from a prism, pyramids, shards from a tetrahedron and near-spheres. Each is stretched to its axes, cut by fracture planes, roughened by noise and worn at its edges. The title gives each style's share of boulders.

Code

Models variety. The default mix of twelve boulder models from seeds 1 to 12, each seed picking a style by its share of boulders and drawing that style's axes, fractures, noise and wear, so no two rocks in a field are alike. A field can instead share a small library of prototype shapes, instanced across its boulders. Each title gives the seed and the style drawn.

Code

Models weathering. Weathering and face roughness on the block style from the same seed. In the top row edges and corners are worn back by none, the style's own (weathering 1, the default), twice and four times its edge softness, from fresh, sharp breaks to rounded, long-exposed rock. In the bottom row fracture faces undulate by none, 6% (the block default), 15% and 30% of each plane's offset, from flat cleavage to rough breaks.

Code

docs.title: Pose
docs.text:
Fillets. Fillets, the aprons of regolith banked against a boulder's base, around one 2 m boulder on a 6 m square, reaching 0.3 diameters beyond its edge. From left to right there is no fillet, then fillets rising to 30% and 60% of the boulder's exposed height. The top row is shaded in 3D at twice the true height, the middle row hillshaded with a low sun, and the bottom row shows profiles west to east through the boulder.

Code

Pose burial. How deep boulders sit in the regolith. The same boulders of 0.3 m and up on a 30 m square, sized by Golombek and Rapp's model at 10% rock cover, are each buried by a share of their height drawn between none and none, 0.1 and 0.4 (the default), and 0.5 and 0.9, drawn to scale and colored by the height they stand above the ground. The bottom plot shows how many stand at least each height, the measure a rover's clearance meets.

Code

Pose burial by wear. Older boulders sink deeper. Boulders of 0.3 m and up on a 30 m square at 10% rock cover, between craters so their wear spans every stage, are buried between none and 0.8 of their height with wear setting none, half (0.5) and all (1) of the draw. They are drawn to scale and colored by their buried share. The bottom plot shows buried share against wear, from scattered to tracking wear.

Code

Pose height ratio. How tall boulders are for their width. The same boulders of 0.3 m and up on a 30 m square, sized by Golombek and Rapp's model at 10% rock cover, have heights drawn between 0.2 and 0.3 of their diameters (flat slabs), 0.4 and 0.6 (the default) and 0.7 and 0.9 (near-round blocks), each buried by the default 0.1 to 0.4 of its height. They are drawn to scale and colored by the height they stand above the ground. The bottom plot shows how many stand at least each height.

Code

# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause

"""Boulders of 0.3 m and up on 80 m squares at the same mean abundance, from NASA SP-8023's maximum
intercrater curve, drawn to scale and colored by their wear. On the left they are scattered. In the
middle 90% gather around the nearest of a jittered lattice of centers 20 m apart. On the right 90% lie
in Thomas clusters, Gaussian clumps around Poisson centers that overlap and add."""

import gallery
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import terraingen

WIDE = True
SECTION = "Placement"

HALF_SIZE_M = 40.0
PANELS = [
    ("Scattered", 0.0, terraingen.BoulderClusterModel.NEAREST),
    ("Nearest clusters", 0.9, terraingen.BoulderClusterModel.NEAREST),
    ("Thomas clusters", 0.9, terraingen.BoulderClusterModel.THOMAS),
]


def figure(quick=False):
    region = (-HALF_SIZE_M, -HALF_SIZE_M, HALF_SIZE_M, HALF_SIZE_M)

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(14, 4.4), layout="constrained")
    for ax, (title, share, model) in zip(axes, PANELS, strict=True):
        options = terraingen.BoulderLayerOptions(seed=4)
        sizes = options.sizes
        sizes.distribution = terraingen.sp8023_intercrater_blocks(terraingen.SpecificationCurve.MAXIMUM)
        sizes.min_diameter = 0.3
        options.sizes = sizes
        clusters = options.clusters
        clusters.share = share
        clusters.model = model
        clusters.center_spacing = 20.0
        clusters.radius = 3.0
        options.clusters = clusters
        table = terraingen.BoulderLayer(options).boulders(region).table
        gallery.show_boulders(ax, table, region, table["wear"], label="Wear", vmin=0.0, vmax=1.0)
        ax.set_title(f"{title}: {len(table['diameter'])} boulders")
    return fig

Crater blocks fade as their craters age. A 60 m crater (gray rim) is shown 0, 10 and 30 Myr old, with blocks of 0.3 m and up sized by Golombek and Rapp's model at 15% rock cover, drawn to scale and colored by the height they stand above the ground. The top row thins them by freshness, falling toward 0.7, below which a crater keeps no blocks. The middle row thins them by age, as (1 - age / 40 Myr) cubed. The bottom plot shows the abundance at 1.5 radii against crater age for both.

# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause

"""Crater blocks fade as their craters age. A 60 m crater (gray rim) is shown 0, 10 and 30 Myr old,
with blocks of 0.3 m and up sized by Golombek and Rapp's model at 15% rock cover, drawn to scale and
colored by the height they stand above the ground. The top row thins them by freshness, falling toward
0.7, below which a crater keeps no blocks. The middle row thins them by age, as (1 - age / 40 Myr)
cubed. The bottom plot shows the abundance at 1.5 radii against crater age for both."""

import gallery
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from matplotlib.patches import Circle

import terraingen

SECTION = "Crater ejecta"

HALF_SIZE_M = 90.0
DIAMETER = 60.0
AGES_GYR = [0.0, 0.01, 0.03]
AGINGS = [
    ("By freshness", {}),
    ("By age", {"aging": terraingen.EjectaAging.AGE, "lifetime_gyr": 0.04, "aging_exponent": 3.0}),
]


def boulder_layer(craters, fields):
    """Golombek-Rapp blocks out of `craters` 10 m and up, aged as the BoulderEjecta `fields` say."""
    options = terraingen.BoulderLayerOptions(seed=4)
    sizes = options.sizes
    sizes.min_diameter = 0.3
    options.sizes = sizes
    ejecta = options.ejecta
    ejecta.min_crater_diameter = 10.0
    ejecta.distribution = None
    ejecta.coverage = 0.15
    for name, value in fields.items():
        setattr(ejecta, name, value)
    options.ejecta = ejecta
    return terraingen.BoulderLayer(options, craters)


def figure(quick=False):
    region = (-HALF_SIZE_M, -HALF_SIZE_M, HALF_SIZE_M, HALF_SIZE_M)

    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(11, 12.5), layout="constrained")
    maps, curves = fig.subfigures(2, 1, height_ratios=[2.1, 1])
    map_axes = maps.subplots(2, 3)
    for row, (aging, fields) in zip(map_axes, AGINGS, strict=True):
        for ax, age in zip(row, AGES_GYR, strict=True):
            craters = terraingen.CraterLayer.manual([terraingen.Crater(0.0, 0.0, DIAMETER, age_gyr=age)])
            table = boulder_layer(craters, fields).boulders(region).table
            ax.add_patch(Circle((0.0, 0.0), 0.5 * DIAMETER, fill=False, color="#888888", lw=1.0))
            circles = gallery.show_boulders(
                ax, table, region, table["height"], cmap="magma_r", vmin=0.0, vmax=1.0, colorbar=False
            )
            ax.set_title(f"{aging}, {age * 1000:g} Myr old")
    maps.colorbar(circles, ax=map_axes, label="Height (m)", shrink=0.85)

    ax = curves.subplots()
    ages = np.linspace(0.0, 0.06, 30 if quick else 80)
    for aging, fields in AGINGS:
        abundance = []
        for age in ages:
            craters = terraingen.CraterLayer.manual([terraingen.Crater(0.0, 0.0, DIAMETER, age_gyr=age)])
            abundance.append(boulder_layer(craters, fields).abundance_at(0.75 * DIAMETER, 0.0)[1])
        ax.plot(ages * 1000.0, abundance, lw=1.6, label=aging)
    ax.set_xlabel("Crater age (Myr)")
    ax.set_ylabel("Ejecta abundance at 1.5 radii")
    ax.legend()
    return fig

"""How rocky a crater's rim is. A fresh 60 m crater (gray rim) has blocks, on top of the background
boulders, sized by Golombek and Rapp's model at 5%, 15% and 30% rock cover at the rim, falling
smoothly to nothing at three radii. Blocks of 0.4 m and up are drawn to scale and colored by the
height they stand above the ground. The bottom plot shows the cumulative number of blocks per square
meter within 1.5 radii against diameter, the rockier rims richer in large blocks as well as small."""

import gallery
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from matplotlib.patches import Circle

import terraingen

WIDE = True
SECTION = "Crater ejecta"

HALF_SIZE_M = 80.0
DIAMETER = 60.0
SETTINGS = [0.05, 0.15, 0.3]
COLORS = ["#1f77b4", "#d62728", "#2ca02c"]


def ejecta_boulders(craters, coverage):
    """Background boulders and blocks thrown from `craters` at `coverage` rock cover."""
    options = terraingen.BoulderLayerOptions(seed=4)
    sizes = options.sizes
    sizes.min_diameter = 0.4
    options.sizes = sizes
    ejecta = options.ejecta
    ejecta.min_crater_diameter = 10.0
    ejecta.distribution = None
    ejecta.coverage = coverage
    options.ejecta = ejecta
    return terraingen.BoulderLayer(options, craters)


def figure(quick=False):
    region = (-HALF_SIZE_M, -HALF_SIZE_M, HALF_SIZE_M, HALF_SIZE_M)
    craters = terraingen.CraterLayer.manual([terraingen.Crater(0.0, 0.0, DIAMETER, age_gyr=0.0)])
    near = 1.5 * 0.5 * DIAMETER

    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10.5), layout="constrained")
    grid = fig.add_gridspec(2, len(SETTINGS), height_ratios=[1, 0.7])
    map_axes = [fig.add_subplot(grid[0, column]) for column in range(len(SETTINGS))]
    sizes_ax = fig.add_subplot(grid[1, :])
    for ax, setting, color in zip(map_axes, SETTINGS, COLORS, strict=True):
        table = ejecta_boulders(craters, setting).boulders(region).table
        ax.add_patch(Circle((0.0, 0.0), 0.5 * DIAMETER, fill=False, color="#888888", lw=1.0))
        circles = gallery.show_boulders(
            ax, table, region, table["height"], cmap="magma_r", vmin=0.0, vmax=1.0, colorbar=False
        )
        ax.set_title(f"coverage {setting:g}: {len(table['diameter'])} blocks", color=color)
        inside = np.hypot(np.asarray(table["x"]), np.asarray(table["y"])) <= near
        diameters = np.sort(np.asarray(table["diameter"])[inside])[::-1]
        density = np.arange(1, len(diameters) + 1) / (np.pi * near**2)
        sizes_ax.loglog(diameters, density, color=color, lw=1.6, label=f"coverage {setting:g}")
    fig.colorbar(circles, ax=map_axes, label="Height (m)", shrink=0.85)
    sizes_ax.set_xlabel("Block diameter (m)")
    sizes_ax.set_ylabel("Blocks at least this large (per m$^2$)")
    sizes_ax.legend()
    return fig

import gallery
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from matplotlib.patches import Circle

import terraingen

WIDE = True
SECTION = "Crater ejecta"

HALF_SIZE_M = 160.0
DIAMETER = 60.0
SETTINGS = [0.3, 0.7, 1.5]

def ejecta_boulders(craters, decay):

# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause

"""Blocks thrown out of a fresh 60 m crater (gray rim) on top of the background boulders, blocks of
0.3 m and up sized by Golombek and Rapp's model at 15% rock cover, drawn to scale and colored by the
height they stand above the ground. On the left the abundance falls smoothly to nothing at three
radii. In the middle it falls exponentially beyond the rim, with a few blocks left on the floor, as in
synthterrain. The right plot shows the two profiles against distance from the crater's center."""

import gallery
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from matplotlib.patches import Circle

import terraingen

WIDE = True
SECTION = "Crater ejecta"

HALF_SIZE_M = 100.0
DIAMETER = 60.0
PROFILES = [
    ("Smoothstep", terraingen.EjectaProfile.SMOOTHSTEP),
    ("Exponential", terraingen.EjectaProfile.EXPONENTIAL),
